Requirement_Text: Current corruption-detection requirement: Inventory, Add New Shows and Tag shall not inspect media for corruption unless actual tagging is enabled or Deep Audio Check is checked. Before deep checking, a reversible write/read/restore tag probe shall be performed. A non-access tag-write failure is corrupt and suppresses further analysis of that file; transient access/resource and failed restoration are unverifiable and cannot trigger deletion. If Deep Audio Check is enabled and the tag probe succeeds, FLAC shall be decoded in full with the source-built LGPL FFmpeg raw PCM path; the computed whole-audio MD5, decoded samples and final decoder exit status must agree with STREAMINFO. An unset/all-zero STREAMINFO MD5 means not computed, not a tag-write failure and not corruption. If the reversible tag-write probe and full audio decode including available sample-count check succeed, tagging may proceed; log that the stream was decoded without stored-MD5 authentication. If tag writing fails for non-access reasons, treat the file as corrupt, regardless of MD5. Timeouts, access errors, and incomplete validation remain unverifiable and block mutation. Duplicate cleanup still requires a nonzero matching MD5 before moving copies. Other supported audio uses full-stream FFmpeg decoding. A processing cancellation, timeout or infrastructure failure remains unverifiable. Deep Audio Check is expensive; users must be warned. Manual Tweaks never performs corruption checks. Existing file/folder deletion policy and percentage thresholds are unchanged. POSIX filename safety: when an audio path contains filesystem bytes not representable as UTF-8, the inventory walker SHALL report an explicitly unidentified path using the filesystem-byte hex identifier, rather than emit a logging traceback or silently discard it. It SHALL not write the raw surrogate to bootlist or setlists, and Dry Run SHALL not modify unidentifiedShows.txt.

Installer licensing: The Windows MSI license-agreement dialog SHALL display the complete GNU General Public License version 3, matching the LICENSE text in the public TLO GitHub repository. WiX placeholder/Latin text is prohibited. The installer SHALL bind WixUILicenseRtf to a complete, valid GPL v3 RTF document, and shall fail if the RTF is missing.

Release provenance: the separately versioned GitHub Build Process SHALL include exactly one simple build-process version in the root build-provenance.json of every new complete/update distribution ZIP and identify the same version in GitHub Release Notes and build logs. This is one version for the whole release; no per-platform version or fingerprint, and no retroactive labels on old releases.

Remove Startup Profiles from the Main hamburger menu and delete its profile application module. There is a single shared TLOHome/tlo-preferences.ini, loaded at startup; no preset selection or hidden profile rewrites.

Edit Preferences SHALL offer buttons labeled Save & Close and Cancel. Save & Close validates the entire INI; if valid it saves atomically, closes the editor and tells the user to restart Main/Search to apply the new defaults. Cancel does not save and confirms before discarding modified text. Invalid values do not get saved and keep the editor open.

Editing and saving preferences SHALL NOT apply any changes to the running application, including previously live-applied font preferences. The app remains running and retains the values currently selected by the user or previously loaded at launch. A restart (new process) is the only way the changed preferences take effect; explicit GUI selections can continue until that restart.

Duplicate-folder cleanup: a duplicate match requires matching relative file names, exact byte sizes and recursive folder structure, including empty folders. Do not hash or read candidate file contents to identify duplicates. Equal-name/equal-size files count as duplicates even if their bytes differ. Reject symbolic links and unsupported filesystem objects. Recheck names/sizes immediately before relocation into the recoverable duplicates holding folder. This overrides earlier release duplicate-move SHA-256 requirements. FLAC health checks and repair remain independent operations; their integrity safeguards are unchanged.

Update downloads: preserve signed metadata, signed asset size and SHA-256 verification, staged ZIP structural inspection and safeguards against overwriting existing Downloads files. Download to a temporary non-release filename, and only after verification publish with an atomic same-directory, no-replace rename. Do not use hard-link publication. On Windows the shared [general] update_downloads preference SHALL select msi or zip and default to msi even if the INI is absent, lacks the preference, or the application was installed from ZIP. Selecting zip downloads the matching portable ZIP (prefer update to complete) without applying it. Selecting msi downloads the authenticated signed MSI without falling back to ZIP; an MSI-owned installation may use its verified external worker and a portable installation may launch the interactive Windows Installer. The MSI SHALL NOT delete the existing portable TLOHome/apps directory; users may remove it themselves. Linux and macOS retain ZIP updates.

GitHub release approval gate: TLO Main and Search manual and automatic update checks SHALL use only the official GitHub /releases/latest production endpoint. They SHALL reject draft/pre-release results and malformed or missing GitHub approval fields before build comparison, signed metadata retrieval, asset selection, or download. Successful pre-release builds MAY remain publicly downloadable via GitHub, but SHALL NOT be offered by the TLO updater until explicitly promoted. The publisher MAY change only the promoted release status and Latest designation; historical production releases and assets remain intact. Existing independent signing, SHA-256, ZIP safety, and download-only protections remain mandatory.

Windows UNC shares : TLO SHALL accept a fully qualified network directory of the form \\server\share\folder in Full Inventory Path(s), control files, Manual Updates and Copy Requests, without requiring a mapped drive letter. The operating-system path shall be retained for actual filesystem operations. On non-Windows platforms an unmounted UNC spelling SHALL fail clearly instead of being treated as a relative directory.

UNC storage identity : The network share root (server plus share) SHALL be the deterministic visible volume identity, expressed as UNC:server/share, regardless of remote volume-label availability. bootlist.csv and group-log SEARCH_PATH SHALL store [UNC:server/share] plus the path relative to that share; no extra column is required. UNC labels shall be compared case-insensitively, and equal subpaths on different shares SHALL NOT collide. Copy Requests SHALL reconstruct the share path from this identity and report an unavailable share as disconnected/waiting, without requiring mount enumeration. Manual Updates SHALL compare both relative path and share identity. Device namespaces SHALL NOT be treated as UNC shares. Postprocessing may read UNC setlists only beneath a root selected and accessed by the current inventory operation, never merely because a persisted log named a network path.

Update-package validation: The running updater SHALL verify independently signed metadata with its pinned key, the downloaded ZIP size and SHA-256 digest, exact release platform/build/kind, safe ZIP member paths, limits, duplicates and protected user-data paths. It SHALL NOT reject a cryptographically verified update merely because its TLO_DBs file names differ from a hard-coded database list. The databases_included boolean SHALL continue to control TLO_DBs protected-path restrictions for database-free updates; complete packages SHALL declare database inclusion. The release build process SHALL separately verify that physical TLO_DBs/artists.sqlite, venues.txt and cities.sqlite are included in complete/database-inclusive releases before signing and publishing. Do not use database-free bridge updates to migrate an installation that lacks cities.sqlite; its already-installed old updater may require a trusted manual upgrade.

SHN conversion: strict FFmpeg decoding and independently verified complete source/FLAC PCM equivalence are required. Verified SHN originals go to native Trash/Recycle Bin or, if unavailable, the same-volume .tlo-shn-originals/<unique-id>/<original-filename> recoverable folder. Held originals SHALL be excluded from Tag Copy and Copy Requests, and never purged automatically.

Normative keywords: uppercase and lowercase MUST/must and SHALL/shall mean a mandatory requirement; MUST NOT/must not and SHALL NOT/shall not mean a prohibition; SHOULD/should means a recommended behavior that may be departed from only for a documented reason; MAY/may means permitted behavior. These meanings apply throughout the normative sections regardless of capitalization.

Terminology: “Full Inventory” is the full tlo-main Inventory action; “Add New Shows” is the main-window button that opens the Add Shows workflow; “Process New Shows” and “Process Potential Duplicate/Upgrades” are actions inside Add Shows. “Manual Updates” is the child window historically reached through the Manual Tweaks command. “Main GUI” is the primary tlo-main graphical interface; “Path(s)” is its main input. “Search Path” is the underlying inventory-root concept and --search-path is its CLI form. “etreeDB” is the GUI label; “eTreeDB” names the external service. “Artist in Album” is the GUI label for the Artist-in-Album tagging rule. “Trash/Recycle Bin” means the platform trash mechanism and never permanent-delete fallback behavior.

Examples introduced by “for example”, “e.g.”, or “such as” are illustrative unless the requirement explicitly states that the list is exhaustive. Named constants or shared policy modules referenced by a requirement are normative sources for enumerated implementation values; copied appendix lists are descriptive aids and must not override the governing policy.
The system must identify Artist, Date, Venue, and Location: City, State/Region, and Country only when the country is not the United States.

The city catalog SHALL be a physical support database, not an embedded fallback. The build process SHALL stage and verify TLO_DBs/cities.sqlite alongside artists.sqlite and venues.txt, and SHALL validate the database in packaged distributions. Database-inclusive distributions SHALL also stage the physical TLO_DBs/venues.sqlite master; retain venues.txt for legacy fallback.

City data release placement: All complete distributions and database-inclusive updates SHALL contain a separate physical TLO_DBs/cities.sqlite, alongside TLO_DBs/artists.sqlite and TLO_DBs/venues.txt. The build SHALL stage it from the vetted SQLite master, verify its SHA-256 bytes and declare cities.sqlite in database_files. Updates with databases_included=false SHALL contain no TLO_DBs files. No Python module or frozen executable SHALL contain an embedded duplicate city catalog. Database-inclusive distributions SHALL also stage the physical TLO_DBs/venues.sqlite master; retain venues.txt for legacy fallback.

External city database: The runtime SHALL load city names from a physical TLO_DBs/cities.sqlite in the configured TLOHome or adjacent to the installed distribution. There SHALL be no embedded fallback. Missing/corrupt city data SHALL not interrupt inventory processing and SHALL not trigger speculative place recognition; all prior path/setlist/artist rules remain.

Windows MSI TLOHome management: During per-user MSI setup, display a folder-selection dialog defaulting to C:\.tlo unless an existing user TLOHome environment variable or saved DataHome points elsewhere. Persist the user selection in HKCU\Environment as TLOHome and HKCU\Software\TradersLittleOrganizer\UserSettings as DataHome, without requiring elevation. Executables remain under LocalAppData Programs. Preserve TLOHome, preferences, inventory, logs and setlists on MSI upgrades and uninstall. On the first launch following an MSI upgrade, the installed MSI may replace its managed TLOHome/TLO_DBs master files (artists.sqlite, venues.txt, cities.sqlite); user edits to these files may be overwritten and are not guaranteed compatible across versions. Do not delete other TLOHome files. Main and Search provide Open TLO Folder commands. Database-inclusive distributions SHALL also stage the physical TLO_DBs/venues.sqlite master; retain venues.txt for legacy fallback.

City-name reference: TLO SHALL read canonical names and aliases from the single external SQLite city master. A verified Artist DB prefix and complete date precede city-only inference. Source spelling is retained; no state or country is inferred from a regionless city name. Ambiguous aliases and unsafe recording or artist descriptors are rejected; recognized same-name city spellings do not establish geography.
Normalize single quotes so that curly quotes, backticks, and other apostrophe variants do not cause search failures.

When TLO writes user-facing names or audio metadata values, normalize them to standard printable ASCII. This applies to Show Names, compliant folder names and copy/move targets, generated setlist filename bases, and audio tag Artist, Album, and Title values. Accented Latin characters such as umlauts must be transliterated to plain ASCII equivalents, smart punctuation must be converted to ordinary ASCII punctuation, and remaining non-ASCII/control characters must be removed before writing.

When writing setlist .txt files to the setlists directory, name each exported file using the concatenated metadata fields Artist + Date + Venue + Location. Remove filename-unsafe and extra characters from Artist, Venue, Location, Parentheticals, and ordinary fallback Show-name text, but preserve ampersands (&) because they are meaningful in artist, venue, album, and show names. Preserve dash characters in Date, including complete dates and date ranges. If fallback Show-name text is used because discrete metadata fields are incomplete, normalize compact date-like substrings before sanitizing: yyyymmdd becomes yyyy-mm-dd when valid, and compact plausible year ranges such as yyyyyyyy become yyyy-yyyy. Do not remove the dashes introduced by this normalization. If a String1 - String2 record has no parsed Date but String2 itself is date-like, preserve the literal artist/String2 separator and preserve the date dashes inside String2, for example Iris Dement - 1998-10-03 must export as IrisDement-1998-10-03.txt rather than IrisDement-19981003.txt. Search/open filename generation in tlo-search must use this same normalization so a Show value resolves to the exact filename inventory creates; non-date dashes such as the dash in (pre-fm) are removed, while yyyy-mm-dd date dashes are preserved.

Do not strip or drop trailing parenthetical qualifiers when generating exported setlist filenames. This rule is universal: if a Show Name, album-style show name, or source main folder includes trailing parentheticals such as (SBD), (FM), (Volume 1), (Vol 2), or (v.3), the sanitized parenthetical text must remain part of the setlist filename base. Same-base Volume/Vol siblings therefore produce distinct setlist filenames based on their own parenthetical suffixes rather than relying on alternate collision suffixes. A recognized performance qualifier such as Early Show or Late Show must remain part of the final Show identity as a parenthesized suffix when it is not already present, so separate performances on the same date remain distinct.

Before applying setlist filename sanitization, normalize date-like tokens embedded in the base text. Compact yyyymmdd tokens must become yyyy-mm-dd, compact yyyyyyyy year ranges must become yyyy-yyyy, and separated date tokens using spaces, underscores, periods, or extra dashes must be normalized to yyyy-mm-dd. Separator dashes around the date token are not preserved as extra artist/date punctuation; the date dashes inside the normalized date are preserved. Date-like String2 values in String1 - String2 records must not be duplicated by also extracting the same token as a fallback Date for the output filename.

Supported normalized partial dates in Show values must preserve their internal date dashes when forming exported setlist filenames. For example, 1973-12-xx must remain 1973-12-xx, not 197312xx. Collection Search must use the same postprocess filename-creation helper used for inventory exports rather than a separate normalization algorithm.

Generated setlist file when no source setlist exists: If no usable setlist file is found for a show, create a setlist .txt file during postprocess. The output file name must still be based on the normal Artist + Date + Venue + Location setlist naming rule. The generated file contents must put Artist, Date, Venue, and Location at the top, each on its own line and omitting any missing metadata value. After a blank line, include a TRACKS: heading and one numbered row per recognized music file, deriving the row title from the music filename when possible rather than copying the raw filename as the title. Do not copy any original placeholder setlist into TLOHome/setlists when this generated file is used.

Legacy placeholder setlist regeneration: If a selected source setlist contains only the text "Folder never contained an info file" case-insensitively, allowing punctuation, whitespace, and normal single-quote variants, treat that source as a marker-only placeholder. Do not copy the marker-only source text into TLOHome/setlists. Instead, create or replace info-gen.txt in the associated MAIN_DIR_PATH folder and use that generated content for the normal TLOHome/setlists export. info-gen.txt must contain only known metadata using explicit Artist:, Date:, Venue:, and Location: lines, omitting any unknown metadata field, followed by the exact basenames of recognized music files as File: filename.ext rows. The original marker file is left unchanged. If the marker appears along with other usable content, do not generate info-gen.txt solely because the marker text is present; parse and export that source normally. On later inventories, a real/generated info file must rank ahead of the old marker-only placeholder, while a marker-only file remains selectable when it is the only usable candidate so regeneration can occur.

After the inventory worker phase completes, postprocess must print concise status lines to the console with a POSTPROCESS: prefix for each major finalization stage, including reading metadata logs, resolving existing bootlist/volume policy, preparing the setlists directory, exporting setlists/building bootlist rows, writing bootlist.csv, writing unidentifiedShows.txt, writing artistsNotInDatabase.txt, and writing summary.log. Setlist export progress must be throttled so large runs do not flood the console with frequent X/Y processed messages; report only coarse progress plus completion.

For every path-scoped re-inventory that replaces existing bootlist rows, postprocess must reconcile the old replacement population with the new scan before final output is considered complete. The reconciliation must report each affected volume/path scope, previous bootlist rows replaced, Stage 2 groups prepared, the prepared-versus-previous delta, Stage 3 metadata records, groups omitted before metadata output, groups removed for proven corruption, final new bootlist rows, unresolved records omitted from bootlist output, the net replacement-row change, and the current unresolved/corruption-removed paths when any exist. TLOHome/logs/reinventoryDelta.log must additionally account for every previous bootlist row with an evidence-based disposition: UNCHANGED, METADATA_CHANGED, RENAMED, RENAMED_METADATA_CHANGED, SPLIT, MERGED, REGROUPED, CORRUPTION_REMOVED, UNRESOLVED, or MISSING. It must separately list current NEW rows that have no previous-row disposition. Each detailed entry must include the old Show/path, any corresponding current Show/path values, and a concise reason. A rename or transfer may be classified as such only when the current metadata record preserves its first pre-mutation MAIN_DIR_PATH as ORIGINAL_MAIN_DIR_PATH; corruption removal must preserve the removed show-root path for reconciliation. Anything without affirmative evidence remains MISSING rather than being guessed away. Write the full per-entry detail append-only to TLOHome/logs/reinventoryDelta.log. Append the compact count/disposition summary (not thousands of per-row detail blocks) to summary.log and print one concise POSTPROCESS: re-inventory reconciliation status line to the console. The counts are diagnostic accounting; a changed row count is not by itself an error, but every reduction between prepared groups, Stage 3 records, and final rows must be visible.

When postprocess exports setlists and builds bootlist rows, it may split the work into parallel pieces according to the selected performance mode. The split must group records by normalized/truncated setlist filename base so duplicate shows and alternate setlist files cannot span worker boundaries. Each parallel piece may produce bootlist rows and setlist files for its filename-base group, but the final bootlist.csv write must remain single-threaded after all pieces are stitched, sorted, and combined with any kept existing rows. The number of filename-base groups is not the number of executor threads: postprocess must bound the ThreadPoolExecutor worker count, honor a positive --max-workers/Max Workers value, and never attempt to create one operating-system thread per filename group. If a parallel worker pool fails, preserve completed path results. Retry only paths without confirmed successful results, and never automatically replay uncertain mutating work (rename, tag, move, conversion, or deep checks); report the incomplete scope for review.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Search Path is required for every Full Inventory run. In the GUI it is entered in the main Path(s) text box; on the inventory CLI it is supplied with --search-path STRING. For UNC paths, the server/share root is an independent visible volume identity (UNC:server/share); only its relative subpath is stored.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Path(s) may contain one or more semicolon-separated entries. A direct entry uses the same inventory-control grammar formerly used by one toBeInventoried.txt line: optional [Volume] prefix, a fully qualified path, and optional --/slam ARTIST_NAME, --/copy DESTINATION, or --/copy-delete DESTINATION directives. Commas and apostrophes/single quotes are ordinary characters inside paths and directive values and do not require quoting. Matching double quotes remain accepted when users prefer them. A Path(s) entry whose physical path ends in .txt is treated as an inventory-control file under the established line/comment rules. UNC shares shall strip server/share for path comparison but preserve their share identity in the separate volume label.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Before inventory workers start, identify each search root by visible volume name plus the path below that volume. The physical drive letter, such as E: or F:, and WSL mount prefix, such as /mnt/e or /mnt/f, are not part of the stored inventory identity. Existing groups*.log files may contain more than one top-of-file SEARCH_PATH line for the same token; startup must read every header SEARCH_PATH value, falling back to legacy groupsLog header text only when SEARCH_PATH is absent.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: For existing-log comparison and bootlist replacement, strip any Windows drive letter or WSL mount prefix from both the queued search path and the stored log/header/bootlist path before testing exact, parent, child, or subtree relationships. The visible volume name is compared separately. bootlist.csv and top-of-log SEARCH_PATH headers must write the rootless path; detailed structured records such as MAIN_DIR_PATH may still preserve the physical path used by the scan for diagnostics and file access.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: A blank visible volume label is an append-only special case. There is only one blank-volume log set. When the visible volume label is blank, log SEARCH_PATH headers must be written as [] with no path. Blank-label inventories never trigger skip, overwrite, or re-inventory decisions; every blank-label run appends to the blank-volume log set. The user is responsible for tracking blank-label drives and cleaning duplicates if the same content is scanned more than once.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: REQ-PHYSICAL-DRIVE-001  On native Windows, physical-disk scheduling may query Get-Partition/Get-Disk using only the PowerShell executable under System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0 obtained from the trusted Windows directory API (GetSystemWindowsDirectoryW / GetWindowsDirectoryW). Never locate this executable using PATH, the process current directory, or environment variables. If the API directory is missing, malformed, or the command fails, report unknown physical-drive identity and use existing visible-volume scheduling fallback rather than executing another binary. Under WSL, keep the separate interoperable powershell.exe discovery path.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: When more than one accessible search path is queued, scheduling is based on the resolved visible volume label and a best-effort runtime physical-drive identity. Labeled volumes are processed before blank-label volumes. Labeled volumes on different physical drives may run in parallel; labeled volumes detected on the same physical hard drive must be placed in one serial worker group to avoid competing I/O. Every path whose resolved visible volume label is blank must be searched serially after labeled-volume work completes, sorted by drive letter or WSL /mnt/<drive> letter. Paths with nonblank visible volume labels are eligible for parallel processing according to Performance Mode and Max Workers. Different named volumes may run concurrently. Multiple roots that resolve to the same named volume must remain serial within one volume worker so they cannot write the same tokenized log files concurrently. On native Windows, any PowerShell helper used to resolve physical-drive identity must run without creating a visible console or Windows Terminal window.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: When multiple queued search paths share the same nonblank visible volume and do not overlap, the dispatcher must assign or reuse one token for that visible volume and append each non-overlapping root to the token header. A mixed run that replaces one same-volume subtree and adds another same-volume non-overlapping path must preserve unrelated existing bootlist rows and must not fail volume-action validation.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: TLOHome/toBeInventoried.txt is not an automatic inventory input. Full Inventory must never fall back to or silently read that file when Search Path is blank. The file remains distributed in COMPLETE installations only as an example/template; to use it, the user must explicitly enter its fully qualified .txt path in Search Path. Any other .txt filename is equally valid when explicitly supplied through Search Path.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: All editable GUI fields that accept a filesystem path SHALL support Windows File Explorer drag/drop under native Windows TkDND. This includes Main Path(s); the Destination of Copies dialog shared by Tag Copy and Tag Copy/Delete Original; Copy Requests Path(s) and Destination; Manual Updates Original and destination Path; the New Name folder drop; and Add New Shows Search Path. A folder dropped onto a single-directory field fills that entry; a file uses its containing folder unless the field explicitly supports a .txt control file. Existing field validation SHALL run after the drop, including the destination capacity check and disabling OK when the destination is invalid. Non-path fields and Linux/WSL controls do not gain drop targets.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: On native Windows only, the GUI Path(s) text box accepts drag/drop from File Explorer. Each Windows/TkDND drop payload must be processed as the complete file list supplied by File Explorer, so one drop may contain one or more folders and/or .txt control files and every selected item is retained. Every dropped item is converted using the established Path(s) drop rules, then appended to the existing Path(s) value in payload order with semicolons inserted automatically. Repeated drag actions are cumulative. For example, dropping A, then B, then C and D together produces A;B;C;D. Commas inside dropped paths remain ordinary path characters and do not require automatic quoting.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Under WSL and regular Linux, Search Path drag/drop is not an available feature. The GUI must not register or advertise a file-drop target on WSL or regular Linux; users should type/paste the required Search Path or use --search-path. A .txt control file is used only when its fully qualified path is explicitly supplied in Search Path.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: For a .txt inventory-control file supplied through Search Path, blank lines and lines whose first non-whitespace character is # are ignored. Lines beginning with REM remain accepted as comments. Each remaining line is one inventory root using the established inventory-control line format.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Each direct Search Path entry and each non-comment .txt control-file line may include optional per-path directives after the path: --/slam ARTIST_NAME, --/copy DESTINATION, and --/copy-delete DESTINATION. Directive order after the path does not matter, but --/copy and --/copy-delete are mutually exclusive on one entry.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: When --/copy or --/copy-delete is used on a direct Search Path entry or inside a .txt control file, the destination must be an existing fully qualified directory. --/copy activates inventory-time Tag Copy for that path only and keeps inventory ownership with the original source tree. --/copy-delete activates Tag Copy/Delete Original for that path only. TLO must complete show grouping and metadata extraction from the original source tree before copying or moving the identified show folder. After transfer, tagging and final inventory output use the copied/moved destination tree, unless the main-window Tag Copy/Delete Original checkbox is active; in that case, the destination selected in its warning dialog is the global override. Exception: a Windows UNC share always receives its canonical UNC:server/share identifier rather than a blank label, even if the remote share reports no volume label.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Each search path string may optionally begin with a bracketed visible volume prefix immediately before the fully defined physical path. Accepted forms include [Volume]E:\path, [Volume]E:, [Volume]/mnt/e/path, [Volume]/mnt/e, and [Volume] /mnt/e/path. The bracketed value is the visible volume name and must be stored/logged without the brackets.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: If no bracketed visible volume prefix is supplied, resolve the operating-system volume label for the physical search root and use that label as the visible volume name for search-path comparison and top-of-log writing. If the operating system reports no volume label, or reports a default non-identifying label of New Volume or Local Disk, the visible volume name remains the empty string, log headers are written as [] with no path, and the run uses the blank-label append-only policy. An explicit bracketed prefix, including an explicit [] blank prefix, is not replaced by the operating-system volume label; instead, if the operating-system volume label can be resolved, the explicit prefix must match the mounted drive label or the path is rejected before inventory processing starts. Explicit bracketed labels of [New Volume] or [Local Disk] are treated as blank visible volume labels.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Both quoted and unquoted path strings must be supported where the shell/platform allows them.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Windows drive-rooted search paths must preserve the complete user-supplied subtree when normalized for WSL/Linux, including comma-bearing artist folders such as D:\B-J\D\Dudek, Les. A non-root Windows path must never be reduced to only /mnt/<drive> during full inventory path normalization.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: A slam value may be associated with an individual direct Search Path entry or with an inventory root inside a .txt control file by using --/slam ARTIST_NAME.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The main GUI does not provide a separate Slam field. GUI users attach --/slam ARTIST_NAME to the applicable Path(s) entry or place it on the applicable line in a .txt control file. The command line may supply --/slam STRING for direct --search-path entries. Do not combine the separate command-line --/slam value with a .txt Search Path control file, and reject an entry that supplies both an inline and separate slam as ambiguous.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: --/slam/--/slam must not be accepted by itself. If supplied without Search Path, report an error and exit.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: If slam is non-empty for a search path, use slam as the artist for all groups under that path and skip artist identification for those groups.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Slam values are treated as supplied artist names for metadata purposes, then pass through the same downstream artist-name normalization and setlist-filename sanitization used for other artist names. Do not use filename-unsafe characters from slam values verbatim in generated setlist filenames.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Resolve TLOHome before loading input files or databases.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: TLOHome precedence must be: --myTLO, then --TLOHome, then the TLOHome environment variable.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: --myTLO is undocumented and must override --TLOHome if both are supplied. This compatibility argument is accepted by tlo-gi.py, tlo-main.py, and tlo-research.py, but must not appear as a visible GUI input field or ordinary user-facing help option.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: If no TLOHome source is available, present a readable startup error.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Normalize search paths consistently across Linux, Windows, WSL, and macOS.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Windows paths such as E:\B-J\G must be accepted on Windows.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: WSL mount paths such as /mnt/e/B-J/G must be accepted on WSL/Linux.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: When a Windows drive path such as E:\B-J\G and a WSL/Linux mount path such as /mnt/e/B-J/G refer to the same physical root on the current platform, normalize the physical path for scanning, but keep the bracketed visible volume name unchanged for log output and comparison.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Do not rely on brittle WSL mount assumptions; prefer checking whether the normalized path can be listed/read.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Before path scanning and path-worker dispatch, check every search root for accessibility.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: For each inaccessible root, record and report the original path, normalized path, and reason.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Reasons should include at least: path does not exist, path is empty, or path is not readable.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Accessible roots proceed to inventory; inaccessible roots are reported and skipped unless all roots are inaccessible.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Print the root-preparation summary after accessibility checks.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Check all search roots for duplicate paths after normalization.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Reject overlapping search roots before scanning. Examples: /mnt/e/g and /mnt/e/g/more; E:\G and E:\G\More.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: If overlapping roots are detected, report a readable error and do not start scanning.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Perform uniqueness and overlap checks before worker dispatch so collisions are detected early.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The User Manual must warn that OS-specific aliases, symlinks, junctions, mount aliases, or case-sensitive/case-insensitive equivalents may not all be detected as overlaps and can produce duplicate inventory entries if supplied as separate roots.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Print a startup banner that includes the executable name, application version, and build number.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The startup banner build number comes from constants defined in the source package, not from the script filename or a command-line argument. The release change-description text must not be appended to the startup banner, including when debug is enabled.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Print Starting inventory after roots are loaded and validated.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: When multiple accessible search paths exist, use the performance-controlled worker count for volume work groups. All blank-volume paths form one serial work group, sorted by drive letter or WSL /mnt/<drive> letter. Blank-volume work must start only after all labeled-volume work has completed; blank-volume roots do not run concurrently with labeled-volume roots. Each distinct nonblank visible volume label forms a visible-volume group, and roots sharing that label run serially inside the same worker. Before dispatch, named visible-volume groups that are detected on the same physical hard drive are combined into one serial physical-drive worker group. Named visible-volume groups on different physical drives may run in parallel. Parallel workers are used only when the effective worker count and named physical-drive work-group count are both greater than one.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Print a queued line for each search path, including the slam value even if blank.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Startup banner example: Starting tlo-gi <current DISPLAY_VERSION>. The displayed public version/build must come from tlo_version.DISPLAY_VERSION rather than from a hard-coded version string.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Each search path must emit the following status and completion lines exactly, except for substituted values.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The lines are suppressed when --silent is set.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The program must run on Linux, Windows, WSL, and macOS.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Frozen Windows executables must support multiprocessing startup without argparse rejecting bootstrap arguments and without leaving active worker processes running after GUI cancellation.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Both tlo-gi.py and tlo-main.py must call multiprocessing.freeze_support() before command-line parsing, Tkinter initialization, inventory startup, or process-pool creation.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Frozen Windows child-worker bootstrap arguments must be consumed by multiprocessing startup and must not be parsed as normal TLO command-line arguments.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: A frozen tlo-main.exe must not open duplicate GUI windows in multiprocessing child workers.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The same code path must remain harmless under normal Python execution on Linux, WSL, macOS, and non-frozen Windows.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: If a path-worker process pool becomes unusable because of startup or infrastructure failure, report the pool failure and retry the affected inventory paths serially rather than ending the run with only a generic process-pool error.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The runtime must keep track of the active ProcessPoolExecutor so GUI Quit and Ctrl-C can terminate path-worker processes before active log cleanup.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: When the GUI Quit button or the window close control is used while an inventory scan is still active, immediately display an alert that inventory is stopping and it will take a moment to clean up before exiting. The alert must appear before active workers are terminated and active logs are cleaned up.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The cleanup path must work on Windows frozen executables and normal Linux/WSL/macOS execution without leaving worker processes running after the parent GUI exits.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The inventory must support CPU and filesystem load controls so large scans do not make Windows File Explorer or the host operating system unusable.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Add --performance-mode with values gentle, balanced, fast, and extreme.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Add --max-workers N. On the CLI, 0 continues to mean use the selected Performance Mode default. In the GUI, Max Workers is a worker ceiling, not a requested or forced worker count. Unless a positive launcher --max-workers value is supplied, the displayed automatic ceiling must match the selected mode: gentle = 1; balanced = min(2, platform CPU count); fast = platform CPU count; extreme = min(4 × platform CPU count, 64), with a minimum of 1 in every case. Selecting a different Performance Mode must reset Max Workers to that mode’s automatic ceiling. The user may then edit Max Workers to another positive ceiling. Each phase remains free to use fewer workers when its Performance Mode, physical-drive serialization, work-group count, correctness constraints, or phase-specific safety limit requires fewer.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Gentle mode uses one search-path worker by default and applies filesystem traversal throttling. On Windows, the long-lived inventory process uses idle priority when supported. On POSIX platforms, the long-lived GUI/CLI parent remains at normal priority; gentle niceness is applied only inside worker processes so a later mode cannot leave the GUI permanently deprioritized.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Balanced mode uses limited parallelism, no more than two workers by default and no more than the platform CPU count, and applies light traversal throttling. On Windows, the long-lived inventory process uses below-normal priority when supported. On POSIX platforms, only worker processes are niced; the long-lived GUI/CLI parent remains at normal priority.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Fast mode uses maximum-throughput behavior: available workers up to the platform CPU count and, at runtime, up to the number of parallelizable volume work groups; it uses normal process priority and no traversal throttling. On Windows, selecting Fast after Gentle or Balanced must explicitly restore the process priority class captured at application startup (normally Normal).

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Extreme mode is the opt-in speed-first mode. It uses normal priority, no traversal throttling, and unsorted Phase 1 traversal. Extreme may request one search-path worker per otherwise-parallelizable work group, but the runtime count is still bounded by the positive Max Workers ceiling and all physical-drive/correctness constraints. Postprocess remains separately bounded and honors the same positive Max Workers ceiling. On Windows, selecting Extreme after a lower-priority mode must restore the startup process priority class.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The effective runtime worker count is the minimum of the selected Performance Mode demand, the number of parallelizable work groups after physical-drive serialization, the phase-specific safety/correctness limit, and the positive Max Workers ceiling. A phase may therefore use substantially fewer workers than the Max Workers value. CLI --max-workers 0 or omission selects the normal mode/platform default behavior; the GUI displays a positive ceiling rather than an auto sentinel.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The GUI and CLI must default to balanced Performance Mode unless another mode is supplied.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The CLI must default to balanced mode.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The GUI must expose Performance Mode and Max Workers controls.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The GUI must provide Pause and Resume controls. Pause must cause traversal to yield between directory operations; workers complete their current directory operation before suspending, and no new directories are dispatched while paused. Resume must continue the run without restarting it. Pause applies to active traversal/inventory work and does not delete logs or cancel already completed postprocess output.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: On Windows frozen executables, the GUI process and worker processes should run at idle priority in gentle mode and below-normal priority in balanced mode when supported. The runtime must remember the original process priority class before lowering it and must restore that class explicitly for Fast and Extreme, including Gentle -> Fast and Balanced -> Extreme transitions in one GUI session.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: On Linux, WSL, and macOS, the long-lived GUI/CLI parent process must not be permanently niced. Gentle and balanced priority reduction should be applied only inside spawned inventory worker processes where supported. If a run executes serially in the parent, worker-count limits and traversal throttling still apply while the parent remains at normal niceness.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: If OS-level priority changes are unavailable, the program must continue without error and rely on worker limits and traversal throttling. Failure to lower or restore priority is best-effort and must not prevent inventory.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Filesystem-heavy walkers must periodically yield during directory traversal in gentle and balanced modes.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Phase 2/3 should build music groups from the Phase 1 complete-path log instead of performing a second full discovery walk over the same search tree. Phase 2/3 must read representative media-file paths from the complete-path log, derive the music directory and media type from those paths, and rescan the known music directory or allowed parent only when a later step needs setlist candidates, media counts, exact filenames, filename-date evidence, or tag samples.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Before Phase 1 begins, TLO must preflight destinations for operations that will create a real copy. This includes --/copy directives on direct Search Path entries or inside .txt control files, separate command-line --/copy directives applied to direct Search Path entries, Tag Copy destinations, and any --/copy-delete or Tag Copy/Delete Original destination that is on a different filesystem from its source. Same-filesystem Copy/Delete Original transfers are directory moves and must be excluded from source-size totaling and destination-capacity comparison.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Before totaling source folder sizes for this preflight, TLO must print a console note that it is checking source folder sizes before validating destination capacity. The note is informational and must appear before the potentially slow folder-size walk starts.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: When Inventory is started with Tag Copy or Tag Copy/Delete Original selected, TLO must open the selected mode's destination dialog. Both dialogs require an existing fully qualified path and may display readable free-space information. Tag Copy states that the original is retained and always performs exact source-size capacity preflight because it always creates another tree. Tag Copy/Delete Original additionally warns that original material will be removed after transfer; its exact source-size capacity preflight applies only to source roots on a different filesystem from the destination. The selected destination is a global override for per-path --/copy and --/copy-delete destinations. Preflight must sum only roots expanded from the required Search Path that will actually be copied. A Dry Run still requests the destination so planned move/copy behavior and any applicable capacity requirement can be reviewed, but it must not transfer, Trash, or delete any content regardless of the corruption setting.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The preflight must group sources by effective destination, calculate the size of each top-level source tree, compare the total required destination space to current free space, and stop startup if a destination does not have enough space. The alert/error must identify the destination, the source path or paths feeding it, required space, available space, and additional space needed.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: REQ-XFER-003  Inventory-time Tag Copy/Delete Original must never populate a normal final-name directory with unverified or incomplete content. For cross-filesystem transfers, allocate an exclusively owned .tlo-partial-* staging directory, copy the entire source tree there, reject symbolic links, verify recursive relative file/directory structure and sizes, then SHA-256-verify every corresponding file. Only after all checks succeed may TLO atomically publish the directory under a collision-safe, non-overwriting final name, and only after publication may source deletion begin. Ordinary copy/verification/publication failure must leave the original intact, delete only the current operation's staging directory, and publish no incomplete normal-name folder. On source-cleanup failure preserve the published verified destination and report the potentially partial source for recovery. For same-filesystem transfers, do not copy or hash files: atomically rename the entire source directory into a unique, Phase-1-pruned .tlo-partial-* sibling under the destination parent, then atomically publish it with no-overwrite semantics. On ordinary publication failure attempt atomic no-overwrite rollback to the original source pathname; on rollback failure preserve the complete staged tree and report its exact recovery path. Worker death/power loss may leave a complete same-filesystem staged tree or a partial cross-filesystem staged copy. Both remain visibly marked and excluded from inventory, and neither may be mistaken for a published show. Tag Copy and Copy/Delete share the copying, verification, staging, and publication helpers while retaining their distinct verification strengths and source-retention rules.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: REQ-XFER-002  Ordinary inventory-time Tag Copy, including GUI Tag and --/copy, must copy the complete identified source folder into an exclusively created sibling .tlo-partial-* directory, which Phase 1 must exclude from inventory. Validate that the staged tree has no symlinks and verify the entire recursive relative directory structure, file names, and file sizes while the source remains intact. Only after success may TLO atomically publish the staged directory under an available final show name using a no-overwrite rename. A concurrently appearing destination must be preserved and a collision-safe alternate name attempted. Copy, verification, or publication failure must leave no incomplete normal-name directory; ordinary exceptions must clean up only the current operation's owned staging tree. Worker termination or power loss may leave an excluded .tlo-partial-* staging directory for later recovery/cleanup. Do not delete the source and do not weaken cross-filesystem Copy/Delete Original SHA-256 safeguards; dedicated Copy/Delete staging is scheduled separately.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: REQ-XFER-001  Transfer destinations must be claimed without overwriting an existing directory. If a destination name races with another creator, TLO must allocate another unique destination rather than replace the existing entry. Cross-filesystem Copy/Delete Original requires matching recursive relative directory/file structure and file sizes followed by SHA-256 verification of every corresponding file before source deletion. Ordinary Tag Copy retains the source and verifies recursive relative folder/file structure and file sizes without byte-content hashing by policy. If a verified Copy/Delete destination has been completed but later source cleanup fails, TLO must keep the verified destination, stop the operation, and report both the possibly partially removed source path and the verified destination for recovery.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Before any Tag Copy or Copy/Delete Original transfer, TLO must complete show grouping and metadata extraction from the original source tree. The source evidence includes the original folder and path components, selected setlist content, music filenames, and existing audio tags. Only after the show metadata record has been resolved may TLO copy or move the identified show folder and rewrite the active working paths to the destination. Tagging and final inventory output then use the destination path; metadata already resolved from the original source is retained. Ordinary Tag Copy always creates a real copy, even when source and destination are on the same filesystem. Before changes begin, TLO must total the full source size and compare it with destination free space. After copying, TLO must compare the source and destination relative-file maps and every corresponding file size before tagging continues; the original is retained. For Copy/Delete Original, TLO must determine filesystem identity before walking the source for sizes. If source and destination are on the same filesystem, TLO must perform a directory rename/move and must not total source file sizes, perform a source-size capacity comparison, or compare file sizes after the move. If they are on different filesystems, TLO must total the source, verify destination capacity, copy the tree, compare relative paths and file sizes, and delete the original only after verification succeeds. A destination must not be the source folder or a child of it.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: A Tag Copy or Copy/Delete Original transfer applies to the complete identified source folder tree rooted at MAIN_DIR_PATH, not only to inventoried music files or selected setlists. The transfer must include every file and every descendant directory beneath that folder, including non-music files and empty directories. A same-filesystem Copy/Delete Original directory rename/move naturally transfers the complete tree. A real copy must recursively copy the complete tree, and post-copy verification must compare all relative file paths, descendant directory structure, and file sizes. Cross-filesystem Copy/Delete Original must additionally compare SHA-256 contents of every corresponding file before deleting the source; ordinary Tag Copy does not require content hashing (REQ-XFER-001).

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Copy-versus-alternate naming is determined by the same recursive filename and exact-size rule used by duplicate cleanup, not by name collision alone. Before TLO appends (copyN) to a Show qualifier or compliant destination/renamed folder, it compares the incoming MAIN_DIR_PATH tree against existing same-base sibling/destination-family trees. Matching relative descendant folder names (including empty folders), file names and exact sizes classify the tree as (copyN), without reading or hashing file bytes. Folder structure or names/sizes that differ yield (altN). If a comparison fails, classify as alternate. A folder already ending with (copyN) is revalidated with the same rule before SHOW_NAME propagation. This applies to show/folder collision naming only; generated setlist filename collision handling remains separate. Cross-volume transfer integrity checks remain byte-verified.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Windows source-preflight safety: all source-bundle ZIP member paths SHALL be compatible with Windows Expand-Archive (no colon or other forbidden characters, reserved device names, or trailing spaces/dots). Regression test mocks of FFmpeg protocol destinations such as pipe:1 SHALL NOT write literal source-tree files. Every ZIP member except the checksum manifest SHALL be listed by filename in the current-build SHA256SUMS manifest. Source preflight SHALL pass Ruff F401 and F841 before hosted release; corrections to legacy tests SHALL NOT disable or weaken the lint gate.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Every numbered source update must produce platform-specific end-user release assets in addition to the source bundle and current Requirements Specification DOCX included in each source, complete and update release package.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Release asset names must use the supplied public version number and numeric build number. The GitHub build process accepts -vnumber VERSION and -bnumber BUILD; it tracks the local release folder by build number while using the supplied version in tags, release titles, asset names, manifests, and notes. External GitHub Actions in official release workflows SHALL be pinned to reviewed full 40-character commit SHAs rather than floating tags or mutable branches.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Release packaging supports three package selections. The default produces eight ZIP assets: complete and update packages for Windows hybrid, Windows shared-onedir, macOS, and generic Linux. Complete-only produces the four complete ZIPs; update-only produces the four update ZIPs. Asset names use the public version supplied by tlo_version.PUBLIC_VERSION/runtime -vnumber and follow TLO_V<VERSION>Build<BUILD>_complete_Windows.zip, TLO_V<VERSION>Build<BUILD>_complete_Windows_onedir.zip, TLO_V<VERSION>Build<BUILD>_complete_Linux.zip, TLO_V<VERSION>Build<BUILD>_complete_macOS.zip, plus the corresponding update names. Distribution-root defaults in the native helper scripts must derive the same PUBLIC_VERSION rather than hard-coding an older release line.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The GitHub Build Process regenerates the Windows distribution builder from a locked template before CI. The generated script SHALL include fail-closed checks for both Main/Search PNG and ICO runtime assets and pass both to the onefile PyInstaller --add-data options and the corresponding shared-onedir Analysis datas. Before push, the process SHALL independently verify that this generated template actually wires those assets, so the main and search windows retain their correct icon after source snapshot preparation.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Canonical application icon assets are icons/tlo-main-icon.*, icons/tlo-search-icon.*, and icons/tlo-tag-icon.* in PNG/Windows ICO/macOS ICNS forms as applicable. Windows and macOS native build helpers must fail closed when required platform icon resources are missing; the Main application must not depend on legacy tlo-inventory-icon.* filenames. Running tlo-main and tlo-search windows shall use the respective TLO artwork rather than the default Tkinter feather: the root window shall set the iconphoto default for subsequently created Tk Toplevel windows, and on Windows shall also apply the matching ICO with iconbitmap. Windows native bundles must embed both the source ICO/PNG window assets as PyInstaller data in addition to the PE executable icon; macOS and Linux bundles must embed the PNG assets. Source and onefile/frozen paths must resolve the packaged assets without depending on the current working directory. A missing or unsupported runtime icon shall not crash inventory or search; CI packaging/behavior contracts must verify the required assets are included.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Windows executables must be built on Windows, macOS executables on macOS, and generic Linux executables on a normal Linux system. The generic Linux build is also the WSL build. The release process must not treat PyInstaller as a cross-compiler for Windows or macOS. The current macOS GUI packaging uses PyInstaller onefile plus .app bundles and therefore requires PyInstaller < 7 until TLO deliberately migrates those GUI apps to an onedir-style bundle. Native/local distribution helpers must reject a supplied bundle/build number that does not match tlo_version.BUNDLE_BUILD. The Windows local-distribution default output must be under a user-writable profile location rather than the root of C:\.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: All platform executables/scripts must be completed before final release assembly. The assembler must reject missing platform folders, missing required applications, missing manifests, missing scan receipts, or missing checksums.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Each native platform build must run at least one configured malware scanner after executable creation. An official scan result must identify an approved scanner identity; an arbitrary command that merely exits successfully must not qualify as an official clean scanner. For a custom Norton receipt, TLO must parse the command as argv rather than shell text, resolve the executable that will actually run, require an approved Norton executable basename, and on Windows require the resolved executable to be under a standard Program Files tree with a valid Norton Authenticode signer. A nonzero scanner result, quarantine/removal, missing executable, unapproved scanner identity, failed executable-identity validation, or post-scan file change must fail the build.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Native PyInstaller packaging of tlo-gi, tlo-main, tlo-tag, and tlo-deleteDupes must include the checksum-pinned ffmpeg executable prepared by prepare_ffmpeg.py beneath tlo_ffmpeg_bin and must execute a frozen tlo-gi packaging smoke test before malware scanning or release assembly. The smoke test must run with a hostile IMAGEIO_FFMPEG_EXE value so an external override cannot satisfy the bundled-binary gate. Failure to import required dependencies, locate/run the packaged ffmpeg, or complete the smoke test must fail the native build. imageio-ffmpeg is not a runtime or packaging dependency.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Each platform scan must produce a clean JSON receipt containing the approved scanner identity, scanner result, platform, and SHA-256 hash and size for every packaged platform artifact. For a custom Norton scan the receipt must also bind the resolved scanner executable path and SHA-256; on Windows it must record Authenticode status and signer subject. Receipt artifact-root/path fields must be portable/relative and must not embed a workstation username-bearing absolute path. Final ZIP assembly must verify that the current files exactly match those receipts.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: After receipt verification, the assembler must run a final aggregate malware scan of each staged complete or update package. A ZIP asset must not be created unless that scan reports clean.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The malware gate establishes only that the configured scanners reported the exact packaged artifacts clean at build time. The project must not claim that no antivirus product can ever report a later heuristic false positive. Windows code signing, macOS Developer ID signing/notarization, reproducible builds, and vendor false-positive submission should be used when available.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Release ZIP filenames are versioned, but ZIP contents must not be wrapped in a versioned top-level folder. Users extract a complete package directly into the chosen TLOHome, or manually copy an update package into an existing TLOHome.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Complete platform ZIPs must include required shared support folders, documentation, starter files, manifests, checksums, scan receipts, a blank header-only bootlist.csv containing exactly sep=^ followed by Show^VolumePath, and TLO_DBs/artists.sqlite plus TLO_DBs/venues.txt for a fresh install. Update ZIPs omit TLO_DBs by default, but the build process may explicitly include exactly TLO_DBs/artists.sqlite and TLO_DBs/venues.txt in update packages when a database refresh is requested. Database-inclusive distributions SHALL also stage the physical TLO_DBs/venues.sqlite master; retain venues.txt for legacy fallback.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Update ZIPs must contain the matching platform app payload, the current RTF User Manual, consolidated Requirements Specification DOCX, current CHANGES file and FAQ, matching native scan receipt, final aggregate package scan receipt, UPDATE_MANIFEST.json, README_UPDATE.txt, and checksums. They must never contain bootlist.csv, toBeInventoried.txt, setlists/, logs/, debug/, dups/, readyForXfer/, staged/, or other user-created state. Unless database inclusion is explicitly selected, they must not contain TLO_DBs/. When database inclusion is selected, only artists.sqlite and venues.txt are permitted under TLO_DBs/. Database-inclusive distributions SHALL also stage the physical TLO_DBs/venues.sqlite master; retain venues.txt for legacy fallback.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Every update ZIP must include UPDATE_MANIFEST.json with package kind update, exact platform/layout key, build number, safe_update true, requires_complete_install false, installed-path entries, databases_included, database_files, and protected paths documenting user-data areas intentionally absent from the package. Before accepting a downloaded update, TLO must require safe_update to be the Boolean value true and requires_complete_install to be the Boolean value false; require protected_paths to match the canonical protected user-data set, with TLO_DBs/ protected unless an explicit database refresh is declared; reject any ZIP member at or below a protected path using case-insensitive path comparison; reject ZIP member names that collide case-insensitively; and reject any ZIP path component that is a Windows reserved device name, including the superscript COM/LPT 1-3 forms, through the shared Windows reserved-name validator. The manifest/readme and actual ZIP contents must agree about database inclusion.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Complete platform ZIPs must include the current RTF User Manual, consolidated Requirements Specification DOCX, current CHANGES file, an example/template toBeInventoried.txt, the blank header-only bootlist.csv starter file, manifest data, checksums, and clean scan receipts. The starter bootlist is for a new TLOHome only and must never be included in update ZIPs. The toBeInventoried template is not an automatic TLOHome input; users invoke that format only by explicitly supplying the template path (or another .txt control-file path) in Search Path. The requirements document remains in the source bundle and is provided separately; it is not included in end-user complete or update ZIPs.

Section: 2. Search Path, Accessibility, and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The TLO application source bundle and the independently versioned GitHub Build Process are separate artifacts. The flat TLO source bundle shall contain no GitHub Build Process files, including Run-TLO-GitHub-Build.ps1, Create-TLOArtifactSigningMetadata.ps1, TLO_GitHub_Build_Process_Requirements_v<PROCESS>.docx, TLO_GitHub_Build_Process_v<PROCESS>.zip, or other process-only support/setup files. Application distribution helpers such as createWindowsDist.ps1, createLinuxDist.sh, createMacOSDist.sh, and scan_release_artifacts.py remain TLO source-bundle content. The GitHub Build Process shall be distributed only as its own independently versioned package and may supply/inject its own transient build-process helpers when it consumes a TLO source bundle. Every source, complete, and update package SHALL carry exactly one current-version User Manual (RTF), Requirements Specification (DOCX), and change log (TXT); no other versions, historical change-log archives, or replacement specification files may ship. Missing or extra documentation SHALL block signing and publication.
If a directory name ends with -ignoreDir, do not record that directory and do not descend into it.

Phase 1 and Phase 2/3 shall continue descending into child directories after a parent directory containing music has been recorded. A nested music folder can therefore be inventoried independently as an opening act. Existing wrapper/part aggregation remains authoritative for CD, Disc, Set, volume, and other recognized multi-part structures. A date-bearing show may nevertheless remain one logical show when all music is exactly one validated media-wrapper level deeper, such as Show/FLAC/Set 1 and Show/FLAC/Set 2; this guarded case does not authorize scanning sibling shows.
Skip Windows system directories including $RECYCLE.BIN and System Volume Information.
Directory pruning must prevent descent by modifying the traversal directory list in place when using os.walk.

Walk each directory only until a real music/video file has been identified. Once a real media file is found, Phase 1 must identify the directory as a media directory and must not continue collecting every media filename from that directory. (see Appendix E1)

Once a music/video file is found, Phase 1 records one representative media-file path for that directory rather than every media filename, but traversal continues into child directories so independent nested shows/opening acts can still be discovered. Recognized wrapper/part and dated-show supplemental containment rules may later aggregate qualifying descendants back into one logical show. The directory path and media type are derived later from the representative sample path.

After Phase 1 finishes for a search path, compact the active compN.log complete-path log defensively so it contains no more than one representative media-file row per music directory. This compaction also applies to append-mode and reused logs so legacy entries that listed every media file do not remain. Later grouping and tagging stages must rescan the known music directory when they need counts or full file lists; compN.log is not a tag manifest.

Phase 1 must not carry .txt, .rtf, .doc, or .docx setlist candidate filenames forward in the complete-path log. Setlist candidate discovery happens later by scanning the known media directory, then the allowed immediate parent when the parent-safety rules permit it, then selected sibling information folders such as info, setlist, set list, data, notes, docs, or text inside a compact parent, and descendant locations only as the lowest-priority fallback.

Parent/sibling setlist discovery is allowed only under the combined compact/safe-parent rules. The immediate parent may be searched when the music directory is its only child, when all relevant child directories are recognized related wrapper/release parts, or when the parent is compact with twelve or fewer child directories. In those same safe-parent cases, sibling information folders such as info, setlist, set list, data, notes, docs, text, or similar may be searched. Direct music-folder candidates remain highest priority; unsafe broad parent/sibling scans are not permitted.
Targeted descendant setlist lookup must log candidate setlist files only. It must not log deeper media files as inventory candidates and must not create additional music groups from that descent.
If a usable setlist candidate is found in the music directory itself during later setlist selection, do not promote lower-priority descendant candidates ahead of it.

When music is found in a folder whose visible name is a common media-only or wrapper-style folder name, such as CD1, Disc 1, flac, music, tunes, audio, or similar names defined by the wrapper rules, the inventory may check the immediate parent folder for a setlist only when that parent is directly related to the child music folder. Direct relation means the parent has only that one child directory, or the parent child directories are all related wrapper/release parts for the same logical release. This eligibility check is performed during setlist candidate discovery and must also constrain later setlist ranking/selection so an ineligible broad-parent setlist is not promoted. Do not use a parent-folder setlist from a broad artist, collection, or storage directory merely because it contains the current music child among many unrelated children.

Before ranking or selecting a setlist source candidate, inspect a leading content sample when available. Source setlist candidates may be plain text .txt files and the supported rich-text/word-processing exceptions .rtf and .docx. Legacy binary .doc names may be recognized for diagnostics, but .doc content is not decoded as text and cannot satisfy the readable-text candidate checks. Reject candidates that are empty, unreadable, binary-like, full of NULL characters, lack readable alphabetic content, are checksum-only, or match housekeeping names. Valid UTF-16 text must be decoded before applying the NULL/binary rejection rules to .txt files. Rich-text/Word candidates must still pass the same naming, housekeeping, and readable-text rules used for setlist candidates. TLO must read no more than 1 MiB while sampling an ordinary text/RTF candidate. A full ordinary text read must be rejected when the file exceeds 16 MiB. Before reading a DOCX candidate, TLO must inspect word/document.xml and reject it when its declared uncompressed size exceeds 16 MiB; the oversized XML entry must not be decompressed.

A parent directory with multiple child directories is related only when every direct music-bearing child directory belongs to the same wrapper/common release relationship, such as CD1/CD2/CD3, Set 1/Set 2, Disk3, or wrapper-suffixed siblings that share the same stripped release base such as Big Release CD 1 and Big Release CD 2. If any direct music-bearing sibling is unrelated, the parent is a collection/search container and must not become the logical show root.

In non-compliant mode, if a music directory visible name is, or ends in, a wrapper-like release-part string such as CD 1, CD1, Disc 1, Disk3, Part 2, Set 1, or similar, check sibling music folders under the common parent for related release parts. Named suffix folders aggregate only when at least two related parts exist and all direct music-bearing children under the parent belong to that same release. Exact wrapper folders may use the parent only when no unrelated direct music-bearing child exists.
