In Compliant mode, group a dated show parent containing two or more direct media-bearing Disc/CD/Set/Part/Tape/Side sibling folders only when the folders all use the same wrapper kind and their unique sequence numbers are consecutive beginning at 1. Use the parent for show identity; preserve all disc media paths; do not require a setlist or read tags. A single disc, a numbering gap, an unrelated or mixed-kind sibling, direct parent audio, or an unidentifiable collection parent prevents this Compliant aggregation.

A guarded nested wrapper layout may cross exactly one additional non-numbered media-container folder. For example, Show/FLAC/Set 1 and Show/FLAC/Set 2 form one logical show rooted at Show, and a setlist stored directly in Show applies to both parts. The numbered part names include Set, Disc, Disk, CD, D, Part, Side, and Tape forms recognized by the wrapper rules. Promotion requires a date-bearing Show folder, an exact non-numbered media-container directory, a validated related part relationship, and no music-bearing descendant of Show outside that container. Setlist lookup may inspect only the direct files in Show; it must not enumerate or recursively revisit Show's sibling directories.

Exact wrapper part folders such as Jayhawks - Big Release/CD1, Jayhawks - Big Release/CD2, and Jayhawks - Big Release/CD3 must be aggregated as one logical show rooted at the common parent Jayhawks - Big Release.

Parenthesized-number release parts: a bare terminal (N) is not a generic wrapper marker. Aggregate folders named Parent (1), Parent (2), through Parent (N) only when at least two parts exist, their numeric suffixes are unique and consecutive beginning at 1, every direct music-bearing child under the common parent belongs to that same numbered set, the stripped common base exactly matches the parent directory name, and the parent itself contains no directly inventoried music. Otherwise keep the children as separate logical groups. A valid numbered set is rooted at the common parent and creates one metadata record.

Wrapper-suffixed music folders such as Marcus, Jay/Big Release CD 1, Marcus, Jay/Big Release CD 2, and Marcus, Jay/Big Release CD 3 must be aggregated as one logical album named Big Release under the common parent Marcus, Jay.

Volume-style release-part suffixes such as (Volume 1), (Vol 2), (Vol. 2), (v.1), and v2 are non-compliant release-part aggregation markers only for collection-style sibling folders under a common parent. A short v-number inside a larger descriptive parenthetical, such as (WLIR-FM, rm v.2), is not a volume marker. Differing-base volume siblings aggregate only when every direct music-bearing child under the parent is a volume part; the presence of any unrelated music sibling prevents parent aggregation.

Aggregated release-part groups must collect representative media-file paths and representative media extensions from all related part folders and must create only one metadata record and one bootlist row for the logical show. An aggregated group must never overlap another logical group under the same parent. Setlist candidates and exact media filenames are discovered later from the known part folders when needed.

After non-compliant grouping decisions are complete and before Stage 3 mutation work is scheduled, buckets that resolve to the same normalized physical MAIN_DIR_PATH must be collapsed into one logical group. Merge their unique music directories, media files, sample files, and media extensions and preserve applicable aggregation metadata. No two Stage 3 jobs may independently tag or rename the same logical show root merely because direct root audio and wrapper/supplemental descendants were initially discovered through different grouping paths.

Sequential number-word show parts: During non-compliant Full Inventory, direct sibling music directories named one, two, three, etc. MAY be one logical show only when their immediate common parent has a fully specified performance date and a shared parent-local setlist, all direct music-bearing siblings are uniquely numbered in uninterrupted word order starting at one, and each part contains at least two directly held, regular audio files with fully numbered, non-overlapping contiguous track filenames that together form sequence 01 through N. Individually supplied part setlists, gaps, duplicate track numbering, absent common evidence, or additional unrelated music-bearing child folders MUST block this special promotion. Compliant mode is unchanged. Grouping MUST retain all original part folders and setlist content, must produce one metadata/bootlist row, and Tag Copy/Delete Original SHALL move the parent safely once using existing transfer integrity protections; it must not publish a redundant copy1 just because the tracks were split among those children. Audio tag ARTIST/ALBUMARTIST values SHALL NOT participate in the decision to aggregate folders; they remain eligible as metadata only after the physical group is fixed.

Dated show subfolders with same-show edition/part labels: In non-compliant Full Inventory, when a parent directory has a fully specified performance date and at least two music-bearing first-level child branches whose names are the exact parent show name or that name followed by terminal parenthesized copyN, altN, one/two/three, Set N, CD N, Disc N, Part N, Side N or Tape N labels, TLO SHALL aggregate all related children under that parent as one logical show. At least one child SHALL have such a suffix; every music-bearing first-level child SHALL match the same parent, and music may reside beneath recognized media, CD, Disc, or Set wrappers within those matching branches, and independently named/dated shows and unrelated branches SHALL block promotion. The parent itself SHALL NOT contain directly inventoried audio in this special case. Neither matching track numbering nor a shared setlist nor existing audio tags shall be required to infer the physical grouping; alternate copies may restart numbering. Preserve every child, all files and the existing collision and verified-transfer safeguards. Do not transfer the parent multiple times, do not add subordinate child (copyN)/(altN)/(two) labels to SHOW_NAME, and emit one inventory record and bootlist entry. A standalone folder with a suffix SHALL retain its preexisting semantics when no related sibling and dated same-name parent exist. Compliant mode remains path-only. The prior artist-tag-dependent grouping veto is superseded by this structure-only requirement; artist metadata source precedence after grouping is unchanged.

For differing-base volume-style siblings, the stripped volume names do not need to match. Example: Bob Dylan - Collection/Early Days (Vol 1) plus Bob Dylan - Collection/Latter Days (Vol 2) aggregate under Bob Dylan - Collection, with the parent as the logical inventory path.

For same-base volume-style siblings, do not aggregate. Example: Bill Dickens 1987-03-14 Great Venue NY NY (Volume 1) plus Bill Dickens 1987-03-14 Great Venue NY NY (Volume 2) are two separate inventory entries. Each row points to its own volume folder. The stripped show base is used for metadata/setlist naming, and normal size-aware setlist collision handling assigns alternates such as base.txt and base(alt1).txt when needed.

Non-date sibling collection discovery applies only during a real non-compliant Full Inventory run and only to direct sibling folder families represented by the current search path. Dry Run must not create, rename, or move a collection folder; if an interrupted prior consolidation is present, Dry Run blocks for recovery instead of changing it. A candidate shared release base must contain an Artist - Release delimiter and must not contain a complete performance date. The complete unknown-date placeholder xxxx-xx-xx (case-insensitive, with the supported date separators) is treated as a specific-date boundary for this sibling-collection rule and also excludes consolidation. A single year, year span, decade label such as 1980's, or no year remains eligible.

Recognize incrementing D, CD, Disc, Disk, Set, Part, Side, Tape, terminal parenthesized-number, and alt-number suffix families. Candidate discovery may walk upward only through the current media file's own ancestors to locate its suffixed collection child; it must not enumerate or revisit unrelated folders one level above the current search root.

All candidate collection children and their proposed parent must have the same filesystem device identifier. TLO must not search another partition for grouping or discrimination evidence, and a mixed-device family must fail closed without moving any folder.

D/CD-style numbered children are explicit multipart evidence. Numbered alt children require usable song-title evidence from discriminated setlist files or audio filenames. If two alternatives have at least 60 percent title overlap relative to the smaller distinct list, or a shifted contiguous run of at least three titles covering at least half the smaller list, treat them as similar alternatives and do not fold the later copy into the collection. Insufficient alt evidence also fails closed.

For each accepted family, create a unique hidden temporary sibling directory at the same filesystem level as the collection members, write a transaction journal naming the exact original, staged, and final paths, and move only the accepted collection members into that temporary sibling. For ordinary D/CD/Disc/Part families, preserve each member folder name. For an alt family that includes the unsuffixed base folder, never create a final Name/Name parent-child pair: stage that unsuffixed original as Name (alt0), followed by the existing alt1, alt2, and later members. Create parent info.txt by concatenating every usable member setlist in collection order. Preserve the member directories and their source setlist files inside the aggregate.

After all member moves and the generated info.txt write succeed, rename the temporary sibling directory to the exact stripped shared release name and atomically rewrite current complete-path log entries to their new aggregate paths. For an alt family, the rewritten unsuffixed member paths point to Name (alt0), so the aggregate parent keeps the normal shared release name without containing a second child of that same name. Inventory only the new aggregate parent and generated info.txt. If an independent destination exists, any move fails, or log commit fails, roll back the complete transaction to the exact original sibling names. On the next normal (non-Dry-Run) inventory, a validated interrupted journal must be rolled back before scanning.

When interrupted sibling-collection recovery cannot be completed automatically, the user-visible error must identify the recovery container, recovery journal, planned final folder when available, and every journaled member's original path, staged path, and current state (including ORIGINAL_ONLY, STAGED_ONLY, BOTH, MISSING, or a recovery-container/original-path collision). The message must explain that TLO stopped rather than guessing, advise closing programs that may hold the folders open and rerunning Inventory, and tell the user not to delete or merge the recovery container/journal manually. Dry Run remains read-only and must display the same path/state evidence while instructing the user to perform a normal inventory for automatic recovery. When a journal path was translated between Windows and WSL forms, the diagnostic must show the current-runtime path and the journal path form so the user can see why the paths differ. Automatic rollback is permitted only for a bounded recovery journal that validates structurally and carries a nonce registered under the active TLOHome/logs directory. Unregistered or oversized journals must fail closed without moving, renaming, or deleting any filesystem object. generated_info may be absent or exactly info.txt; staged/member names may not be . or ...
Confirm that the item is actually a music file, not a directory whose name happens to contain a music extension. (see Appendix E1)
Do not treat .flac, .flac16, .shn, or similar substrings in a directory name as a music file. (see Appendix E1)

The -ignoreDir rule is a hard traversal rule. Any directory or folder whose visible name ends in -ignoreDir, case-insensitively, must be disregarded before type checks, recording, scanning, grouping, placeholder setlist scanning, or recursion.
The same directory-pruning rule applies during any later scan that walks the original music folder, including generated placeholder setlist music-file scanning.

REQ-WALK-001  All collection walkers must apply the shared tlo_path_policy prune policy before descending into directories. This includes Phase 1, sibling-collection discovery, Add Shows folder scans, and every tlo-deleteDupes discovery/comparison walk. The shared exclusions include operating-system managed trash/index folders and TLO .tlo-collection-, .tlo-case-rename-, .tlo-copy-, .tlo-partial-, .tlo-restore-, and .tlo-convert- work trees so interrupted or in-progress operations are never inventoried, compared, moved, or otherwise treated as Shows.
Artist database schema is defined in Appendix G – Artist Database Schema.
Current working baseline database location is TLOHome/TLO_DBs/artists.sqlite.

Artist database and matcher caches must be bounded for long inventory runs. Repeated artist/alias lookups may be cached during a run, but distinct-query caches must have an upper bound and use an eviction policy such as LRU when that bound is reached.
If a query returns exactly one matching master name, return the master/prime name, the search term, and all aliases for that master name so they can be cached. (see Appendix E7 and Appendix G)
If a query returns more than one matching master name, record a query collision, include the colliding master names, and leave the artist blank.
Always save artists using the master name when a DB match is used.
When searching, strip articles such as the and a in any required form, case-insensitively.
Normalize single quotes before searching.

When the exact Artist DB master/alias lookup does not identify an artist, try the database's lowercase punctuation-stripped compressed-name representation (retain digits) against the entire String1 artist candidate. Accept only one unambiguous Artist DB master; if multiple masters share the same compressed key, report a collision rather than guessing. Exact master/alias lookup has precedence over compressed fallback. This applies to compliant and non-compliant inventories, Add New Shows, and Tag. For example, weather-report1975-10-07.146696.sbd.mee.flac1644 contains String1 weather-report and date 1975-10-07; weather-report compresses to weatherreport, which uniquely resolves to Weather Report if that compressed term is in artists.sqlite. The selected setlist Artist: Weather Report may independently corroborate a punctuation-compressed artist prefix directly adjacent to a complete YYYY-MM-DD, without accepting arbitrary substrings or unrelated artists.

If a potential artist candidate ends with the separate final word Band or Group, with a terminal All Star/All Stars spelling (All Star, All Stars, All-Star, All-Stars, AllStar, or AllStars; case-insensitive, with a space or dash allowed before the All-Star suffix), or with terminal All Star Band / All-Star Band (including plural All Stars Band / All-Stars Band) and the complete candidate returns no Artist DB match, retry the Artist DB lookup once after removing that terminal suffix. The complete candidate is always searched first and wins if it exists. Accept the stripped retry only when the remaining artist text resolves uniquely in the Artist DB. When it does, use the resolved DB master to identify the base artist, then restore the exact terminal suffix text that was removed and use that restored expanded name as the artist for the performance. If the resolved DB master already ends in a supported grouping suffix, do not append another suffix. Ambiguous stripped matches remain unresolved. The suffix rule applies only at the end of the potential artist name.

When the terminal-suffix fallback succeeds and the restored performance artist is not itself the full Artist DB master, mark that restored artist as not present in the database and persist it to TLOHome/artistsNotInDatabase.txt. Preserve prior file entries in their existing encounter order, append newly encountered current-run restored artist names in current-run encounter order, and de-duplicate case-insensitively. Do not alphabetically sort this review file. Do not add an unchanged DB master when the master already contains the supported suffix.

For non-compliant identification, apply artist evidence in the following order. Later tiers are fallbacks unless the structured-setlist exception below explicitly permits replacement of weak generic path evidence. Within any DB-backed tier, use the Artist DB master unless As-Is Artist Name applies.

Dates may be ranges of the form YYYY-YYYY, YY-YY, YYYY-YY, and increasing multi-part ranges such as 1996-97-98. Ranges may use only dashes or underscores; dots, spaces, slashes, and compact eight-digit forms are not range delimiters. All year-range components must increase after normalization. Ranges whose components are all explicit four-digit years, such as 1917-1939, have no span cap and are valid if each year increases left to right. Shorthand or mixed ranges that use any two-digit component remain capped at a five-year normalized span. YY-YY ranges use the normal two-digit-year pivot, and YYYY-YY continuation values expand near the first year, so 96-98 and 1996-97-98 normalize to 1996-1998. A four-digit year followed immediately by two digits, such as 200104, may be ambiguous between yyyy-mm-xx and yyyy-yyyy when the final two digits plausibly advance the year, including 1999-to-2000/2001 rollover; setlist date/range confirmation and a leading setlist collection clue resolve conflicts. Textual month-day-year forms may include a comma before the year, such as June 15, 2006, and must normalize to yyyy-mm-dd. Numeric separated dates must use one separator style consistently within the candidate; do not accept mixed separator candidates such as yyyy-mm/dd, yyyy.mm/dd, yyyy mm-dd, yyyy mm.dd, or mm/dd-yy. Whitespace around punctuation separators such as " - ", "- ", " -", and " . " is acceptable when the effective separator kind remains consistent. See Appendix E4 for exact patterns and normalization behavior.

A date may appear in any valid numeric, alphabetic, or mixed alphanumeric format. Textual month dates must continue to support no-space forms such as 14APR01, 14APRIL01, 14April01, Apr142001, and 2001APR14; dash, dot, and underscore forms such as 14-Apr-2001, 14.APR.2001, and 14_April_2001; and comma/space variants such as April 14 2001, April 14, 2001, and April 14,2001.

Support US order and European order where the date is otherwise valid. For all-numeric separated dates in paths and filenames, the delimiter must be dash, dot, underscore, or space and must not be mixed; the only mixed numeric case retained is FOUR_PLUS_FOUR_RE handling. For selected-setlist content and sampled audio DATE tags (FLAC or MP3) only, slash-delimited m/d/y and d/m/y forms are accepted with spaces around slashes allowed.
Support single-digit month, single-digit day, and two-digit year.
Support ordinal days such as 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and uppercase suffix variants such as 1ST, 2ND, 3RD, and 4TH. Do not support fully spelled-out ordinal days as ordinals.

For two-digit years, choose the most recent century interpretation that does not place the year in the future relative to the runtime current year. A two-digit year less than or equal to the runtime year's final two digits maps to the current century; larger values map to the preceding century. Complete normalized dates later than the current date are invalid; explicit four-digit future years are invalid. Partial years that do not identify a definite future date retain the established partial-date rules.
Dates may contain x placeholders or 00 placeholders.

x placeholders are valid only as a contiguous right-side suffix across the normalized yyyymmdd token. Valid forms include 2001-04-1x, 2001-04-xx, 2004-0x-xx, 202x-xx-xx, 19xx-xx-xx, 20xx-xx-xx, and xxxx-xx-xx. Century-known partial years 19xx and 20xx are legitimate only when every less-significant date component is also unknown, as in 19xx-xx-xx or 20xx-xx-xx. Broader one-digit-known years such as 1xxx and 2xxx remain invalid. Examples such as 19xx-05-xx, 20xx-xx-14, xxxx-04-14, 2001-x4-14, 2001-xx-14, and 2001-04-x4 are invalid.

Support YYYY MMDD and YYYY-MMDD through FOUR_PLUS_FOUR_RE. The space form must resolve to a valid date in US MMDD order or, when US order is invalid, European DDMM order. Ambiguous valid space values continue to prefer US MMDD. The dash form must first be checked as a possible YYYY-YYYY range; valid exact ranges remain ranges, and non-range dash values may then resolve as compact dates.

Support forms such as 1972 march 9 and include appropriate month abbreviations. Recognize complete German, French, and Italian month names, commonly used abbreviations, and German/French accentless or transliterated spellings. Examples: 01. Juni 2022, 1er juin 2022, and 1° maggio 2022 all normalize to yyyy-mm-dd. Preserve the established English and numeric date parsing and calendar validation.
If the normalized result is not a valid date, disregard the candidate date.

Compact eight-digit values are date candidates only, not date ranges, during date extraction. Compact YYYYMMDD must normalize to yyyy-mm-dd only when it forms a valid calendar date. Filename normalization has a separate exception: when an eight-digit token is not a valid YYYYMMDD date but is an increasing compact year range such as 19961998, exported setlist filename text normalizes it to 1996-1998; decreasing compact ranges such as 19981997 remain unchanged.

Audio sample-rate/bit-depth expressions are not date evidence. Values such as 44.1/16, 24/96, 16/48, 16-44, 24-96, or similar source-format references must be ignored during date extraction even when found in the selected setlist text, path text, music filename, or generated-setlist filename fallback text.

In non-compliant mode only, before applying the deferred audio-tag fallback tier, sample tags from up to two supported tagged audio files (FLAC or MP3) regardless of Performance Mode. Unsupported audio formats are skipped while selecting those samples. In compliant mode, do not read, carry forward, log, or use sampled FLAC/MP3 metadata tags. (see Appendix E1 and Appendix E7)
Check ARTIST and ALBUMARTIST.

In non-compliant mode, evaluate populated ARTIST/ALBUMARTIST values against the Artist DB before applying generic unknown/track noise rejection. A value that resolves unambiguously in the Artist DB remains valid artist evidence even when its legitimate artist name contains words such as Unknown or Track. Only after the Artist DB does not identify the value may the established generic unknown/track marker rule treat it as blank; the metadata log must show an ignored artist-tag field as blank and path-based artist detection may continue.

A usable populated sampled-audio tag artist that resolves unambiguously in the Artist DB is a DB-backed artist candidate in the audio-tag tier defined by Section 4.1; it does not bypass stronger artist evidence. Before lookup, separate an explicitly dash-delimited or parenthesized terminal performance qualifier such as Early Show or Late Show from the tag artist candidate. If the normal exact lookup misses, TLO may retry after removing apostrophe characters from the candidate and Artist DB aliases; accept that retry only when exactly one master matches. Store the DB master name (or the cleaned As-Is artist spelling when that option is selected) when this audio-tag tier supplies the final artist.

If both ARTIST and ALBUMARTIST are populated and equal, or one is a substring of the other, use the longest populated value as the candidate tag artist; if only the shorter value resolves in the Artist DB, use the shorter value's master name.
If both ARTIST and ALBUMARTIST are populated but neither is a substring of the other, look up both values. If both resolve to the same master name, use that master name.
If both ARTIST and ALBUMARTIST are populated but do not resolve to the same master name, and ALBUMARTIST contains various case-insensitively, set the artist to Various Artists.

Within the sampled-audio tag evidence tier (FLAC or MP3), ALBUMARTIST wins over ARTIST. If both are populated and disagree after the normal blank/noise checks, consider usable ALBUMARTIST values before ARTIST values. This preference does not raise audio-tag evidence above /slam, strong path/folder/commercial evidence, structured selected-setlist Artist metadata, or selected-setlist-filename evidence.
If only one of ARTIST or ALBUMARTIST is populated, use that value as the candidate tag artist.
If the candidate tag artist matches the Artist DB, store the DB master name.

If the candidate tag artist does not match the Artist DB, do not immediately make it the show artist. Defer the normalized raw tag value while DB-backed path artist evidence and explicit selected-setlist artist metadata are checked. If neither identifies an artist, use the deferred raw tag artist as the last-resort fallback and record observations for both the deferral and fallback.

When sampled ARTIST/ALBUMARTIST values do not resolve in the Artist DB, reject values that are plainly metadata noise rather than artists, including numeric-only track identifiers such as 01 or 02 and date-like values such as 1976-05. Do not defer those rejected values as raw-artist fallbacks. Continue checking the remaining sampled ARTIST/ALBUMARTIST values. A numeric or date-like-looking value that does resolve unambiguously in the Artist DB remains a valid artist, so legitimate DB-backed numeric artist names are not suppressed.

The sampled-tag search must not allow the first populated tag value to monopolize artist resolution. Reject numeric/date-like or otherwise unusable values and continue through later samples. Within the low-priority tag tier, evaluate ALBUMARTIST candidates before ARTIST candidates.
In non-compliant mode only, after artist tags, always check the music file DATE tag regardless of Performance Mode. In compliant mode, do not read, carry forward, log, or use the music file DATE tag.
If the tag exists and is populated, retrieve the string and check whether it is a valid date.
If valid, normalize it and keep it as the potential show date.
Assume many shows have an artist name, artist abbreviation, and date in the path.
Common patterns are String1 Date String2 and String1 Date; String1 Date String2 is preferred because it usually contains most desired metadata.

MAIN_DIR_PATH is the logical owning/root directory for a show group. It is normally the directory that contains the music files, but validated wrapper, multipart, collection, and String1 - String2 aggregation rules may intentionally promote a common parent or logical release directory to MAIN_DIR_PATH. MUSIC_DIRS identifies the actual directories that contain the group's music files. Metadata extraction must use the logical MAIN_DIR_PATH together with the group MUSIC_DIRS under the specific precedence/aggregation rules in this section; it must not assume that the logical root and every music-bearing directory are always the same path.

During metadata extraction, ignore path components that are themselves wrapper/non-main directories, exact wrapper names, or four-digit wrapper folders. Do not discard an otherwise meaningful show/release component merely because it contains wrapper terminology such as FM Broadcast, Soundboard, FLAC, Audio, or Video. The broader wrapper-term containment patterns in Appendix E2 remain available for wrapper/setlist relationship logic but must not suppress Artist/Date parsing of a meaningful component.

Example: Firefall 1976-05-xx Cleveland FM Broadcast is a metadata-bearing show-folder component and must remain eligible for String1 Date String2 parsing; a standalone folder named FM Broadcast remains an exact wrapper.
Any directory name that is a four-digit number is also a wrapper.
Examples include music, tunes, flacs, D1, CD1, and Set1, but the code-derived patterns in Appendix E2 are authoritative.

Before cleaning a candidate path component for String1 Date String2 analysis, capture every trailing parenthetical item from the original folder name in left-to-right order. Then strip those items and trailing whitespace for artist, date, venue, and location parsing. The captured items must remain available in PARENTHETICALS for final show-name construction.
Start at the end of the path and work backwards.
Skip wrapper directories.
If the artist is not already identified and there is one pattern match, extract String1.
Strip leading/trailing whitespace, leading/trailing dashes, leading the, leading A, trailing , a, trailing ,A, trailing , the, and trailing ,the.
Article stripping must be case-insensitive for a and the.
Search the Artist DB for the stripped value. If matched, record the master value as the artist.
If there is more than one String1 Date String2 pattern match in the overall path, search the Artist DB for each String1 and compare results.
If all String1 values resolve to the same artist, confirm that artist.
If they resolve to different artists, record an artist conflict, mark the path unresolved, and leave the artist blank.

For non-compliant DB-backed path-artist fallback, exact whole-component lookup remains the first test. If an exact component does not resolve, also try a simple Last, First reversal for a component containing one comma, so Ellington, Duke may resolve as Duke Ellington.

If exact and Last, First reversal do not resolve the component, search the component for the longest Artist-DB-backed artist phrase. This permits a descriptive folder such as Duke Ellington, Unissued recordings by Danish Radio 1957-70 to identify Duke Ellington without treating arbitrary unmatched substrings as artists. Artist collisions discovered by these DB-backed path checks must retain the normal conflict behavior.

In non-compliant mode, a short String1 directly adjacent to the date with no whitespace is weak artist-abbreviation evidence, not a primary artist identification. This includes the short prefixes commonly mirrored at the front of traded-music filenames, such as gd in gd1977-05-08....

The path component containing the String1Date or String1DateString2 abbreviation match must be excluded both from the pre-abbreviation path-artist check and from the ordinary subdirectory artist scan so the same short prefix cannot be rediscovered and promoted as independent path evidence.

Do not immediately resolve the short prefix as the artist. Allow stronger artist sources to complete first, including a usable DB-backed audio ARTIST/ALBUMARTIST tag, a full DB-backed artist elsewhere in the path, non-abbreviation path-pattern evidence, explicit selected-setlist artist metadata, DB-backed selected-setlist filename evidence, a usable deferred raw artist tag, and other structured artist fallbacks.

If stronger artist evidence identifies exactly one artist, use that artist and do not use the abbreviation. If stronger path evidence produces an incompatible artist collision/conflict, leave the artist unresolved and do not allow the abbreviation to override the conflict.

Only after the stronger local artist sources are exhausted may String1 be considered as the abbreviation fallback, and only if it has no internal whitespace, contains only alphabetic characters, is four characters or fewer, and is not mixed case.

For the final abbreviation fallback, search the Artist DB alias terms for String1. A short abbreviation prefix from a music filename is not itself promoted as a stronger artist source; music filenames remain available for date fallback according to the filename-date rules.
If the abbreviation resolves to exactly one master artist, use that master only as the final local artist fallback and record the evidence as low-confidence last-resort abbreviation evidence.
If the abbreviation resolves to multiple artists, record an artist collision and leave artist blank. If it does not resolve, leave artist identification to the normal unresolved-show behavior.

After selecting a last-resort abbreviation, if an exact yyyy-mm-dd date is available and eTreeDB and/or setlist.fm lookup is enabled, attempt the enabled artist/date lookup. A successful performance lookup is additional confirmation of the abbreviation and must be recorded in observations.

If no stronger local evidence or enabled online lookup confirms the abbreviation, the fallback artist may remain in use, but observations must explicitly state that the last-resort abbreviation remained unconfirmed.
Compliant mode uses the existing compliant path-pattern rules and is not changed by this non-compliant weak-abbreviation timing rule.
For each cached artist, store master name, abbreviations, and aliases.
Search order should be last artist match, then cache, then Artist DB.
The Artist DB is assumed immutable while the application is running; artist-cache correctness depends on no external edits to artists.sqlite during an active run.
Extract dates from path components using the same date rules.
If more than one date appears in different path components, normalize each date and compare normalized values.
If normalized dates differ, record a date conflict, save original date strings and normalized versions, and leave the show date blank.
If normalized dates agree, set the show date to the normalized date.
If a potential show date came from the music DATE tag, compare it with the path-derived date and apply the same conflict rules.
Treat String2 as a combination of venue and location.
Strip parenthetical items from the end of String2, cache all stripped parenthetical items in their original left-to-right order, then strip trailing whitespace.

Save all captured parentheticals as a single string in the metadata field PARENTHETICALS, separated by one space and preserved in their original order. Merge folder-, String2-, and lookup-derived items without duplicate parenthetical groups.
Search the end of stripped String2 for a valid country name or country alias from Appendix E5.

If a country is found, first check whether the text immediately before the country contains a state, province, or region anchor. For U.S. country aliases, city + state + country forms such as Austin Texas USA, Austin, Texas U.S., Marina Del Rey, California USA, and New York, New York U.S.A. must normalize to City + StateCode, with USA not printed in the show name.
The venue is whatever remains before the city.

For non-U.S. countries, city + region/province + country forms should be parsed when the region/province is explicit, especially comma-separated forms such as Sydney, New South Wales Australia or Melbourne, Victoria Australia. Canadian postal region abbreviations AB, BC, MB, NB, NL, NS, NT, NU, ON, PE, QC, SK, and YT are built-in location anchors, as are their full province/territory names. Newly inferred Canadian two-letter abbreviations are case-sensitive and must be uppercase so ordinary words such as on are not reinterpreted as Ontario. Store Canada as the country when the Canadian code/name is unambiguous or when Canada is explicit; NT remains a recognized region code but does not by itself infer a country because NT is also used for Australia's Northern Territory. If no region/province is present, continue to treat the text immediately before the country as the city.
If the venue appears to end with the first part of a multi-part city name, move that trailing venue word or phrase to the beginning of the city.
The authoritative multi-part city prefix list is Appendix E5. Section 7.10 must not maintain a separate inline list that can drift from the code-derived Appendix E5 list.
If no country is found, search for U.S. state abbreviations and full U.S. state names from Appendix E5.

Search two-letter state abbreviations first when present, then search full state names and longer state aliases. When a two-letter U.S. state code is also an ordinary/common short word, uppercase remains the default for newly inferred free-form path/String2 text: IN means Indiana but mixed/title-case in/In does not; OR means Oregon but or/Or does not; ME means Maine but me/Me does not. The guarded common/noisy U.S. set is CO, DE, HI, ID, IN, LA, MA, ME, MO, OH, OK, OR, and PA. One path-only exception applies: an exact lowercase code may be accepted when the entire path-derived location fragment is consistently lowercase and the additional structure/noise safeguards are satisfied; common/word-like codes require a comma immediately before the code or both a venue and city. Mixed-case fragments and selected-setlist/free-form metadata do not receive this relaxation. Non-common U.S. postal codes retain existing compatibility behavior. Full state names and longer aliases may be matched case-insensitively.

A recognized U.S. state or Canadian province/territory code or full region name must appear at the very end of String2, or immediately before a trailing source/recording tail separated by whitespace, comma, or dash, to count as a state/location match. Newly inferred Canadian two-letter codes and common/noisy U.S. codes are uppercase by default; the only lowercase exception is the guarded, consistently-lowercase non-compliant path-derived location rule in the preceding paragraph. Selected-setlist/free-form metadata remains uppercase-only for these codes.

If found, normalize the region to its two-letter code and treat it like a country/location anchor: city immediately before the region and venue before the city. U.S. state codes keep the existing U.S. location behavior. Canadian codes retain the province/territory code in Region and infer Country=Canada when unambiguous or explicitly supplied. When the left side is a short location-only phrase before a full region name, keep that phrase as city and leave venue blank.
If no state is found in an allowed state-anchor position, leave venue and location blank.
Special case NYC or nyc: City is New York, State is NY, and Venue immediately precedes NYC.
Special case NOLA or nola: City is New Orleans, State is LA, and Venue immediately precedes NOLA.
A trailing LA state abbreviation must remain Louisiana. Do not convert LA to Los Angeles while detecting state/region values.

When a valid state anchor is immediately followed by an allowed trailing source/recording/descriptor tail, preserve the text after the state as one PARENTHETICAL after stripping leading whitespace, commas, and dashes. A two-letter code in this non-terminal position must be uppercase in the source text; ordinary title/prose words such as In must not be interpreted as IN. Full state names/long aliases remain case-insensitive. If the text before the state cannot produce a valid city/venue split, reject the state-tail interpretation rather than returning a state alone.
If the artist has not been identified and String1 Date String2 is not found, retry with String1 Date.
In this case, venue and location are blank.
Perform this second check while each subdirectory is still in hand, but do not stop searching for the original String1 Date String2 pattern until all subdirectories have been processed.
If a retry match is found, keep note of it for later use.

If neither String1 Date String2 nor String1 Date matches a subdirectory, and the subdirectory is not a pure number, a single character, or a wrapper directory, look it up in the Artist DB. For a date-bearing path component, generic partial artist scanning must reject a DB artist phrase found entirely inside the parsed venue, city, region, or country tail. Thus Attic inside Eddie's Attic is venue text, while an exact path component named Attic remains eligible as an artist directory.
Before generic partial-artist scanning, recognize the non-compliant Date Artist Venue Location path pattern when the date begins the path component.

The Artist must be the longest unique Artist DB match anchored immediately after the leading date. An Artist DB term found later in the component is not eligible for this pattern, and an ambiguous Artist DB result must remain unresolved.

After removing the matched Artist, parse only the remainder as String2. A venue must remain after removing the Artist, and the remainder must also parse into City plus Region or Country; otherwise reject the pattern and continue with the ordinary evidence process.

Example: 1997-04-05 Genesis Old Pub London England resolves to Artist Genesis, Date 1997-04-05, Venue Old Pub, and Location London, England. In contrast, 1990-07-10 Palace Melbourne Australia must not use this pattern because removing Palace leaves only City and Country and no venue.
If matched, set the artist to the master name.
When walking back up the tree, compare each subdirectory artist match with any artist identified from String1 Date String2.
It is acceptable if the subdirectory artist match is a subset of the previously identified artist.
If names do not have a set/subset relationship, mark the show as in conflict and leave the artist blank.
A longer matching term outweighs a shorter matching term. No voting/tally mechanism is used to override that ordered matching rule.

After the ordinary String1 Date String2 artist lookup and the Date Artist Venue Location pattern have had their normal opportunity to resolve the path, non-compliant mode may recognize a narrowly gated Artist + Place + Date + TechnicalSuffix component. This fallback exists for traded-show folders such as RTF Paris 7 March 76 flac16 and Todd Snider Skipper's Smokehouse, Tampa, FL 2005-04-16 sdb, and must not broaden or replace the ordinary String1 Date String2 parser. This guarded fallback is non-compliant only; Compliant mode is unchanged.

In non-compliant Inventory, Add New Shows, and Tag, the ordinary String1 Date String2 rule must not mistake a confirmed Artist Venue City Date [source note] folder for a larger artist name, or treat the post-date collector/taper note as String2. A selected local setlist may confirm this fallback only when its artist matches the complete leading folder tokens, it supplies exactly one date agreeing with the folder ISO date, and it identifies a distinct venue term followed by the named city in the pre-date folder remainder. The selected setlist then supplies the venue, city and region; artist output still honors Artist DB master/alias preferences and unknown artists are logged. Conflicting artist/date/place evidence must not trigger this fallback. Separately, when String2 is absent, a unique Artist DB prefix plus a pre-date venue/city/region parsed using existing location rules may establish the show without a setlist. Otherwise do not guess where the artist or venue ends. Example: NRBQ The Stephen Talkhouse Miami Beach 1994-12-10 Dolphinsmile Master with a setlist headed NRBQ 12/10/1994 and The Talkhouse, Miami, FL becomes NRBQ 1994-12-10 The Talkhouse Miami, FL.

The Artist portion must be a direct, unique Artist DB match for a prefix at the beginning of the same path component. Alias/abbreviation terms already present in artists.sqlite are eligible. TLO must not construct, infer, or guess an initialism from another artist name. If RTF is not represented in the Artist DB, this fallback does not manufacture Return to Forever from those initials.

The Date must be recognized by the existing date parser. Text after the Date must be fully accounted for by existing recognized metadata: either media/source technical tokens such as flac, flac16, flac24, shn, wav, 16-bit, 24-bit, SBD, AUD, FM, matrix, soundboard, or audience, or one existing terminal performance qualifier such as Set 1, Early Show, Late Show, Soundcheck, or Rehearsal. The literal SDB spelling is accepted only inside this guarded fallback as a compatibility spelling of a source/technical tail; it does not create or alter qualifier metadata. Ordinary title text after the Date does not activate this fallback.

Text between the DB-backed Artist and Date is a venue/location hint, not automatically authoritative metadata. Existing structured String2 parsing may immediately use state/country-anchored venue/location text, and an exact venues.sqlite or the legacy venues.txt match may be used as Venue. Otherwise only a single unanchored word may be retained as a low-confidence final location-text fallback, and only after eTreeDB, selected setlist metadata, and setlist.fm have all failed to provide stronger venue/location data. Unknown multi-word text must not be promoted to venue/location metadata. The fallback is all-or-nothing: if its Artist prefix or recognized post-date tail gate fails, it must not partially overwrite Artist, Venue, Location, Date, or Qualifier fields.

Examples: with RTF present as an Artist DB alias for Return to Forever, RTF Paris 7 March 76 flac16 resolves Artist Return to Forever and Date 1976-03-07. Todd Snider Skipper's Smokehouse, Tampa, FL 2005-04-16 sdb resolves Artist Todd Snider, Date 2005-04-16, Venue Skipper's Smokehouse, and Location Tampa, FL when Todd Snider is a direct unique Artist DB prefix match. A tail such as Set 1 is handled by the existing qualifier machinery. If stronger eTreeDB or selected-setlist venue/location metadata exists, that stronger metadata retains precedence.

Non-compliant Artist, City Date parsing SHALL require city confirmation from the built-in city vocabulary or TLOHome/TLO_DBs/cities.sqlite. A capitalized word alone is NOT city evidence. Recording descriptors such as Soundboard, Matrix, Rehearsals, Bootleg, Encore and Remaster SHALL NOT become cities without city-reference evidence. A comma-inverted Artist DB alias (including Kinks, The and Band, The) SHALL NOT be treated as an Artist, City prefix. Jethro Tull, Derby 2007-02-04 SHALL remain supported without an invented venue or state.
If neither String1 Date String2 nor String1 Date matches, search all path subdirectories for a date.
If one date is found, use it as the show date.
If more than one date is found, normalize all dates before comparison. If they disagree, mark the show as having a date conflict.
Not finding the date elsewhere should be recorded as an observation, not a conflict.

If a date still has not been found, check music filenames for a date using all the same date patterns. Phase 1 is not required to log every music filename for this check; later stages may rescan the already-identified music directory when filename-date evidence is needed.

Music-filename dates must preserve the full recognized precision. A complete compact filename date such as 19981003 or 20020810 is normalized to 1998-10-03 or 2002-08-10 and must not be downgraded to yyyy-mm-xx merely because it came from a music filename.
If found, normalize complete filename dates to yyyy-mm-dd and partial filename dates to the appropriate yyyy-mm-xx or yyyy-xx-xx form, then save the normalized value as the date.

When multiple date candidates are identified in non-compliant mode, prefer a complete yyyy-mm-dd date over less-specified date candidates such as yyyy-mm-xx, yyyy-xx-xx, or month-year text such as November2020.

If exactly one complete date remains after normalization, use that complete date and ignore less-specified date candidates, even when both the complete date and the less-specified date appear in the path.
Example: if both 1997-11-05 and November2020 / 2020-11-xx are found, use 1997-11-05 and do not mark a date conflict.

If multiple complete dates or otherwise incompatible date candidates remain, treat that as a perceived date conflict and check the selected setlist file contents for a valid date before leaving the show in date conflict.

If a setlist-derived date validates exactly one of the conflicting candidates, use the most specific validated date, clear that date conflict, and record an observation explaining that the conflict was resolved from setlist contents.
If setlist-derived date evidence validates none of the conflicting candidates, or validates more than one incompatible candidate, retain the date conflict and leave the date blank.

If the existing non-compliant date methods do not produce any usable date and no unresolved date conflict remains, check only the selected setlist file metadata/header area for a valid date using the same date patterns. The setlist-date fallback must stop before the first true track-list line, checksum/hash line, or checksum/log section. It must not scan dates from song titles, lineage, verification logs, ffp/md5/st5/sfv/hash sections, or text after those boundaries.

When the selected setlist contains complete date evidence in an explicit metadata line, such as DATE: or VENUE:, and the only path/filename date candidate is a compatible year range, use the complete selected-setlist date instead of the range and record an observation explaining the override.

For setlist-date fallback and date-conflict validation, rank date evidence by context: explicit DATE: and VENUE: metadata lines first, concise header-like metadata lines next, and long prose/commentary paragraphs last. Broad collection or series ranges found in prose are only low-confidence range clues unless no better evidence exists.

For explicit VENUE: lines, scan the performance side before Air date, aired, broadcast, simulcast, or similar labels as date evidence. Dates after those broadcast labels are air/broadcast dates and must not be used as performance dates.
Do not use the setlist filename or setlist path as date metadata input for date conflict validation or setlist date fallback.

For aggregated groups with multiple source setlist files, collect one leading-content date candidate from each unique source setlist file and apply the same validation and conflict rules across those candidates.
If exactly one normalized setlist-derived fallback date remains, use it as the show date and record date evidence with a setlist_file source.
Failure to match String Date String or String Date should be recorded as an observation, not a conflict.
This failure must not prevent show-name creation if artist and date rules otherwise allow it.
If an artist name is found in the path, use it.
If different artist master names are found, record an artist conflict, do not populate the artist, and do not create a show name.
If date is blank and there is no date conflict, set Date to xxxx-xx-xx.
If an artist is identified and the date is non-blank, create the show name.
If a show has not yet been identified, check for Date String3.
If a valid date is found, normalize String3 using the usual rules for whitespace, the, a, and other standard normalization.
Check String3 against the Artist DB. If matched, record the master name as the artist and the identified date as the date.

If String1 Date String2 is not found, check path subdirectories for String1 - String2 before treating String1 Date as the controlling fallback. Artist/Album separator may omit spaces on either or both sides only when the complete left side resolves uniquely in the Artist DB; split that first DB-confirmed dash only, preserve every later dash in String2, and do not relax unknown or ambiguous left sides. Example: Van Morrison-Saint Dominic's Preview-Hard Nose The Highway Live retains the second dash inside String2.

Generic String1 - String2 is a fallback, not an immediate commercial-release conclusion. Preserve the explicit leading-year Artist - Album commercial-release form, but otherwise inspect String2 for a complete performance date, a supported partial date at a clear beginning/end boundary, and conservative state/country-anchored venue/location evidence before storing ALBUM_NAME. A partial date embedded inside album-like middle text remains insufficient to force performance mode.
Normalize String1 using the usual rules for whitespace, the, a, and other standard normalization.
Check String1 against the Artist DB. If matched, record the master name as the artist.

If String1 does not match the Artist DB and does not collide with multiple DB artists, check the rest of the subdirectories in the path for a valid Artist DB match before assuming String1 as the artist.
If a valid artist is found elsewhere in the path, use that DB master artist for the show and record an observation/evidence entry that the artist came from another path subdirectory.
If no valid artist is found anywhere else in the path, use String1 as the artist and record an observation/evidence entry that the artist was assumed from String1.
If String1 collides with multiple Artist DB masters, record an artist conflict, leave artist blank, and do not create the show name from this fallback.

For an ordinary non-compliant String1 - String2 match, inspect String2 before using the album fallback. First extract a complete valid performance date when present. Also accept a supported normalized partial date when it occurs at the beginning or end of String2; partial dates embedded in the middle of album-like text must not trigger performance mode. After removing the accepted date, trim the surrounding dash separators and apply the conservative String2 venue/location parser. A state/country-anchored location with no unexplained trailing text is strong enough to establish venue/location evidence. If an accepted date or strong venue/location evidence is found, continue normal performance metadata processing and do not enter album mode. Example: Ray Price - Gilley's - Pasadena, Texas - xx-xx-81 must normalize Date to 1981-xx-xx, resolve Venue Gilley's and Location Pasadena, TX, and build Show Ray Price 1981-xx-xx Gilley's Pasadena, TX rather than treating the entire tail as an album title. Only when no such performance evidence is found may String2 be stored as ALBUM_NAME under the generic Artist - Album fallback.

Commercial-release year form: in non-compliant mode, recognize only a leading four-digit 19xx or 20xx year that is either enclosed in parentheses or is the complete first dash-delimited component, followed by Artist - Album. Examples: (1991) - Rod Stewart - Vagabond Heart and 1995 - Rod Stewart - A Spanner In The Works. The release year is classification evidence only: do not assign it to DATE and do not include it in SHOW_NAME. Resolve the middle Artist component normally and use only the Album component as ALBUM_NAME.

The commercial-release year rule must not accept complete or partial dates, year ranges, two-digit years, x-filled years, or a four-digit year embedded inside another component. Examples that are not commercial-release year forms include 1991-06-29 - Artist - Album, (1991-06-29) - Artist - Album, 1991-1998 - Artist - Album, and Album 1991 - Artist - Tail.

For any non-compliant String1 - String2 album fallback, if the album tail begins with an exact repeat of the resolved Artist followed by the dash separator, remove that one redundant Artist component before storing ALBUM_NAME and building SHOW_NAME. Matching is case-insensitive and whitespace-normalized, and must remove only a complete leading Artist component. Example: resolved Artist Rod Stewart plus String2 Rod Stewart - Camouflage produces ALBUM_NAME Camouflage and SHOW_NAME Rod Stewart - Camouflage.

If String2 is date-like and consumes the full String2 value, such as Artist - 2010-08-01, Artist - 20100801, or equivalent valid separated/compact date text, treat String2 as the show date rather than as ALBUM_NAME. Normalize the date and continue normal non-compliant metadata processing, including selected-setlist explicit label extraction. Do not assign xxxx-xx-xx merely because a true album-style String1 - String2 fallback has no date.

When the non-compliant group was formed from exact wrapper part folders under a String1 - String2 parent directory, use the parent String1 - String2 directory as the logical release name. Example: Jayhawks - Big Release/CD1, /CD2, and /CD3 resolve to one show named Jayhawks - Big Release.

When the non-compliant group was formed from wrapper-suffixed part folders, use the stripped folder base as the album name. Before using a raw parent name, search the rest of the path for a valid Artist DB match. Example: Marcus, Jay/Big Release CD 1, /Big Release CD 2, and /Big Release CD 3 resolve to one show named Jay Marcus - Big Release when Marcus, Jay resolves to the DB master Jay Marcus.

For aggregated wrapper-part album records, String2/the stripped release base continues to be treated as ALBUM_NAME. It is not parsed, validated, or split into venue/location fields, and no date is assigned merely because the aggregation has no date. The same ALBUM_NAME rule applies to Parent/Parent (1)..Parent (N) multipart-release aggregation.

If an aggregated wrapper-part group has more than one source setlist file, postprocess must concatenate the unique setlist texts into one generated setlist file for the single bootlist entry. Duplicate setlist texts must be written only once.
The show name is Artist - Album Name, with any trailing parentheticals preserved in their original order.

If a non-compliant String1 - String2 album fallback later receives better structured performance metadata from selected setlist metadata, selected setlist date fallback, DATE tags, music filenames, or other structured parsing, rebuild the show name from Artist + Date + Venue + Location rather than keeping the earlier Artist - Album Name fallback. This keeps SHOW_NAME, bootlist.csv, and the generated setlist filename aligned. A dash-album fallback remains valid only when no stronger performance date/venue/location metadata has been established.
The canonical venue/location source precedence and non-overwrite rules are defined in Section 9. This subsection defines only how selected setlist contents are examined within that sequence.

This check applies only to non-compliant mode. Compliant mode continues to ignore sampled FLAC/MP3 metadata tags and does not use this setlist metadata check unless a future requirement says otherwise.

The setlist metadata check uses the selected setlist file for the show group. The setlist file contents remain the source for normal Artist/Venue/Location metadata parsing. The selected setlist filename/path must not be used as date, venue, city, region, country, or location metadata input. As an artist-only fallback in non-compliant mode, when no DB-backed path artist and no explicit setlist-content artist has been identified, search the selected setlist filename (basename without extensions) for the longest unambiguous Artist-DB-backed artist phrase before falling back to an unmatched raw audio ARTIST tag.

Selected-setlist-filename artist evidence is lower priority than DB-backed path artist evidence and explicit selected-setlist-content Artist metadata, but higher priority than a deferred unmatched raw ARTIST/ALBUMARTIST tag. Record filename-derived artist evidence with a setlist_filename source and do not use filename text to infer any non-artist metadata field.

Before applying setlist header metadata rules, skip leading false-header commentary/noise. False headers may be decorated with asterisks or rule characters, but they may also be ordinary prose about the recording, upload, lineage, sharing notes, or similar commentary. If the first nonblank lines look like sentences, skip them until the first plausible metadata line. A line with only one or a few words is more likely to be the artist/header start than a preceding sentence-like commentary line.

After false-header trimming and before general artist/venue/location inference, the setlist metadata check must recognize explicit start-of-line labels such as Artist:, Artist -, Band:, Performer:, Venue:, Venue -, Location:, Location -, Loc:, City:, State:, Region:, Province:, Country:, Date:, and Place:. The label may have light leading decoration, such as asterisks or rule characters, but it must appear at the beginning of the logical line, not embedded inside a long sentence. Separators may be colon, equals, hyphen, en dash, or em dash with optional surrounding spaces. Label values that are long prose, recording commentary, or sentence-like descriptions must still be rejected. An explicit Artist/Band/Performer/Act label may fill a missing artist; the other explicit labels support missing venue/location parsing. If an explicit Venue label value contains a trailing location after comma-separated venue text, such as Venue: Osheaga Festival, Parc Jean-Drapeau, Montréal, QC, parse the rightmost valid city/region/country portion as location and retain the preceding comma-bearing text as the venue.

For explicit VENUE: metadata, do not reject the whole field merely because the full value contains sentence-like tails, semicolons, dates, or broadcast text. First trim broadcast/air-date/source tails and trailing date tokens, then apply prose rejection and venue/location splitting to the cleaned metadata prefix.

A VENUE: line may contain venue, location, and the performance date on the same line. Example: VENUE: Madison Square Garden, New York 23/12/72; Air date: ... must yield venue Madison Square Garden, location New York NY when support data allows it, and date 1972-12-23 as performance-date evidence.

Setlist venue/location recognition SHALL retain explicit metadata and existing positional and syntax fallbacks if a venue reference database or legacy venue list is unavailable. A complete, context-supported catalog match may assist venue recognition.

When cities.sqlite contains LA or L.A. as shorthand aliases for Los Angeles, accept those aliases only when explicit California evidence follows immediately, such as LA CA or LA, California. Otherwise, leave LA available for state/region parsing as Louisiana.

The setlist metadata check must limit artist/venue/location/date detection to the header/metadata area of the setlist contents. It must stop scanning metadata candidates when the track list starts or when a checksum/hash/log section starts. Track-list starts include punctuated track numbers such as 01., 1), and 03 -, plain track numbers such as 01 TrackTitle and 1 TrackTitle, bracketed-time forms such as 01 [08:23] TrackTitle, and file-style forms such as Track01 and d1t01. However, valid date header lines must not terminate metadata scanning merely because they look track-shaped. Track/hash/log boundaries should normally require a section label or multiple nearby track/hash lines; for very small setlist files, a single track or hash line may terminate scanning only after enough prior header evidence has been collected. Checksum/hash/log boundaries include checksum, ffp, md5, st5, sfv, verification, flac conversion, shntool, aucdtect, individual 32- to 64-character hex hash lines, and filename.ext:<hex> checksum rows for recognized audio extensions, such as 01 Highway Star.flac:81b2cf16b83390c1875f67afb2d37350. Filename.ext:<hex> checksum rows should ordinarily appear as multiple consecutive rows before they are treated as a hash/checksum section boundary.

The setlist metadata check must also recognize strict unlabeled multi-line header blocks before the metadata scan boundary, when the block has a validated structure such as Artist / Venue / Location / Date, Artist / Date / Venue / Location, or Artist / combined Venue, City, Country / Date. The first Artist line from such a validated unlabeled block is artist evidence, not merely a structural delimiter. The structured scan must remain bounded to the same header/metadata window and must not search copied headers, notes, song-title sections, hash/checksum sections, or other text after the first true track-list or checksum/hash/log boundary. The strict unlabeled-header shape also extends to allow one additional short room/hall line between Artist and the named Venue when the following Location and Date lines validate the structure. For example, Artist / Concert Hall / Kennedy Center / Washington, DC / Date must keep the first line as Artist and use Kennedy Center as Venue; Concert Hall must not shift into the artist slot.

Structured Live-at header rule: before applying the looser unlabeled Artist / Venue / Location shapes, the selected-setlist metadata parser must recognize the strong traded-setlist form Artist / Live at Venue, City, State/Region/Country, Date. Introductory prose above that pair must not shift the artist or venue slots. The trailing performance date is metadata and must be removed before splitting Venue from Location. When the structured artist contains an obvious duplicated terminal grouping word such as Group Group or Band Band, collapse only the repeated word before Artist DB resolution; a single legitimate Group or Band suffix remains unchanged. Before resolving any structured artist, separate an explicitly dash-delimited or parenthesized terminal performance qualifier, and after an exact Artist DB miss allow the same unique-only apostrophe retry defined for tag artists. A structured unlabeled artist still requires a unique Artist DB match (or an already-defined conservative collaboration resolution) before use. Once DB-confirmed, this high-confidence selected-setlist artist may replace a conflicting artist supported only by weaker generic path-pattern/subdirectory evidence. It must not displace /slam or explicit strong folder/commercial artist evidence. Structured selected-setlist Artist metadata is evaluated before selected-setlist-filename and sampled-audio-tag artist evidence, as defined by the canonical precedence in Section 4.1.

A city-list hit with no explicit state, region, country, comma/slash location context, or other strong location evidence is not sufficient by itself. For example, Nice by itself must not become Nice France when it appears as an adjective or comment fragment. Location parsing must also accept City + Region/State/Province + Country forms in setlist headers, including Marina Del Rey, California USA and comparable non-U.S. comma-separated region/country forms. Setlist header parsing must recognize short unlabeled combined venue/location lines in the form Venue, City, Country; Venue, City, State; Venue, City, State/Region, Country; and conservative Venue City Country forms where the country is known and the city can be identified as a short suffix. For example, Parc des Expos, Reims, France must resolve to Venue = Parc des Expos and Location = Reims France, and Stadthalle St. Ingbert Germany must resolve to Venue = Stadthalle and Location = St. Ingbert Germany. This combined-line split and any trailing-state/region fallback must be limited to header-like location evidence; a recognized state/region must terminate the location expression and must not be taken from inside artist/title text.

Candidate lines that look like prose, recording commentary, taper notes, or long sentence-like descriptions must not be searched for venue or location evidence. This includes long lines with sentence punctuation or recording-source terms. Venue words embedded inside such prose, such as stage inside a recording note, must not be accepted as the Venue.

Date-like tokens found in long prose, recording commentary, collection descriptions, or introductory paragraphs must be downranked compared with explicit metadata/header evidence. A paragraph saying from 1972-75 is a collection/range clue, not preferred performance-date evidence when a VENUE: or DATE: line supplies a complete date.

This header limit prevents song titles, track titles, hashes, and verification/log text from being parsed as dates or locations, such as treating HANG ON SLOOPY as city HANG and region ON, or treating She Left Me as city She Left and state ME. A two-letter state/region code found in setlist metadata must be uppercase to count as that abbreviation; full state names remain case-insensitive.
Header location lines may contain a city with a full U.S. state name, with or without a comma, such as Boca Raton,Florida or Boca Raton Florida. Normalize the region to the two-letter state code.

The setlist metadata check normally fills missing artist, venue, city, region, country, and location fields. It must also run for selected setlist files when a path matched String1 - String2, so explicit labels can fill otherwise missing venue/location fields. A narrow correction rule applies for non-compliant venue/location metadata: when an existing venue/city/region/country value is supported only by lower-confidence path_part evidence, a non-equivalent selected-setlist value with strictly higher confidence may replace that weak path value. A separate narrow artist correction applies: an artist line extracted from a strict unlabeled structured header may become or replace Artist only when it resolves uniquely in artists.sqlite. It may replace an incompatible Artist only when the current Artist is supported solely by weaker generic path/subdirectory artist scanning. It may also resolve a generic path-only artist conflict. It must not override /slam, audio-tag artist evidence, explicit String1 - String2/commercial-release artist rules, setlist-filename artist evidence, Artist DB collisions, or other stronger/non-path artist evidence. All replacements must be recorded as observations. Equivalent values may be retained and corroborated without a disagreement observation. Location-tail artist safety applies for generic path/subdirectory scanning. That safety also extends to any Artist DB phrase found wholly inside the parsed venue/location tail of a date-bearing folder and adds qualifier cleanup plus a unique apostrophe-insensitive retry for tag and structured-setlist artist candidates. The reported The Travelin' McCoury's - Early Show / Eddie's Attic / Decatur, Georgia / 11/4/2022 case must resolve Artist = The Travelin' McCourys, Date = 2022-11-04, Venue = Eddie's Attic, Location = Decatur, GA, and Qualifier = Early Show; the final Show identity must end with (Early Show). An exact artist directory named Attic remains eligible. The guarded Date Artist Venue Location path pattern also applies: the Artist must be a unique DB match anchored immediately after a leading date, and removing it must leave a complete Venue plus City and Region/Country.

If the setlist check supplies artist, venue, city, region/state, or country, add evidence entries using a setlist_metadata source and record an observation that the selected setlist file was used. Explicit artist labels must use a setlist_metadata:EXPLICIT_ARTIST_KEY source when they fill a previously missing artist. A DB-confirmed artist from a strict unlabeled structured header must use setlist_metadata:STRUCTURED_UNLABELED_ARTIST_HEADER. An unlabeled header artist that is absent from artists.sqlite or resolves to multiple Artist DB masters must not be promoted to Artist. The structured-header rule also permits a strict structured collaboration header such as Chick Corea and Herbie Hancock when the complete phrase has no single Artist DB row only if every component separated by a conservative standalone and, with, &, or + connector resolves uniquely in artists.sqlite. If any collaboration component is absent or ambiguous, the combined header contributes no artist candidate and TLO must not guess.

Required structured-header regression: a setlist beginning with commentary such as Great vintage stuff!!, followed by AL DiMeola Group GROUP and then Live at Gürzenich, Cologne, Germany, 1978-10-13, must resolve the structured artist through artists.sqlite as Al DiMeola Group, resolve Venue=Gürzenich and Location=Cologne, Germany, and must not reinterpret the commentary as Artist or the artist line as Venue. If a weaker generic path artist was already selected, the DB-confirmed structured setlist artist must replace it under the normal confidence rule.

Required strict-unlabeled-header regression: for a selected setlist beginning Kinky Friedman / Lone Star Cafe, New York, NY / Early 1980s, the structured header must identify Kinky Friedman as the DB-confirmed artist and Lone Star Cafe / New York NY as venue/location. This must remain true even if an erroneous Lone Star Cafe artist entry is still present in artists.sqlite and generic path scanning encounters it. With no exact performance date, the resulting Show Name is Kinky Friedman xxxx-xx-xx Lone Star Cafe New York, NY.

For non-compliant venue/location source order and online-lookup authority, Section 9 is canonical. Selected-setlist correction in this section is limited to replacing non-equivalent venue/city/region/country values supported solely by lower-confidence path_part evidence when selected-setlist confidence is strictly higher. eTreeDB and other stronger evidence must not be overwritten, Location must be rebuilt after an authorized correction, and Thorough Setlist Matching may gather additional setlist.fm candidates without increasing setlist.fm source authority.

Path String2 parsing must reject day/track-style numeric debris of the form numeric-token + numbered-city-prefix before a valid state/country anchor. For example, "04 05.Reidsville NC" must normalize to no venue, City=Reidsville, Region=NC; it must not produce Venue=04 or City=05.Reidsville. This cleanup is conservative and applies when the putative venue is numeric-only and the city token begins with a numeric prefix followed by period, underscore, or dash.

If no usable setlist file exists, the candidate is unreadable, NULL-filled, binary-like, checksum-only, housekeeping-only, no support data exists, or no usable artist/venue/location metadata is found, record only an observation when appropriate and continue normal non-compliant processing.

Selected setlist metadata parsing must recognize concise spaced double-dash headers when exactly one side is a strong location and the other side is a plausible venue. Both Location -- Venue and Venue -- Location are valid and run before generic venue-database substring fallback. Example: Winnipeg, MB -- CBC Winnipeg studios resolves to Venue CBC Winnipeg studios and Location Winnipeg MB when MB is supported region data.

A concise date header may carry a trailing duration separated by a spaced double dash, such as 1991-09-21 -- 51:27. The duration is annotation and must not prevent the date from remaining valid header/date evidence.

Generic venue-list fallback must exclude concise comma-separated performer/personnel lists with three or more name-like entries unless the line itself parses as a location. A one-word venue of five or fewer normalized characters must stand alone or be supplied by an explicit Venue: field before generic fallback may use it. Thus Van in Townes Van Zandt is not venue evidence, while Van by itself or Venue: Van remains valid.

For a partial one-word Artist DB match at the beginning of a selected setlist filename, a date may establish strong filename structure only when the date is the first substantive component after the artist, allowing only normal filename separators between the artist and date. Thus Prince 1984-06-07, Prince - 1984-06-07, and Prince_1984-06-07 remain valid, while Two Gentlemen 1979-10-05, Live In Boston 1999-01-01, and The Wall 1980-08-09 must not promote Two, Live, or The merely because a date appears later.

The trailing full-state/region-name location parser must reject title-like text when the putative city fragment ends in a connective/preposition and there is no comma before the region. Two Gentlemen In New York must not become Location Two Gentlemen In, NY. Real location forms such as Albany New York remain valid.

Generic String2/path parsing must refuse to use a lone connective/preposition as a city. Two Gentlemen In, NY must not become Venue Two Gentlemen / City In / Region NY. Path and setlist location parsing must use the same shared connective-word definition so their decisions cannot drift.

Compliant mode must not read sampled FLAC or MP3 metadata tags. ARTIST, ALBUMARTIST, ALBUM, and DATE tags must not be sampled, carried forward from old group logs, logged, or allowed to affect compliant-mode artist, date, venue, location, evidence, conflicts, observations, generated setlists, or show-name construction.
Extract the last subdirectory name from the main directory name.

When compliant-mode media files are video files, check the path subdirectories associated with the video group for compliant folder patterns before falling back to the leaf folder name. The pattern checks must include String1 Date String2, the String1 - String2 Date boundary refinement, String1 - String2, and String1 Date. This allows video wrapper folders such as VIDEO_TS, AUDIO_TS, BDMV, CERTIFICATE, Video, DVD, BluRay, or Blu-Ray to resolve from a parent or other path subdirectory that carries the show name.

Apply the normal compliant pattern sequence to the first matching video path subdirectory text: String1 Date String2; then, if that fails and the text is String1 - String2, inspect String2 for one complete performance date at its beginning or end; then generic String1 - String2; then String1 Date. If no matching subdirectory pattern is found and the leaf folder is a standard video wrapper folder, the immediate parent directory may still be used as the compliant fallback text. The MP3 year special case remains audio-only and applies only when its separate conditions are met.

Search for String1 Date String2 by first looking for a Date in yyyy-mm-dd form. If no yyyy-mm-dd match is present, look for an accepted year-range date. Only if those compliant-primary forms are absent may the broader historical date parser be used as a fallback.
When found, strip leading and trailing whitespace from String1 and treat the result as the candidate artist text.

Artist identification continues to use the existing Artist DB rules. As-Is Artist Name and Proper Grammar affect only the outward-facing artist spelling after identification. By default, when a discovered artist or alias matches one Artist DB entry, TLO uses the database master artist name. When As-Is Artist Name is checked, TLO preserves the artist spelling and wording from the metadata source that identified the show while still using the Artist DB to recognize aliases and resolve matches; As-Is Artist Name always overrides and suppresses Proper Grammar output conversion. When Proper Grammar is checked and As-Is Artist Name is unchecked, TLO prefers a qualifying DB alias such as Last, First or Band, The when one exists; otherwise it falls back to the same name the current master/alias logic would have produced.
If the Artist DB does not find one unambiguous master, use the artist text found in metadata and record the miss or collision as an observation rather than an unresolved reason.

TLO must not open a Master-versus-As-Is selection window or command-line prompt. The GUI uses the As-Is Artist Name checkbox, which defaults to unchecked. The CLI uses --as-is-artist-name. The hidden legacy --compliant-artist-mode master|as-is argument may remain accepted for compatibility but must not be documented in help output.
Strip parenthetical items from the end of String2, cache them in order, and save them in PARENTHETICALS.
String2 is also stored as ALBUM_NAME in compliant mode when used raw.

When --etree-lookup is false, do not parse, validate, or split String2 into venue/location fields. Use String2 exactly as found after trailing parenthetical extraction. The show name is Artist Date String2.

If String1 Date String2 is not found, check for String1 - String2. Before accepting the generic dash fallback, inspect String2 for one complete performance date at a boundary.
