When a complete date is at the end of String2, normalize it into Date and keep the remaining leading String2 text as the raw album/show/venue tail. A complete date at the beginning of String2 is already covered by the higher-precedence String1 Date String2 form when trailing String2 text exists. Bare years, year ranges, partial dates, and dates embedded in the middle of String2 must not trigger this boundary-date refinement. The same DB-gated Artist/Album spacing rule applies in compliant mode: Artist - Album, Artist- Album, Artist -Album, and Artist-Album are equivalent only after the left side uniquely identifies the artist; later dashes remain in String2.

Use the run-wide artist naming settings. As-Is Artist Name has highest precedence and preserves String1 as the output artist name. Otherwise, normalize String1 for Artist DB lookup and use the DB master name when matched; if Proper Grammar is checked, replace that outward-facing master spelling with a qualifying DB-backed Last, First or Band, The alias when one exists. If no qualifying Proper Grammar alias exists, keep the current master-name result.

For the String1 - String2 Date refinement, Date is the normalized complete boundary date and the remaining String2 text is stored as ALBUM_NAME and raw venue/show text under the same no-venue/location-parsing rule used by compliant String2. Example: The Georgia Satellites - Santa Cruz 01-17-87 resolves to Artist The Georgia Satellites, Date 1987-01-17, String2 Santa Cruz, and Show The Georgia Satellites 1987-01-17 Santa Cruz. If the boundary-date refinement does not match, generic String1 - String2 assigns no Date and String2 remains the album/show tail. Artist output still follows the run-wide As-Is Artist Name setting.
If the Artist DB does not find one unambiguous master, use String1 as the artist and record the miss or collision as an observation.

For compliant String1 - String2 Date and generic String1 - String2 cases, treat the remaining String2 as the album name. Do not parse, validate, or split String2 into venue/location fields unless eTreeDB lookup succeeds under the online lookup rules.
For String1 - String2 Date, when --etree-lookup is false, the show name is Artist Date String2. For generic String1 - String2 there is no date and the show name is Artist - String2.

For the generic String1 - String2 compliant case, there is no date. Do not assign xxxx-xx-xx for the compliant extraction record or generated setlist content. This no-date rule does not apply when the String1 - String2 Date boundary refinement supplied a complete Date.

The generated setlist text filename for generic String1 - String2 with no parsed Date must include a dash between the sanitized Artist/String1 component and the sanitized String2 component: Artist-String2. String1 - String2 Date uses the normal dated setlist filename construction from Artist + Date + Venue + Location + Parentheticals.
If String1 Date String2, String1 - String2 Date, and generic String1 - String2 are not found, check for String1 Date.
If found, String1 is the candidate artist and Date is the show date.

Use the run-wide artist naming settings. As-Is Artist Name has highest precedence and preserves String1. Otherwise use the Artist DB master when matched, then, if Proper Grammar is checked, prefer a qualifying DB-backed Last, First or Band, The alias when available. Misses and collisions fall back to String1 with an observation.
No venue or location is assigned for this pattern.
If none of the compliant patterns are found, use the folder name as the Show name.
For this fallback, Artist, Date, Venue, and Location remain blank.
The generated setlist text filename must be based on the Show name with normal setlist filename stripping.

The main GUI includes As-Is Artist Name and Proper Grammar checkboxes. Both apply to compliant and non-compliant metadata collection and both default to unchecked. Proper Grammar is positioned directly under As-Is Artist Name. The CLI surfaces tlo-gi, tlo-main, and tlo-tag expose --proper-grammar wherever their other shared artist-naming options are available; --old-grammar is not a supported compatibility spelling. As-Is Artist Name always overrides Proper Grammar.

With As-Is Artist Name unchecked and Proper Grammar unchecked, TLO uses the existing artist-name decision logic: an unambiguous Artist DB match produces the DB master name, while a miss/collision uses the discovered text and records an observation. With Proper Grammar checked, after the artist has been identified but before the Show Name is constructed, TLO looks within that artist's DB master/alias family for a Proper Grammar output spelling. Prefer an article-suffix alias such as Kinks, The when it exists. For person-style comma aliases such as Smith, John, accept the alias only when its swapped spelling corresponds to another known master/alias for the same artist; a comma alone is not sufficient, so ordinary comma-bearing artist names such as Emerson, Lake & Palmer are not reinterpreted. If no qualifying alias exists, use the ordinary current result.

With As-Is Artist Name checked, preserve the artist text from the metadata source used to identify the show, including String1 in compliant patterns, audio tags, path matches, and selected setlist metadata. The Artist DB may still be used to recognize aliases and determine that the artist is known, but Proper Grammar is ignored even when its checkbox is checked. Proper Grammar changes only output spelling and must not alter Artist DB identification, eTreeDB/setlist.fm lookup keys, source precedence, or conflict decisions. When effective, the selected Proper Grammar spelling becomes the Artist used for Show names, generated/exported setlist metadata, tags, Artist-in-Album prefixes, bootlist identity, and Rename Compliantly folder names. Collaborations may apply the preference independently to each uniquely known artist component while retaining the original connector text.

This section is the canonical definition of venue/location source precedence, usable-result criteria, lookup dependencies, and overwrite behavior. The normal order remains path, eTreeDB, selected setlist metadata, then setlist.fm. The only correction exception is the higher-confidence selected-setlist correction rule permitting a higher-confidence selected-setlist venue/location component to replace a value supported solely by weaker path_part evidence. Appendices H and I contain service-specific query, response, and throttling details and must not restate the precedence rules.

In non-compliant mode, venue/location sources are applied in this order: path-derived metadata, eTreeDB, selected setlist metadata, and setlist.fm last. In normal mode, setlist.fm is eligible only when eTreeDB did not return a usable venue/location result for the current Artist and normalized Date. Thorough Setlist Matching is the explicit exception: when enabled and setlist.fm is enabled, TLO may query setlist.fm proactively for corroboration/deconfliction even after a usable eTreeDB result, without giving setlist.fm greater overwrite authority. In compliant mode, selected setlist metadata is not used, so the same path/eTreeDB/setlist.fm ordering applies, with the same Thorough exception.

Every source after path parsing fills blank VENUE, CITY, REGION, COUNTRY, and LOCATION fields only. It must not replace nonblank path-derived, heuristic, venue-list, or selected-setlist values. Non-equivalent disagreements are observations; equivalent values and token-boundary subset/superset values are not disagreements. Captured parentheticals remain appended to the final show name.

A usable online lookup result must match the requested normalized yyyy-mm-dd Date and provide enough data to construct a location: venue and city are required; United States results also require state/stateCode, and non-United States results require country. Incomplete results are observations and do not suppress later eligible sources.

--etree-lookup, --setlistfm-lookup, and --setlistfm-upgrade all default to false. The upgrade flag is effective only when setlist.fm lookup is enabled. setlist.fm may be enabled only when eTreeDB is enabled. Command-line startup with --setlistfm-lookup but without --etree-lookup is an error; the GUI must keep the dependency visible by restoring etreeDB when necessary.

eTreeDB resolves the exact artist using artistsRoot(name eq), queries the nested Artist.performances relationship filtered by year, normalizes returned dates locally, and matches the requested yyyy-mm-dd Date. The top-level performances(...) query must not be used. Detailed eTreeDB behavior is in Appendix H.

For tagging-title fallback only, the eTreeDB match may also provide set1, set2, and set3 when local title sources are unavailable. This title fallback does not alter inventory venue/location precedence or overwrite show metadata.
Lookup failures, no matches, invalid dates, and incomplete results must be recorded as observations and processing must continue with the next eligible source while retaining existing metadata.

setlist.fm requires Artist and a normalized yyyy-mm-dd Date. Detailed request construction, result selection, show-name construction, coordination state, throttling, lock timeout, and normal and upgraded quota rules are in Appendix I.
Compliant and non-compliant processing must call the same shared online-lookup functions so lookup behavior is maintained in one implementation path.

A blank Artist does not by itself make a record unresolved when an explicit compliant fallback rule has already produced a nonblank SHOW_NAME. A record is unresolved for output purposes when SHOW_NAME is blank; then its path is added to the to-be-resolved/unidentified list under the rules below.

Maintain an overall running list of directories that do not resolve. Reasons include artist conflict, unable to identify artist, and date conflict. Missing date by itself is not unresolved when an artist is identified and no date conflict exists, except where a compliant-mode rule explicitly keeps the date blank.

TLOHome/unidentifiedShows.txt is a persistent unresolved-show review list. Preserve prior unresolved entries in their existing encounter order, append newly unresolved paths in current-run encounter order, and de-duplicate without alphabetically sorting the file. When a path that is already in the file is processed again and the current metadata record now has a resolved nonblank SHOW_NAME, remove that prior unresolved entry. If a rename occurred, ORIGINAL_MAIN_DIR_PATH is also an addressed alias for removing the stale prior entry. A path that remains unresolved in the current run must remain listed, and an old entry that was not processed in the current run must not be removed merely because it was absent from current metadata.
Append new unresolved paths in encounter order and remove duplicates without sorting. Do not alphabetically reorder either prior unresolved entries or newly appended entries.

Include a bootlist/output CSV row whenever SHOW_NAME is nonblank and the row otherwise satisfies the inventory-output rules, even when Artist is blank under an explicitly supported compliant fallback. Do not create a bootlist row for a record whose SHOW_NAME is blank.
If the show name is blank, write the MAIN_DIR_PATH to TLOHome/unidentifiedShows.txt.

Postprocess must independently scan all meta*.log metadata records for blank SHOW_NAME values before or separately from bootlist row generation. If SHOW_NAME is blank and MAIN_DIR_PATH exists, the path must be written to TLOHome/unidentifiedShows.txt even if the conflict log did not capture the unresolved condition.

Blank-show reporting must not depend solely on whether a bootlist row is created, skipped, or reconstructed during aggregation. The unidentifiedShows.txt file must represent every metadata record with a blank SHOW_NAME.
The unidentifiedShows.txt format is one path per line with no delimiters, prefixes, or suffixes.
Apply the following outcomes for missing dates, date conflicts, and unresolved handling.
Generated setlist filenames must preserve parentheses. Captured parentheticals must be included in the filename base when present.

When postprocess is invoked without a completed in-memory current-run metadata result, it may read the selected matching meta*.log files from TLOHome/logs as its source. When inventory scanning has completed and current-run metadata records have been supplied, that in-memory list is authoritative even when it is empty; postprocess must not fall back to rereading a reused historical token merely because the list contains zero records.

If the date is blank but the artist is defined and no date conflict exists, set the date to xxxx-xx-xx and establish the show name, except for compliant String1 - String2, non-compliant String1 - String2 album fallback, and compliant final folder fallback cases defined in Section 10.1.

Unknown-date descriptor fallback: when Date is exactly xxxx-xx-xx and both Venue and Location are blank, TLO may derive a separate non-geographic Descriptor so a collection/show can retain a useful identity without inventing venue/location metadata. Descriptor evidence is ranked conservatively from the selected/local setlist metadata region: explicit Title/Release/Collection/Bootleg/Event/Session/Broadcast/Program/Show/Recording/Descriptor labels first; strong broadcast/session/rehearsal/soundcheck/demo/collection/archive-style header text next; quoted or decorated release titles next; then a concise title-like header that is separated from the track list; then a descriptive setlist filename; and finally meaningful main-directory residue after removing artist/date, disc/set/part, and technical-format tokens. Header scanning must stop at the first track-list/checksum boundary. Artist-only/date-only lines, technical lineage, disc/CD/set labels, generic housekeeping names, sentence prose, and track-like rows are rejected. The automatic minimum score is 60 and the stored Descriptor is capped at 60 characters. The Descriptor must never populate Venue, City, Region, Country, or Location. When used, SHOW_NAME becomes Artist xxxx-xx-xx Descriptor (plus any established qualifier/parentheticals), metadata logs include DESCRIPTOR and DESCRIPTOR_SOURCE, and generated setlist filenames use the same descriptor. If no safe descriptor exists, retain the existing Artist xxxx-xx-xx behavior.

If a show name is established, append a space and PARENTHETICALS to the end of the show name, preserving multiple parentheticals in their original order. This is a universal finalization rule for compliant and non-compliant show-name construction, including String1 Date, String1 Date String2, String1 - String2, lookup-enriched names, Add Shows records, Dry Run output, bootlist rows, folder renames, generated setlists, and audio Album tags. Path cleanup must never discard the cached value. For example, Danny Gatton 1994-03-13 Bottom Line NYC (set 2) resolves to Danny Gatton 1994-03-13 Bottom Line New York, NY (set 2).
The aggregator must continue to work with short token metadata logs such as metaX.log.

Direct/legacy postprocess callers that have not supplied authoritative completed current-run metadata may read matching meta*.log files from TLOHome/logs. Completed inventory runs use their authoritative in-memory current-run metadata and apply the keep/replace volume/path policy to existing bootlist rows.

For every non-skipped bootlist row, postprocess must resolve an exported setlist .txt file under TLOHome/setlists. bootlist.csv must contain exactly two caret-separated data columns after the sep=^ line: column 1 is Show, and column 2 is VolumePath formatted as [Volume] Path, where Path is stored without the drive letter or WSL /mnt/<drive> prefix. The exported setlist filename remains generated and resolved under TLOHome/setlists, but bootlist.csv must not include separate Setlist, Volume, or Path columns. Deterministic volume/path replacement controls which previous rows are kept: exact or parent re-inventory replaces rows under the replaced scope, child re-inventory replaces rows under the child scope, non-overlapping same-volume paths preserve unrelated rows, and blank-label runs append without replacement. If the generated setlist filename collides with an existing TLOHome/setlists file, compare the exact bytes that would be written. A size match is only a fast precheck; reuse the existing filename only when a SHA-256 digest of the existing file matches the SHA-256 digest of the exact new output bytes. If contents differ, including equal-size different-content files, write the new file with (altN) appended to the base filename before .txt, where N is one greater than the highest existing alternate number for that base. The prior plain trailing-integer and (dupN) collision suffixes are not used for new generated setlist files. During a path-scoped re-inventory, the pre-existing rows selected by these same volume/path replacement rules form the previous-row population for the re-inventory reconciliation required by Section 1.4; later copy/delete provenance or the log token that originally created a row must not exclude a row that currently lies inside the replacement scope. When serialized for spreadsheet consumption, a cell beginning with =, +, -, @, tab, CR, or LF must be apostrophe-prefixed so spreadsheet software does not evaluate it as a formula; Escaping and unescaping must be round-trip safe, including cells whose original value already begins with one or more apostrophes; TLO must remove only the protective apostrophe that TLO itself added when reading the CSV back. Existing bootlist.csv data SHALL be decoded without lossy error suppression; undecodable input must block any rewrite, preserving the original bytes for repair.
For aggregated wrapper-part records, postprocess must export one setlist file per bootlist row using the concatenation and de-duplication rules in Section 7.19.
The aggregator must use meta*.log as an independent source for blank-show reporting (see Section 10).
All inventory log files must be written under TLOHome/logs instead of directly under TLOHome.

Maintain one append-only settings log at TLOHome/logs/runSettings.log for every started Full Inventory, Tag, Process New Shows, and Process Potential Duplicate/Upgrades action, including Dry Runs and command-line Inventory or Tag runs. The first line of each entry must identify the action, local date, and local time. The following lines must reproduce the same operation, path, main-window checkbox values, action-specific settings, performance or destination information, and original-file-change statement shown in the Review Operation confirmation window. Separate entries with a blank line. A GUI entry is appended only after the user chooses Start; choosing Go Back or closing the confirmation window must not create an entry. If the settings entry cannot be written, the operation must not start and the user must receive a readable error.
The short tokenized log names remain unchanged inside TLOHome/logs: confX.log, deadX.log, compX.log, dupsX.log, groupsX.log, metaX.log, tagsX.txt, and tageX.txt.

Each SHOW_NAME metadata entry written to meta*.log must include a per-entry switches line immediately after SHOW_IN_CONFLICT. The line starts with "Switches --" and records the effective settings for that inventory item, including Action, Compliant, As-Is Artist Name, Proper Grammar, Tag, Tag In Place, Tag Copy, Tag Copy/Delete Original, Rename Compliantly, Convert shn, Artist in Album, Delete Extra Tags, etreeDB, setlist.fm, setlist.fm Upgrade, and Thorough Setlist Matching. Example: "Switches -- Action: Full Inventory; Compliant: no; As-Is Artist Name: no; Proper Grammar: no; Tag: yes; Tag In Place: yes; Tag Copy: no; Tag Copy/Delete Original: no; Rename Compliantly: no; Convert shn: yes; Artist in Album: yes; Delete Extra Tags: no; etreeDB: yes; setlist.fm: no; setlist.fm Upgrade: no; Thorough Setlist Matching: no;". Add Shows entries use Action: Add Shows and record only settings active for that Add Shows item. Every machine-parsed TLO log entry must remain one physical line: embedded control characters in paths, tag values, online error text, observations, conflicts, and tag output are encoded before persistence. Readers of meta logs must reject a record containing duplicate single-valued identity keys instead of accepting a later overwrite.
Token allocation must check TLOHome/logs for collisions.

Ctrl-C and GUI Quit cleanup must delete only tokenized logs whose tokens were newly allocated by the interrupted run, after active workers have been asked to stop. Reused pre-existing tokens are never deleted wholesale; any run-specific appended/replacement content is handled by the established token/log reconciliation policy.
Postprocess must create TLOHome/logs/summary.log.

Postprocess must maintain TLOHome/logs/reinventoryDelta.log as an append-only diagnostic history for path-scoped re-inventory runs. Each entry must begin with a timestamp and contain the reconciliation fields defined in Section 1.4. Runs that do not replace a path scope do not add an entry.

summary.log must consolidate conflict entries from all conf*.log files in TLOHome/logs and unresolved blank-show metadata records from all meta*.log files. Conflict entries should include the source conflict-log filename, search path when known, and the conflict text. Blank-show entries should include the MAIN_DIR_PATH and the reason, including blank SHOW_NAME and, when applicable, blank ARTIST or SHOW_IN_CONFLICT=yes.
Use short anchor log filenames that do not include the search path in the filename. (see Appendix E8)

X is an alphanumeric log token; existing 0-9 and A-Z single-character token filenames remain unchanged. When these are occupied, new paths receive multi-character tokens beginning at 10, 11, etc. Token values SHALL be unique among existing logs, and reversible history SHALL be preserved.

Before starting workers, check the output directory for token collisions. Allocate unique tokens from the first 1,296 base-36 token values without reusing an existing token; reject oversized allocation requests before writing any logs. Existing one-character token names and log scopes remain compatible.

Choose token values by visible volume label. One token may represent multiple non-overlapping paths on the same visible volume. The top of each tokenized log must list one SEARCH_PATH line for each stored rootless path in that token. The visible search path format is [Volume] Path, where Volume is the normalized bracketed value or operating-system volume label, and Path excludes the drive letter or WSL /mnt/<drive> prefix. If the visible volume is blank, write SEARCH_PATH: [] with no path.
Pass the token to workers so workers access the correct log files.

Exactly one inventory-mutating run may be active for a given TLOHome at a time. TLO must enforce this with an owned cross-process lock held for the full inventory-mutating run; a second tlo-main/tlo-gi inventory against the same TLOHome must fail before tokenized logging or inventory output mutation begins. Search and unrelated read-only operations are not blocked by this inventory lock. Worker processes within the one accepted inventory run remain the supported inventory concurrency model.

REQ-LOG-594  On re-inventory of existing token logs, TLO SHALL serialize in-process access to the log and close active file streams before performing an atomic replacement; it SHALL preserve records outside the replaced search scope and reopen subsequent log writes in append mode. Logger scope transitions SHALL close obsolete file handlers. A temporary Windows WinError 5 or 32 replacement conflict MAY be retried within a bounded interval. Persistent permission failures SHALL remain visible and SHALL NOT truncate, discard, or silently skip the original log.

Put a descriptive header at the start of each log file. If a token covers multiple non-overlapping paths on the same visible volume, the header may list multiple paths; if the visible volume label is blank, the header must not include a path.
The dispatcher should know the tokenized log filenames so it can delete them during Ctrl-C or Quit cleanup when necessary.
For a single --search-path command-line run, --/slam STRING applies the slam artist to that one search path.
For a single --search-path command-line run, --/copy DIR applies Tag Copy to that one search path, using DIR as the destination parent.
For a single --search-path command-line run, --/copy-delete DIR applies Tag Copy/Delete Original to that one search path, using DIR as the destination parent.
--/copy and --/copy-delete are mutually exclusive for one --search-path. If either is supplied without --search-path, startup must report an error and exit.

Command-line and per-entry copy/copy-delete destinations must follow the same startup capacity rules whether they come from a direct Search Path entry, a .txt Search Path control file, or the separate direct-path command-line options: ordinary copy always receives exact source-size preflight, while Copy/Delete Original receives it only when source and destination are on different filesystems.
--setlistfm-lookup command-line gating and online lookup behavior are defined in Section 9; this section lists the CLI-facing options and startup validation requirements.

setlist.fm lookup uses the SETLISTFM_API_KEY environment variable and must not expose or write the API key to logs. setlist.fm Upgrade additionally requires an explicit upgrade-enable variable containing exactly the same API key value as SETLISTFM_API_KEY. The canonical variable is SETLISTFMUPGRADE_API_KEY; SETLISTFM_UPGRADE_API_KEY is also accepted. If --setlistfm-upgrade is supplied while --setlistfm-lookup is off, the upgrade flag is inert and must not cause standalone validation failure. Environment resolution uses an explicit nonblank process/session value first. On Windows, when the corresponding process value is missing or blank because a parent process has a stale environment snapshot, TLO must fall back to the current persisted User/System environment value. A persisted value must not override an explicit process/session value. Neither key value may be displayed or logged.
--compliant defaults to false.
--etree-lookup defaults to false. When true, both non-compliant and compliant modes perform an eTreeDB venue/location lookup after Artist and yyyy-mm-dd Date are identified.
--TLOHome overrides the TLOHome environment variable.
--myTLO behavior and precedence are defined in Section 2.3.
--/slam is valid only with --search-path.
Anything written to the console is blocked only when --silent is set.
Removed arguments must not be present or affect output: --verbose, --flat, --full-logs, --suppress-header, and --interval.
--performance-mode MODE is valid with gentle, balanced, fast, and extreme. CLI default is balanced.
--max-workers N is valid with N >= 0. Zero, performance-mode defaults, extreme-mode display, and parallelizable volume-group caps are defined in Section 2.10.

--tag-during-inventory is valid with no value and defaults to false. When supplied, full inventory Stage 3 tags music files in place and writes concise results to tagsN.txt/tageN.txt under TLOHome/logs. It is mutually exclusive with --tag-copy-during-inventory.

--tag-copy-during-inventory is valid with no value and defaults to false. It requires an existing fully qualified --tag-copy-destination DIR and tags copies while keeping the original source tree as the inventoried location. It is mutually exclusive with --tag-during-inventory.

--tag-copy-delete-original is a tlo-main GUI-launcher flag that enables Tag Copy/Delete Original mode without supplying a destination on the command line. When Inventory or GUI Tag starts, the GUI requests the destination and displays the deletion warning. The flag is distinct from --tag-copy-and-delete DIR, which supplies the destination directly for command-line inventory processing.
--tag-copy-and-delete DIR selects the copy/move, verify, delete-original, and tag-destination workflow. DIR must be an existing fully qualified destination and must pass the startup capacity check.

--rename-compliantly is valid independently of tagging but is mutually exclusive with --compliant. By itself during non-compliant full inventory it renames identified original folders in place without writing audio tags; with a tag/copy mode it applies the resolved show name to the corresponding source or destination.

--convert-shn is valid with no value and defaults to false. When supplied, any .shn or .shnf files encountered during Tag, Full Inventory, or Add Shows are converted to .flac. If tagging is also enabled, conversion must happen before track-title selection and tag writing. If tagging is not enabled, conversion still runs by itself and must not write or change audio metadata tags.

--as-is-artist-name preserves the artist name from the metadata source that identified the show. Without it, a matched Artist DB alias is replaced by the database master artist name. The setting applies to compliant and non-compliant processing.

Neither the inventory CLI nor tlo-main.py GUI launcher accepts --tag-path or --search-folder for GUI Tag. The --search-folder option, compatibility alias --tag-path, and positional search-folder input belong only to standalone tlo-tag.py and must not affect Full Inventory, GUI Tag, or Add Shows processing.

Shared option registry requirement: all non-carve-out inventory/tagger input options must be declared once in tlo_options.py. The registry must define the unchanged command-line flag, one canonical snake_case destination/config field name, kind, default, choices, help text, and GUI presentation metadata when applicable.

Generated parsers requirement: tlo-gi.py, tlo-main.py, and tlo-tag.py must build each application's applicable shared options from the registry rather than maintaining independent hand-written copies. TLOHome, the hidden myTLO compatibility argument, --debug [BOOL], and --/slam remain explicit carve-outs where applicable; standalone tlo-tag.py additionally owns its required search-folder input, exposed as positional SEARCH_FOLDER or --search-folder, with --tag-path retained as a compatibility alias. GUI tlo-main.py has no standalone Tag search-folder input.

Canonical naming requirement: argparse destinations for generated options must use the canonical snake_case names used by Config, such as tag_during_inventory, etree_lookup, setlistfm_lookup, performance_mode, max_workers, search_path_override, and current_storage_volume. Parser code must not translate from camelCase namespace attributes such as tagDuringInventory, etreeLookup, or setlistFM.

Lookup dependency requirement: setlist.fm requiring eTreeDB must be enforced by one shared function. Startup, CLI, and GUI surfaces must all use that same rule; Section 9 is the canonical behavior description.

Add and maintain a standalone command-line tagger named tlo-tag.py. It shares the same tagging engine and metadata/title rules as the GUI Tag action, but it remains a command-line workflow with its own required search-folder input. The preferred named form is --search-folder DIR; --tag-path DIR remains a compatibility alias, and a positional SEARCH_FOLDER is also accepted. The GUI must not open a separate Tagger child window. Clicking the main-window Tag button must use the master Path(s), including any inline --/slam directives, and current main-window options directly and must report progress/output in the main Inventory window. No duplicated main-window option checkboxes or separate inherited-settings notice may be introduced for GUI Tag because GUI Tag has no child Tag surface.

tlo-tag.py must visibly accept --TLOHome STRING, --compliant, a required search folder supplied either as --search-folder DIR or positional SEARCH_FOLDER, and the compatibility alias --tag-path DIR. It must also accept the shared tagging controls --etree-lookup, --setlistfm-lookup, --setlistfm-upgrade, --thorough-setlist-matching, --corrupt-files ACTION, --corrupt-folders POLICY, --corrupt-folder-threshold PERCENT, and --delete-extra-tags and --deep-audio-check, together with the established standalone Tag options for Rename Compliantly, Convert shn, Artist in Album, As-Is Artist Name, and debug. The setlist.fm/eTreeDB dependency and corruption-policy validation must be identical to the inventory command line. For standalone tlo-tag only, --corrupt-folders defaults to never, meaning corrupt folders are kept unless the user explicitly selects all or threshold; Full Inventory keeps its existing shared default. --delete-extra-tags and --deep-audio-check defaults off; when enabled it applies the same exact metadata-retention rule used by Inventory-time tagging. It may continue accepting --myTLO STRING as a hidden compatibility argument, but --myTLO must not appear in help output. If more than one search-folder form is supplied with different non-empty values, report a readable error and exit.
TLOHome resolution for tlo-tag.py must preserve the internal compatibility precedence defined in Section 2.3, while user-facing help documents only --TLOHome and the TLOHome environment variable.

Standalone tlo-tag must not choose TLOHome/readyForXfer or any other implicit tagging path. A search folder is required on every command-line run. If the search folder is omitted, tlo-tag must report a readable command-line error and exit before tagging begins.

When the standalone tlo-tag search folder is a Windows drive-rooted path such as P:\tagtest or P:/tagtest, and the tagger is running under WSL/Linux, the tagger must translate the path to the equivalent /mnt/<drive>/... path before validating that it is fully qualified and exists. Native Windows keeps Windows paths native. This applies to --search-folder, the compatibility alias --tag-path, and the positional SEARCH_FOLDER argument.

When writing audio tags with Delete Extra Tags disabled, TLO must preserve unrelated existing metadata except for the established cleanup of stale TRACKTOTAL, DISCNUMBER, and DISCTOTAL values. This applies to inventory-time tagging and to the standalone tlo-tag and GUI Tag. The normal TrackNo/Track Number tag remains written; only total-track and disc-position/count metadata is removed by the normal unchecked behavior. When Delete Extra Tags is enabled, the stricter four-field retention rule below supersedes that preserve-unrelated-metadata behavior.

Before saving tags to an audio file, normalize the intended Artist, Album, Title, and Track Number exactly as the writer will store them and compare them with the file's current values. If Delete Extra Tags is disabled, the existing no-op rule applies: when all four written fields already match exactly and TRACKTOTAL, DISCNUMBER, and DISCTOTAL cleanup is not required, do not call the audio tag save/write operation and report the file as unchanged. If any written field differs, has additional values that the write would replace, or any obsolete total/disc tag remains, perform the normal tag write and cleanup. If Delete Extra Tags is enabled, a file is unchanged only when those four fields already match exactly and there is no other tag metadata or tag artwork to remove. This no-op guard applies to inventory-time tagging and the standalone tlo-tag and GUI Tag and must not change title-source selection or track ordering.

When Convert shn / --convert-shn is enabled, TLO must convert SHN/SHNF files to FLAC in the selected Tag path, during Full Inventory, and during Add Shows, even when no tagging mode is enabled. Conversion must use only the application-bundled native converter included with the native build. Native release packaging prepares FFmpeg 9.0.2 from an exact versioned release asset, verifies its pinned SHA-256 before extraction, and packages the resulting executable beneath tlo_ffmpeg_bin. Runtime resolution must not honor IMAGEIO_FFMPEG_EXE, PATH, conda, imageio-ffmpeg, or a current-directory ffmpeg fallback. In frozen builds, the resolved converter must remain inside the packaged application.

Supported setlist track identifiers must include at least: 0 Name, 1 Name, 0Name, 1Name, 0-Name, 1-Name, 01-Name, 0)Name, 1)Name, 0) Name, 1) Name, Track 0 - Name, Track 1 - Name, t01: Name, t01 - Name, d1t01 Name, d1t01 - Name, cd1t04 - Name, s2t01 Name, side-letter rows such as A01 Name and B05 Name, 101 [0:26] Name, 201 [1:43] Name, and disc-track dash rows such as 1-1 Name, 1-2 Name, and 2-1 Name, and numbered encore rows such as 09. E: Name or 09. Encore: Name.

When a local numbered setlist is a strong but short run and the audio folder has additional files, inventory-time tagging may preserve the known listed titles and mark only the unmatched trailing audio files as Unknown instead of discarding the setlist titles. This partial-title behavior must remain conservative and must not override exact-count local setlist matches. Bare-number rule: when exactly one contiguous bare-number block begins at 0 or 1, continues consecutively, and its row count exactly equals the audio-file count, treat those numbers as track positions and write Title = Unknown for every row. The numeric values themselves must never be written as song titles by this rule. A count mismatch or multiple competing exact-count bare-number blocks contributes no candidate and is neutral to the remaining title-selection sources.

Comma-separated setlist fallback must support SET ONE/SET TWO style sections. Comma-separated items may include internal medley arrows such as Jam>Flute Down; these arrows must not be split unless a future rule can prove the resulting count is safe.

Numbered setlists may restart at 1 after a clear CD/Disc/Disk/Set heading, or after an established numbered run when no heading is present. The written Track Number tags must remain sequential across sections. Clear headings include roman-numeral and duration forms such as Set I - 89 min. and Set II - 99 min. When no heading is present, a reset is accepted only after the current list has ascended from 0 or 1 and the restarted section is confirmed by the next parsed row continuing to 2. Blank lines are not required and do not affect the reset decision. A lone unconfirmed second 1 must be ignored so revision notes or other prose are not written as titles.

Numbered setlist parsing must tolerate large blocks of non-song text, blank lines, URLs, personnel notes, and ordinary explanatory notes between numbered song rows when the later numbered row validly continues the established sequence or begins a confirmed reset. Terminator-style headings such as Note:, Source:, Transfer:, or Comments: must not end an otherwise valid numbered list if a later numbered row continues the expected number. Patch notes and checksum/hash sections remain hard stops.

Technical audio-analysis and extraction/ripper report sections must not be parsed as song titles. This includes auCDtect result rows and Exact Audio Copy (EAC) extraction logs/TOC tables. Rows such as "101 Ted the Mechanic.wav: track looks like CDDA with probability 100%." and "1 | 0:00.00 | 13:17.25 | 0 | 59799" are technical verification/table data even when their leading numbers form a valid 1..N sequence. Recognized EAC markers such as "Exact Audio Copy", "EAC extraction logfile", and "TOC of the extracted CD" begin a technical tail that is not mined for track titles. In addition to source-specific filters, numbered-title parsing must apply a conservative plausibility check that rejects numeric multi-column/timestamp table rows while preserving legitimate numeric song titles. If these technical rows appear after a valid setlist track list, track-title parsing stops before the technical block; if they appear without a real numbered setlist, they are ignored for title selection.

Ordinal event/header lines must not be parsed as compact numbered tracks. For example, "9th Annual Eddie Moore Jazz Festival" is a header/event line and must not become track 9 with title "th Annual Eddie Moore Jazz Festival". Track extraction must continue past such headers to later real numbered track lists.

Once a setlist track list has started, collector notes, note-to-collectors sections, lineage/source/transfer notes, comments, explicit thank-you prose such as "Thanks to the taper", checksum sections, and similar prose sections must terminate track-title parsing. A later prose sentence that starts with a number, such as "40 years...", must not be accepted as an additional song title.

If metadata cannot be identified, the standalone tagger must skip the folder with a concise console message and processing must continue with the next folder. If a selected setlist exists but no numbered parseable tracks exist, the tagger must check for unnumbered CD/Disc/Disk/Set song-list sections, then unnumbered comma-separated setlist fallback content, before falling back to filename-derived titles confirmed by the setlist text or to existing audio Title tags. If the setlist track count still does not match the number of music files, standalone/GUI tagging may use existing audio Title tags as a last-resort source when at least one existing title is usable; otherwise it skips the folder. Inventory-time tagging may also fall back to existing audio title tags according to Section 14. When an explicit Set/Disc/Disk/CD or Setlist/Tracks/Songs boundary is present, unnumbered title candidates must be constrained to the song region beginning at that boundary; header, venue, and lineage text above it is not eligible merely because including it would make the title count match the audio-file count.

Filename-derived tagging fallback must be conservative. It may use titles extracted after a leading track number, dNtNN/sNtNN token, or embedded date plus disc/track prefix only when a real title remains after the prefix. Fill-in identifiers such as Track, Track 01, d1t03, s1t04, unknown, untitled, or bare numbers are not valid song titles. When a selected setlist exists, filename-derived titles must be confirmed against the setlist text before use.

Standalone tlo-tag scans folders under its required search folder; GUI Tag scans the parsed master Path(s) jobs. Both use the same inventory discovery rules for folders with music. It must choose the selected setlist file with the same setlist-selection rules used elsewhere, parse metadata using compliant or non-compliant inventory rules, and tag all taggable audio files in each folder. FLAC and MP3 are first-class taggable formats and must use the same title/track assignment flow. When the discovery input contains only a representative media sample for a folder, the tag-write step must locally rescan the known music directory and operate on the full set of eligible audio files in that folder. In standalone tlo-tag or GUI Tag, if no setlist is found, attempt filename-derived track titles first; when filenames are generic or unusable, use existing audio Title tags when at least one usable title exists. In Tag During Inventory, if setlist/eTree titles cannot be used or the count mismatches, use existing audio Title tags as the last-resort Title source and write Unknown for empty, generic, or unusable title tags. Generic-title rule: when the complete cleaned candidate song title from any setlist title source (local numbered, local unnumbered, comma-separated, eTreeDB, or cached setlist.fm) or from an existing audio Title tag is exactly Title, Titled, or Titles, case-insensitively, TLO must keep the track row/position but write the Title value as Unknown. This rule applies only when the complete cleaned candidate is one of those three words; longer legitimate titles that merely contain title, titled, or titles remain eligible.

Numbered-setlist safety rule: A leading bare track number such as 01 must be retained as an Unknown-title track only when the next meaningful numbered song row confirms the expected sequence, such as 02 Day Waves. An isolated bare number before unrelated prose must not be manufactured into a track. A one-, two-, or three-digit numeric-only row must not start an unstructured unnumbered-title fallback block, because an isolated short number is more likely to be a bare track number. Numeric song names remain eligible when embedded inside an already-established multi-line unnumbered song block; titles such as 69 and 1999 must remain valid. Compact personnel/credit lines ending in a recognized instrument or role parenthetical, including Gary Burton(vib) and Chick Corea (p), and duration-summary lines such as min 38:24, 38:24 min, and total time 38:24 must not become unnumbered titles. When the local text contains a convincing run of at least three consecutive numbered song rows, later unnumbered prose must not be scavenged merely because its count happens to equal the audio-file count; however, the competing-candidate rule supersedes this blanket gate when a plausible exact-count unnumbered song-list candidate exists and must be compared against the numbered candidate before padding or final selection.

Explicit-setlist and disc-order rule: When a selected local text file contains an explicit Setlist:, Set List:, Songs:, Tracks:, or equivalent track-section heading followed by an unnumbered one-song-per-line list, that section must be evaluated before later numbered prose. A track-list terminator such as Notes: ends the section even when no numbered song rows were seen, so later collector notes beginning 1), 2), 3), and similar numbering must not become titles. Within an explicit/count-matched song section, a legitimate song beginning with Thank, including Thank The Nurse That's Nursing You, must remain eligible; explicit thank-you prose such as Thanks to the taper remains a terminator. Encore abbreviations E:, Enc:, and Encore: must be stripped from the beginning of the song title. Audio files whose names carry both disc/disk/CD and track tokens must sort by disc first and track second even when punctuation such as commas, periods, hyphens, underscores, or spaces separates the tokens; for example CJM-Disc01,Track01.flac through CJM-Disc01,Track10.flac must precede CJM-Disc02,Track01.flac. This ordering prevents disc 1 and disc 2 from being interleaved into odd/even written Track Number tags. The same disc-first ordering extends to a validated multipart release whose immediate music folders use the Parent (1) through Parent (N) shape. For those aggregated parts, the terminal parenthesized part number is the first ordering key and the filename track number is the second, so all files from part 1 are tagged before part 2 and so on; the written Track Number tags remain one album-wide sequential series rather than striping all track 01 files across parts.

Competing-track-list candidate rule: Before a short numbered local setlist candidate is padded with Unknown titles, TLO must evaluate any plausible local unnumbered candidate whose title count exactly equals the number of audio files. Count agreement is primary evidence: an exact-count song list outranks a shorter numbered candidate when the latter does not account for all audio tracks. When numbered and unnumbered candidates both exactly match the audio-file count, TLO may use only positive corroboration from the corresponding audio filename or existing audio Title tag to reinforce either candidate; a missing, generic, unreadable, or unrelated filename/tag value contributes zero and must never reduce a candidate score. Filename corroboration may be established either by a parsed filename title match or by the complete normalized candidate title appearing within the corresponding filename. Existing Title-tag corroboration requires a usable cleaned tag title matching the candidate title. If equally sized candidates have equal corroboration, a short numbered run demonstrably embedded in surrounding prose/collector notes may yield to the exact-count contiguous unnumbered song block; otherwise normal numbered-list precedence remains. The reported Cramps 1984-06-25 example contains three numbered processing notes followed by 17 unnumbered songs; with 17 audio files, the 17-song block must be selected from Devil With A Blue Dress On through She Said.

Explicit track-region boundary rule: When a selected local text file contains an explicit song-list boundary such as Set 1, Set 2, Disc 1, Disk 1, CD 1, Setlist 1, Set List 1, Track List 1, Songs:, Tracks:, or an equivalent numbered section heading, that boundary establishes the beginning of the unnumbered song region. Header, artist, venue, location, lineage, and other plausible short text above the first such boundary must be discarded from unnumbered title candidates and must not be used merely to make the candidate count equal the audio-file count. Subsequent Set/Disc/Disk/CD headings and a bare Encore heading are continuation boundaries and retain the ordered titles already collected. Blank lines may separate title blocks inside the explicit region. A date-labelled divider such as on July 7, 1967: inside that region is a non-title continuation/filler divider; following plausible titles remain eligible and the divider itself is not tagged. Notes/source/checksum/technical terminators and decorative separator lines end the explicit region. Exact audio-count gating still applies. In the reported Reverend Gary Davis 1967-07-08 example with 16 audio files, Reverend Gary Davis, Friends' Center, Seattle, WA, and SBD > ? > CDr > EAC > FLAC above Set 1 must not become titles; the 16 titles are Introduction through Samson and Delilah, including the three continuation titles after the on July 7, 1967: divider.

Numbered-date-boundary and continuity rule: A line that begins with a valid calendar date and then carries broadcast, venue, source, or other subsection context must be treated as a non-title section boundary rather than as a numbered song row. Supported numeric date forms include year-first dates and day/month or month/day forms already used by TLO; calendar validity is required before a date-prefixed contextual line is promoted to a boundary. In an established numbered run, a provisional forward jump must not be committed when the next numbered row is exactly the number TLO was waiting for: for example, after 01 through 07, a false candidate beginning 30 followed by real track 08 means the 30 row is discarded and 08 remains normalized track 8. Confirmed large numbering gaps remain supported when later numbering reinforces the jump, such as 01, 02, 30, 31. A lost newline that directly joins an apostrophe-style duration to a following valid dated subsection heading must not append that heading text to the preceding song title. In the reported Tadd Dameron Royal Roost 1948 example, the dated headings 16.10.1948, 23.10.1948, 30.10.1948, and 06.11.1948 are boundaries, and the fourteen songs remain numbered 01 through 14; 30.10.1948 must never become normalized track 8. Location-safe artist-header and bare-number rule: generic path artist scanning must not promote a DB artist phrase when that occurrence is only the parsed trailing city of a longer location suffix; strict unlabeled headers may contain one extra room/hall line before the named Venue; a collaboration header is accepted only when every component resolves uniquely in the Artist DB; and one exact-count consecutive bare-number block represents Unknown-title track positions rather than numeric song names. The reported Chick Corea and Herbie Hancock 2015-04-10 Kennedy Center example therefore resolves Artist = Chick Corea and Herbie Hancock, Venue = Kennedy Center, Location = Washington, DC, and eleven Unknown Titles.

Thorough Setlist Matching rule: Add an optional Thorough Setlist Matching mode, default off. Normal mode preserves early stopping: TLO uses the established local-setlist/eTreeDB/setlist.fm waterfall and does not spend additional online requests after confidence is already sufficient. When Thorough Setlist Matching is selected, TLO must collect and compare reasonable candidates from the selected local text file, all matching same-date eTreeDB performances when etreeDB is enabled, and setlist.fm when that source is enabled. Thorough setlist.fm collection is proactive even when eTreeDB already returned usable venue/location data and may follow additional same-date result pages. The candidate pool includes exact audio-count lists and near-count lists within two titles of the audio-file count. Candidate ranking must consider local structural strength, audio-count distance, positive positional corroboration from audio filenames and existing Title tags, compatible Venue/Location evidence, and agreement with independent source families. A strong local numbered/explicit recording-specific list may therefore beat online consensus when the actual audio corroborates it, while matching eTreeDB and setlist.fm lists may beat a weak or uncorroborated local parse. Equal title counts alone do not prove alignment: Thorough mode must use sequence alignment when audio evidence supports insertion/deletion skew such as recording-only Intro/Tuning/Crowd tracks or a performance-only Encore. For audio-only aligned positions, use a usable filename title, then a usable existing Title tag, otherwise Unknown; do not shift every later song merely to preserve raw positions. Near-count candidates may be used only when at least two audio positions corroborate the alignment and at least half of the available audio-title evidence agrees; otherwise fall back to the normal selection path. If the two highest-scoring candidates come from different source families, are nearly tied, and materially disagree in sequence, report a Thorough Setlist Matching ambiguity and do not silently choose by source order. setlist.fm Upgrade changes accessibility/capacity only, not authority: with setlist.fm enabled, Thorough mode may be used with or without upgrade, but normal setlist.fm access remains limited to the normal request spacing/run cap and can therefore make thorough coverage slower or incomplete; setlist.fm Upgrade permits the same deconfliction logic to gather setlist.fm evidence much more aggressively under the upgraded limits.

Checking Tag Copy or Tag Copy/Delete Original must only select that mutually exclusive mode. After the user starts Inventory or the main-window Tag action, TLO must open the selected mode's modal destination window and ask for an existing fully qualified destination directory. The Tag Copy window explains that the original is retained, exact capacity preflight always applies, and the recursive folder structure, relative file paths, and file sizes are verified without a SHA-256 content hash. The Tag Copy/Delete Original window additionally warns that original material will be removed; it explains that same-partition transfers are directory moves with no source-size totaling or file-size comparison, while different-partition transfers receive exact capacity preflight, recursive relative path/folder/size verification, and SHA-256 verification of every file before deleting the source. OK remains unavailable until the path is valid and available-storage information can be read. The selected destination overrides per-path --/copy and --/copy-delete destinations from direct Search Path entries and .txt control files. Dry Run follows the same destination selection and planning sequence without performing the transfer.

Add a checkbox titled etreeDB, mapped to --etree-lookup; a checkbox titled setlist.fm, mapped to --setlistfm-lookup; directly beneath it a checkbox titled setlist.fm Upgrade, mapped to --setlistfm-upgrade; and a checkbox titled Thorough Setlist Matching, mapped to --thorough-setlist-matching. Thorough Setlist Matching defaults unchecked and may be used whether or not online lookup sources are enabled. If SETLISTFM_API_KEY is missing or blank when the GUI is built, the setlist.fm and setlist.fm Upgrade checkboxes must both be forced unchecked and disabled so the GUI cannot select an unavailable service. The API key value must never be displayed. When a setlist.fm control is disabled, the main GUI must provide a non-secret reason distinguishing a missing normal key, a missing accepted upgrade key, or an upgrade-key mismatch. The main-window Thorough-specific Info line must appear only when Thorough Setlist Matching is selected, setlist.fm is enabled, and setlist.fm Upgrade is not enabled. In that one case, the Info line warns that Thorough setlist.fm matching will be slow under the normal 600-millisecond / 1,400-call limits. No Thorough-specific Info line is shown when Thorough is off, when setlist.fm is off, or when setlist.fm Upgrade is enabled. The upgrade checkbox itself has no effect unless setlist.fm is enabled and changes accessibility/capacity, not source authority. Add a checkbox titled Delete Extra Tags, mapped to --delete-extra-tags. It defaults unchecked and its visible label is split over two lines as "Delete Extra" / "Tags". When selected, it applies the exact four-field metadata-retention rule in Section 13.1 to Inventory-time tagging, Add Shows tagging, GUI Tag, and standalone tlo-tag. The normal setlist.fm key and the upgrade key must be validated as printable non-whitespace ASCII before enabling their respective controls or reserving any API rate slot. Invalid-key status must be reported without echoing the key, and Unicode/value errors during request construction must be converted to the normal setlist.fm lookup error contract.

If setlist.fm is available and checked, etreeDB must remain checked automatically. If the user clears etreeDB while setlist.fm is still checked, the GUI must restore etreeDB so the dependency remains visible and explicit. Environment resolution checks nonblank process/session values first and uses persisted Windows User/System values only as fallback for a missing/blank corresponding process value. If SETLISTFM_API_KEY remains missing or blank, both setlist.fm-related checkboxes remain disabled and unchecked. If the normal key is present but neither SETLISTFMUPGRADE_API_KEY nor SETLISTFM_UPGRADE_API_KEY is present/nonblank, only setlist.fm Upgrade remains disabled and unchecked. If an upgrade variable is present but does not exactly match SETLISTFM_API_KEY, setlist.fm Upgrade remains disabled and unchecked. The GUI must state the applicable missing/mismatch reason without displaying either key.

The visible main-GUI checkboxes must use a four-row, four-column logical grid. Row and column numbers in this document are one-based. Row 1 is: Column 1 etreeDB; Column 2 Compliant; Column 3 Tag In Place; Column 4 Artist In Album Tag. Row 2 is: Column 1 setlist.fm; Column 2 Rename Compliantly; Column 3 Tag Copy; Column 4 Convert shn. Row 3 is: Column 1 setlist.fm Upgrade; Column 2 As-Is Artist Name; Column 3 Tag Copy/Delete Original; Column 4 Dry Run. Row 4 is: Column 1 Thorough Setlist Matching; Column 2 Proper Grammar; Column 3 is occupied by the wrapped Tag Copy/Delete Original control from Row 3; Column 4 Delete Extra Tags. When tlo-main.py or tlo-main.exe is launched from the command line with --etree-lookup and/or --setlistfm-lookup, the corresponding GUI checkboxes must reflect the launch arguments. Command-line --setlistfm-lookup without --etree-lookup is a startup error; interactive dependency behavior is defined in Section 9 and the preceding GUI checkbox rule. The --debug command-line argument remains accepted, enables debug behavior, and is not shown as a visible GUI checkbox.
Add/maintain a GUI main program named tlo-main.py.
The GUI should reflect the inputs from tlo-gi.py, using checkboxes where possible and text boxes where text is required.
The GUI must include a Performance Mode selector with gentle, balanced, fast, and extreme.

The GUI must include a Max Workers text field. It is a maximum worker ceiling. When the GUI is launched with a positive --max-workers value, display that value initially. If --max-workers is omitted or supplied as 0, initialize the field from the selected Performance Mode: gentle = 1; balanced = min(2, CPU count); fast = CPU count; extreme = min(4 × CPU count, 64), minimum 1. Whenever the user selects a different Performance Mode in the GUI, reset Max Workers to that mode’s automatic ceiling. The user may then edit Max Workers to another positive value. Runtime phases may use fewer workers according to mode, work-group/drive constraints, and correctness rules.

The GUI default Performance Mode must be balanced. With no positive launcher override, Max Workers defaults to the balanced automatic ceiling. Whenever a Performance Mode is selected, Max Workers is reset to that mode’s automatic ceiling, including after startup with an explicit positive launcher value. The GUI must not display explanatory/helper comments next to the Performance Mode selector or Max Workers text field; it should show only the control labels and controls. All visible GUI control fonts must use the configured main GUI font size, defined at startup as two points larger than the Tk default label/checkbutton font, while the bold title font remains two points larger than that main GUI size.

The Main GUI and Search GUI must not display an editable TLOHome input box. Each GUI must display a read-only label showing the resolved TLOHome, formatted as TLOHome: <path>. In the Main GUI, that label must be on the same top row as the Traders Little Organizer™ Main heading and immediately to the left of the hamburger menu; there must be no separate TLOHome row. TLOHome resolution remains non-GUI: --myTLO first, then --TLOHome, then the TLOHome environment variable.

The Main GUI must use an upper-right hamburger menu. The Help cascade contains About and FAQ. About must display Traders Little Organizer™ - TLO with the superscript trademark symbol, the current public version/build from tlo_version.DISPLAY_VERSION, developer attribution, tool attribution, and contact text. FAQ opens TLOHome/TLO-FAQ.txt; TLO-FAQ.txt is included in the source bundle and end-user complete distributions. The About contact address is support@traderslittleorganizer.com.

The Main GUI hamburger menu must include a top-level Donate cascade. Donate contains Venmo and Check cascades, each displayed with the platform menu chevron. Venmo displays @James-Scarano-3. Check displays James Scarano, 49 Majestic Ave., Nashua, NH 03063. All donation detail rows must use normal enabled menu text so they display as dark text rather than disabled gray text. Selecting a donation detail row must not launch an external service or perform another action.

The Main GUI and Search GUI update menus must include Check for updates and Auto update. Check for updates queries the latest GitHub Release under the TradersLittleOrganizer repository, extracts its recognizable TLO build number, and compares that number to the installed build before requiring independent update-signing metadata. A release whose build is older than or equal to the installed build is not an update candidate and must be reported as up to date even if that historical release predates the signed-metadata mechanism. Only a genuinely newer release proceeds to signed-metadata verification and package selection. Manual checks retain direct-download behavior after a newer release has been independently authorized. Auto update is a persistent update-check preference. Windows update_downloads=msi is the default regardless of original install method; update_downloads=zip explicitly requests the portable ZIP: an automatic check must discover a newer exact-match package without downloading it, then prompt the user with Yes and Skip. Yes downloads the verified package to the user Downloads folder, and then allows the user to install a downloaded MSI after a separate confirmation (portable ZIP packages remain download-only); Skip returns immediately without downloading. The official update source is fixed by build-time constants to onaracstlo-lab/TradersLittleOrganizer; environment variables must not redirect it.

Auto update stores its local state in TLOHome/update-settings.json. On startup, the Main GUI and Search GUI read that file, set the Auto update checkmark when auto_update is true, and perform the discovery check at most once every 24 hours. Finding a newer release records the check before the Yes/Skip prompt so choosing Skip does not cause repeated startup prompts inside the same interval. A download occurs only after Yes. Manual Check for updates always runs immediately and continues to download a newer exact-match package directly. The settings record the exact downloaded package kind, platform/layout key, packaging mode, and whether that package includes the TLO database master files.

The updater must never unzip, execute, install, replace, or delete files. It downloads the selected ZIP asset to the user Downloads folder and alerts the user with the full path. Selection must use only official exact release-asset names for the installed operating system and package layout; generic/source ZIPs and the other Windows layout must never be substitutes. The updater must prefer the exact matching update ZIP and fall back only to the exact matching complete ZIP when no matching update ZIP exists. After SHA-256 verification, it must inspect the package manifest inside the ZIP without extracting it, verify package kind/build/platform-layout and database declarations against the ZIP contents, reject mismatches, and report whether the downloaded package includes databases. Windows hybrid and Windows onedir installations must be distinguished from the installed TLOHome/runtime layout.

REQ-NET-001  Updater downloads must sanitize the release asset filename to a basename, accept only allowlisted GitHub-hosted HTTPS asset URLs, and refuse any newer update asset that lacks a valid SHA-256 digest authorized by independently signed TLO metadata. Before transfer, reject any declared asset larger than the configured 1 GiB ceiling. Stream in bounded chunks, reject received bytes above the signed declared size or hard ceiling, and require exact declared-size equality. Before reporting a downloaded ZIP as valid, reject absolute or drive-qualified member names, parent traversal, symbolic-link entries, excessive member count, excessive total uncompressed size, and unsafe compression ratios, then validate the package manifest and ZIP integrity. A digest supplied only by the same GitHub release channel is an integrity aid, not independent publisher authenticity. ZIP validation must also reject duplicate normalized member names, NTFS alternate-data-stream syntax, Windows reserved device names, and path components ending in a dot or space before any package member is trusted.

REQ-NET-002  Cryptographic publisher-authenticity for newer update metadata is mandatory and separate from transport/release-channel integrity. The signing private key must remain protected outside ordinary release-publishing credentials and TLO must pin the corresponding public key. For a release whose recognizable build number is less than or equal to the installed build, TLO may return up-to-date without loading or verifying signed metadata because that release cannot be accepted as an update. For every genuinely newer release, TLO must fail closed unless TLO_UPDATE_METADATA.json and TLO_UPDATE_METADATA.sig verify against the pinned key and authorize the selected asset identity, size, SHA-256, build, package kind, and platform/layout.
Include hidden myTLO compatibility with the same precedence as CLI. It must not appear in help output or as a visible GUI field.

Search Path is required for Full Inventory and its compact main-window label must read simply "Path(s)" with no optional/override text and no helper line beneath the text box. The main GUI must not contain a separate Slam label or entry; per-path artist overrides are entered inline with --/slam on the applicable Path(s) entry or control-file line.

Include Tag, Add New Shows, Research, Manual Tweaks, Quit, Inventory (full), Pause, and Resume buttons in the main button row. Include a Dry Run checkbox in the main options grid. Tag must display at the far left. Add New Shows, Manual Tweaks, and Inventory (full) may use concise two-line labels to keep the main row readable. The Add New Shows button invokes the existing Add Shows/Updater workflow without changing its functionality. Main action buttons should use compact horizontal padding. Folder reversal is intentionally not a main-GUI action; it is provided by the standalone tlo-reverse CLI. Copy Requests is opened from the upper-right hamburger menu and is not a main-row button.

Main button layout: Tag is at the far left, followed by Add New Shows, Research, and Manual Tweaks in the left action group; Quit is centered; and Inventory (full), Pause, and Resume are grouped on the right. Add New Shows invokes the existing incremental Add Shows/Updater workflow. All main-row buttons must use the same main-button style and remain usable when the window is resized. Button labels throughout all TLO windows must remain centered horizontally and vertically. Copy Requests and Redundancy Groups appear only in the upper-right hamburger menu.

Folder reversal is a standalone CLI operation named tlo-reverse. It accepts one required fully qualified folder/path argument identifying the original path, current path, or containing path whose logged folder operation is to be reversed. It restores folder state only and must never attempt to restore, remove, compare, or otherwise change audio tags. Reverse SHALL read both current token-scoped tag logs and the persistent folderOperations.log archive so re-inventory does not eliminate prior reversible folder operations.

tlo-reverse must infer the folder operation from TLOHome/logs success-tag logs; a required copy/rename mode flag is prohibited because the authoritative log line already records the action. It must recognize TAG_COPY_DELETE_MOVE and TAG_COPY_DELETE_COPY as Copy/Delete operations, TAG_COPY as retained-original copy operations, and RENAME_COMPLIANTLY source -> destination as rename-only operations. A combined Copy/Delete + Rename Compliantly run is represented by its final TAG_COPY_DELETE_* source -> destination mapping and is reversed as one folder operation.

The CLI must resolve TLOHome with normal shared precedence and search current tags*.txt plus compatible legacy tag*.log files. The path argument scopes candidate mappings. Current filesystem state is used only to establish which logged run is presently reversible; the exact logged source and destination remain authoritative for mutation. If more than one logged run remains applicable for a broad path, tlo-reverse must stop rather than guess. The user may supply a narrower path or the optional --log argument to select one specific log.

Reversal semantics are operation-specific. For Copy/Delete, restore the exact logged destination folder to the exact logged source path; use a same-filesystem directory rename/move when possible, otherwise copy the complete tree, verify it before delete, then remove the destination. For rename-only, rename/move the exact logged destination back to the exact logged source path. For Tag Copy, retain the original source and remove only the exact logged copied destination; before deletion, require the source and copy to contain the same relative file-name set so an independently modified copy is not deleted. Tag data differences are permitted and are never inspected for reversal.

Before any destructive change, tlo-reverse must report the selected success-log filename and every matching operation. --dry-run must perform selection and report the exact actions without changing folders. Existing source/destination conflicts must never be overwritten or merged. Missing logged destinations are skipped. A Tag Copy reversal whose relative file set has diverged is a conflict and the copied tree is left untouched. Before removing a same-file-set Tag Copy, TLO must also detect destination files whose modification time indicates a possible post-run replacement; such a copy is a conflict and is left untouched rather than silently deleting the potentially replaced file. For a cross-filesystem rename or Copy/Delete reversal, symbolic links must be copied as symbolic links, their link targets must be included in verification, and the logged destination must not be removed until the copied tree is verified with symlink identity preserved.

Every reversal must append an audit record to TLOHome/logs/reverseFolders.log. The audit record includes the requested path, selected success log, operation count, dry-run state, and per-operation outcome. The older embedded Reverse Copy/Delete + Rename GUI workflow is removed from the Main GUI. The obsolete tlo_reverse_copy_delete implementation is not shipped. All supported user-facing reversal behavior is implemented by tlo-reverse/tlo_reverse_folders and covers rename-only, Copy/Delete with or without compliant rename, and Tag Copy with or without compliant destination naming.

Before the GUI Tag or standalone tlo-tag run validates required artist and venue databases, initialize the TLOHome-derived database paths using the standard logging/configuration bootstrap. Validation must check the resolved files, never fail merely because Config database path fields were not yet initialized. Missing or unreadable database files remain explicit errors.

All pre-execution settings reporting must use the canonical Review Operation requirements in Section 14.1. GUI Tag reads the current main-window values when Tag is clicked. Add Shows child-window actions likewise read current main-window values at action time rather than retaining snapshots from when the updater window was opened.

The Add New Shows window must include a Search Path textbox for Process New Shows. It is pre-filled with the current TLOHome/readyForXfer path, accepts one existing directory, and supports native-Windows folder drag/drop. The selected Search Path identifies the directory whose immediate child folders are the new-show candidates; it replaces the previous hard-wired readyForXfer source for Process New Shows and its Dry Run preview. Process Potential Duplicate/Upgrades continues to use TLOHome/dups. If Add Shows is used before any bootlist.csv exists, the updater must warn that Add Shows can create a new bootlist from the selected Search Path but is normally used after a full inventory. The updater must require a non-blank Current Backup/Storage Drive and Volume before bootstrapping the first real bootlist output, and must ask the user to continue or cancel before processing new shows as the first inventory output. The Add Shows window must not contain separate Preview buttons, a Dry Run checkbox, or duplicated main-window option checkboxes. Check for Duplicates remains because it is specific to Process New Shows. When either Add Shows action is clicked, it must read the current main-window checkbox values. When main-window Dry Run is checked, clicking Process New Shows or Process Potential Duplicate/Upgrades must perform the detailed non-destructive analysis instead of moving, renaming, tagging, converting, deleting, or writing inventory output. Dry Run must remain available even when the first real Add Shows run would require a storage-volume value.
Needs_Atomization: yes Process New Shows shall show current folder and processed/total, staged, duplicate, held and error counts while running. After its completion summary, the GUI shall automatically run pending duplicate/upgrade review if dups contains candidates; the manual Process Potential Duplicate/Upgrades button remains available.

Requirement_Text: Add Shows incremental processing must honor the main GUI Tag In Place checkbox. When Tag In Place is selected, both the selected Search Path-to-staged Process New Shows path and the duplicate-resolution Process path must tag the accepted source folder in place after any compliant rename and generated setlist preparation, but before the folder is moved into staged. Add Shows Dry Run must use the production metadata and track-title selection logic and display the resulting show name plus each applicable file's planned Artist, Album, Track, and Title values, title source, SHN conversion target, skip reason, and potential duplicate matches without changing content.

Add Shows potential-duplicate detection must require both a matching performance date and an independently validated artist match against the same existing bootlist Show cell. Raw resolved show names and raw folder basenames may be used only as probes from which the Artist DB resolves a legitimate artist; they must never directly satisfy the artist predicate. Artist comparison must use normalized whole-token/whole-phrase boundaries rather than arbitrary substring containment, while continuing to accept the resolved Artist DB master name and valid aliases.

Add Shows potential-duplicate handling: when Process New Shows has Check for Duplicates selected and a candidate matches an existing bootlist Show, immediately move the incoming folder into TLOHome/dups for later Process Potential Duplicate/Upgrades review. This rule applies regardless of whether the matching show is on the same, another, or an unknown/disconnected partition. Do not add a (pdupNN) suffix or otherwise rename the incoming folder, add any bootlist/inventory row, create or replace an exported setlist, convert audio, or tag the folder during Process New Shows. Move-path name collisions must preserve both folders by allocating a distinct destination name. Continue recognizing pre-existing (pdupNN) names as potential matches without generating new markers. If Check for Duplicates is off or no match exists, retain the normal accepted-show workflow. Add Shows Dry Run must reflect the duplicate-routing action without implying tagging or inventory creation.
Needs_Atomization: yes After Process New Shows completes, the GUI shall automatically scan and open review for any pending dups entries. Quit on an individual candidate shall leave it pending so it can be reviewed via Process Potential Duplicate/Upgrades later.

Requirement_Text: Add Shows does not perform Tag Copy or Tag Copy/Delete Original. If either is selected in the main GUI, Add Shows must report the selected value in Review Operation and identify the two Full Inventory copy modes as not used by Add Shows, so it does not create a second copy-mode destination outside the selected Process New Shows Search Path and the managed dups/staged workflow. Add Shows must not maintain a separate Mode display of duplicated main-window settings. Rename Compliantly continues to run before tagging so the folder name, generated setlist, bootlist row, and audio tags refer to the same final show name.

When Add Shows creates its duplicate-upgrade cleanup script, use deleteReplacedFolders.bat on Windows and deleteBackupFolders.sh elsewhere. The file must name the actual selected old bootlist.csv targets only after translating each rooted VolumePath into syntax valid for the script platform. Windows-drive paths and WSL /mnt/<drive> paths may be translated when the mapping is unambiguous. If a selected row cannot be translated into a safely rooted target for the script platform, skip that delete command, retain that bootlist row, and report the skipped cleanup. Windows batch output must begin with setlocal DisableDelayedExpansion, escape each literal percent sign as %%, and use CRLF line endings. The existing-file Backup Alert must identify the actual script basename, for example "TLOHome/deleteReplacedFolders.bat already exists. Continue or abort?" or the .sh equivalent.
