On Windows, an active rmdir is permitted only after comparing the recorded source label with the label currently present at that drive letter. Unlabeled, mismatched, missing, or unverifiable drives must not be deleted automatically.
Needs_Atomization: yes The Windows cleanup script is a reusable, manually run, permanently destructive rmdir /s /q template. It does not send old folders to the Recycle Bin, journal deleted-folder contents, or provide deletion undo. Its volume-label and path-safety guards remain mandatory.

Requirement_Text: The main GUI must include checkboxes labeled Tag In Place, Tag Copy, Tag Copy/Delete Original, Rename Compliantly, As-Is Artist Name, Proper Grammar, and Dry Run. Proper Grammar appears directly under As-Is Artist Name and defaults unchecked. As-Is Artist Name overrides Proper Grammar when both are checked. Tag In Place, Tag Copy, and Tag Copy/Delete Original are mutually exclusive. Compliant and Rename Compliantly are also mutually exclusive: selecting either one in the GUI clears the other, and supplying both on the inventory, GUI-launcher, or standalone-tagger command line is an error. Checking Tag Copy or Tag Copy/Delete Original only selects the mode; the destination is requested after the operation starts.

The main GUI must include a Convert shn checkbox. The checkbox maps to --convert-shn and applies to Tag, Full Inventory, Add Shows, Tag In Place During Inventory, Tag Copy During Inventory, and Tag Copy/Delete Original During Inventory. Convert shn remains valid when no tagging box is checked; in that case it performs only SHN/SHNF-to-FLAC conversion and does not write tags.

When the selected setlist supplies an explicit or structurally confirmed artist and the beginning of the show folder independently agrees with that artist, TLO shall accept the artist even if the Artist DB has no entry. Require whole artist-name tokens, permitting an initial The and equivalent and/& collaboration connectors but not arbitrary path substrings. Preserve Artist DB canonical/alias precedence when uniquely resolved, and do not override conflicting stronger metadata. Record each accepted unknown artist in run observations and artistsNotInDatabase.txt using the selected artist name. Apply in Inventory and Add New Shows, including compliant and non-compliant modes. Nonmatching or ambiguous headers do not qualify.

Add New Shows must verify its selected Tag In Place operation before a new show is accepted, staged, exported into setlists, or added to bootlist.csv. Use the shared tagging engine and performance grouping; if multiple independent shows are detected beneath one input folder, retain the folder for review rather than assigning a single setlist to all music files. When tagging is selected, accept a show only when every eligible audio file is successfully tagged or is already correctly tagged, with no skipped tagging group or file error. Report every excluded non-taggable audio file separately. Untaggable SHN files require Convert shn to be eligible. If validation is inconclusive or tagging is incomplete, retain the incoming folder in place for review without an inventory or exported-setlist entry. Potential duplicates continue moving directly to TLOHome/dups without tagging or inventory writes. If Deep Audio Check is checked, apply the existing tagging-first corruption classifier and existing file/folder deletion policies before final acceptance. No corruption checks are performed when neither tagging nor Deep Audio Check is selected. Show processed, staged, held, removed, duplicate, tagged, unchanged, skipped, error, and excluded counts in the completion report. Add Shows supports Tag In Place; unsupported Tag Copy/Copy-Delete selections must cause an explicit error before processing, not silently stage untagged files. If staging collides with an existing folder name, write the actual destination name to the bootlist; rollback staging and partial inventory output on acceptance-commit failures. The same verification gate applies when the user explicitly resolves a candidate duplicate as a replacement: do not remove old bootlist rows, write old-folder deletion scripts, stage the new show, or export a setlist until the candidate has passed tagging and optional Deep Audio Check. If verification or acceptance output fails, retain or restore the candidate under TLOHome/dups and preserve the prior inventory and deletion script contents.

Inventory Tag In Place must parse selected local setlist metadata and numbered song titles with the same facilities used by standalone Tag. A concert header of the form Artist(s): Event / weekday and complete performance date / City, State @ Venue may be treated as a confirmed unlabeled artist/location header only when both a complete date and an independently parseable city/region are present. Do not misclassify a weekday or a lineage line as the artist. For a safely confirmed event header, permit the printed multi-artist name when no single Artist DB entry exists, without overwriting stronger existing metadata. When a setlist count cannot be matched to audio, first use corroborated title sources and then consider existing audio TITLE tags as a fallback, logging missing/unknown tracks; never blindly map a mismatched list. Audio title values consisting only of question marks become unknown. Existing safety rules for unidentified shows, corruption checks and deletion continue to apply.

When Tag In Place is checked for an inventory run, each Stage 3 inventory group with music files must attempt to write Artist, Album, normalized zero-padded track number, and Title tags to the inventoried music files. When Tag Copy is checked or --/copy is used, TLO copies each music folder, verifies all relative file paths and file sizes, tags the copy, and keeps the original source tree in the inventory. When Tag Copy/Delete Original is used, TLO captures metadata from the original source tree and records the destination in the inventory. A same-filesystem transfer is a directory rename/move with no size totaling or file-size verification. A cross-filesystem transfer is copied and verified by relative path and file size before the original is deleted; the destination is then tagged.

For Tag Copy/Delete Original, the destination volume label remains the inventory volume identity, but the destination parent is a container and must not become a subtree re-inventory scope merely because prior logs or bootlist rows exist beneath it. Startup must append the transferred shows to the existing destination inventory rather than selecting every prior row under the destination parent for replacement. During postprocess, an existing row may be replaced only when its complete normalized Volume and Path exactly match a destination show path produced by the current Copy/Delete run. Child paths, sibling shows, and all other rows beneath the destination parent must be preserved. This Copy/Delete-specific rule does not change ordinary direct inventory: explicitly inventorying an already inventoried destination tree may still re-inventory that requested tree under the normal same-path/child-path/parent-path policy. If the destination volume label is blank, transferred destination entries continue to append to the blank-volume log set.

Inventory-time tagging must not mutate folders when a show name cannot be determined. In that case, TLO must skip Tag In Place, Tag Copy, Tag Copy/Delete Original, and Rename Compliantly for that group, leave the original folder untouched, and still handle the group normally for inventory and unresolved-show reporting.

Inventory-time tagging results must be split into TLOHome/logs/tagsN.txt and TLOHome/logs/tageN.txt, where N is the same allocated short log token used by confN.log, deadN.log, compN.log, dupsN.log, groupsN.log, and metaN.log for that search path. Successful/status actions go to tagsN.txt. Warnings, skips, cancellations, and errors go to tageN.txt and must use structured reason-code prefixes such as SKIP_SETLIST_MISSING, SKIP_SETLIST_UNREADABLE, SKIP_TITLE_PARSE, SKIP_TITLE_COUNT, WARN_TITLE_PARTIAL, and ERROR_AUDIO_FILE when applicable.

When debug is enabled, Tag In Place During Inventory, Tag Copy During Inventory, and the standalone tlo-tag and GUI Tag may write diagnostic setlist copies to TLOHome/debug only for skipped selected-setlist title diagnostics, such as no parseable tracks or a setlist/audio count mismatch, when a readable selected setlist can be included for review. The debug output .txt filename must match the generated inventory setlist filename. Successfully writing one or more generated Unknown titles, having no readable setlist, bad audio-file errors, invalid FLAC files, failed per-file tag writes, SHN conversion/file errors, metadata-only skips, and target-preparation failures must not create debug files; those conditions are recorded in tageN.txt/tageT.txt with reason codes.

Standalone/GUI Tag logging requirement: tag console/output must be mirrored to TLOHome/logs/tagsT.txt and TLOHome/logs/tageT.txt. Progress/status/success lines go to tagsT.txt; consequential errors, warnings, skips, cancellation lines, and completion lines that report file errors go to tageT.txt. Successful parser-selection decisions (for example selecting the best contiguous numbered block or declining an unsafe prose fallback) are informational and must not be logged/surfaced as tagging warnings solely because a decision was made. Error-log lines should carry structured reason-code prefixes when practical, and each run should emit a problem-summary block by reason code when consequential problems were recorded.

Tagging runs must append the complete path of each FLAC or MP3 file that cannot be opened or written to TLOHome/CorruptFlacs.txt. The filename is retained for compatibility; the file covers both supported corruption-checked formats. This file is additive diagnostic output and does not replace tagsT.txt/tageT.txt or inventory-time tagsN.txt/tageN.txt logging.
Pause must request a traversal pause without deleting logs or closing the GUI. Resume must clear the pause request and continue the same inventory run.

Include an embedded console output window that captures console data. Ctrl-A / Control-A in the main console must select the complete console contents so the full output can be copied without mouse selection.
The embedded console must remain visible together with the full main control area at the bounded initial GUI size; it must not force the main action controls below the usable screen area.

Every editable text input in the TLO GUI applications, including Tk Entry, ttk Entry, editable Combobox, and text-entry widgets created later in dialogs, must support Ctrl-A / Control-A to select the complete current contents. The behavior must be installed application-wide rather than depending on individual fields being wired manually.
The main GUI window title bar must read TLO Main GUI followed by the current tlo_version.DISPLAY_VERSION; the version/build must not be hard-coded in the GUI.
The bold main-GUI heading must read Traders Little Organizer™ Main.

Add/maintain a -h option for tlo-main.py. Help must describe visible text boxes and checkboxes and list arguments as they should be specified on the command line. The GUI help text must not describe a visible Debug checkbox, but command-line help may list --debug [BOOL] as a command-line-only option.

Rename Compliantly must not require Tag In Place, Tag Copy, or Tag Copy/Delete Original, but it must not be combined with Compliant. For non-compliant Full Inventory, Rename Compliantly by itself means rename the identified original show folder in place without tagging. A broad collection or search parent containing unrelated music folders must never be renamed as one show merely because descendant folders contain wrapper or volume-like suffixes. The GUI and CLI must accept the valid rename-only combination without an alert or validation error. Standalone tlo-tag writes tags directly under its selected tag path and may rename an identified show folder before tagging. GUI Tag follows the selected main tag mode: Tag In Place tags the source, Tag Copy tags the verified copy while retaining the source, and Tag Copy/Delete Original transfers then tags the destination; compliant renaming may occur before tagging where valid.

Before Rename Compliantly changes a source folder, require a positively identified show. A proposed name must retain all identifying information present in the original folder: artist, known year/date, city/region, venue, and recording-source qualifiers (such as SBD, AUD, matrix or FM). If uncertainty or material loss remains, skip the rename without altering the source. Capitalization-only differences may be corrected. Punctuation normalization must not cause a second rename on re-inventory; a stable compliant folder name is idempotent. Collision handling and Windows reserved-name protection continue unchanged.

The GUI Tag action must not create a Tagger child window. It uses the main Inventory window console and Current Operation area. It reads the current master Path(s), including inline --/slam directives, the tag-mode checkbox, shared lookup/corruption/tagging options, and Dry Run value when Tag is clicked, then follows the canonical Review Operation reporting rules in Section 14.1. The standalone tlo-tag CLI remains available and requires its own explicit search folder.

On native Windows, drag/drop for GUI Tag is the existing main Path(s) drag/drop behavior. Dropped folders/control files populate or append to the master Path(s) field under its established rules. There is no separate Tagging Path drop target in the GUI. The standalone tlo-tag CLI does not require GUI drag/drop.

Clicking the main Tag button must start the Tag workflow from the main Main GUI without opening a new Tagger window. Tag validates the master Path(s), uses any inline --/slam directives and current main-window options, requires one of Tag In Place, Tag Copy, or Tag Copy/Delete Original, performs the shared Review Operation step, and displays Current Operation/progress/output in the main window. Tag Copy and Tag Copy/Delete Original use the same destination dialogs and safety rules as their Inventory equivalents. Dry Run uses the same inputs/options without mutation.

tlo-main.py must reject --tag-path and --search-folder because GUI Tag has no separate Tagging Path field. Standalone tlo-tag.py remains the only user-facing Tag surface that accepts its own command-line search folder.

When the main GUI Tag action starts, Tag must read and honor the current main etreeDB, setlist.fm, setlist.fm Upgrade, Thorough Setlist Matching, corruption controls, tag mode, Rename Compliantly, Convert shn, Artist In Album Tag, As-Is Artist Name, Proper Grammar, Deep Audio Check, Delete Extra Tags, Dry Run, Performance Mode, and Max Workers ceiling. setlist.fm retains the established eTreeDB dependency and is unavailable in the GUI when SETLISTFM_API_KEY is missing/blank. setlist.fm Upgrade is unavailable unless SETLISTFMUPGRADE_API_KEY or SETLISTFM_UPGRADE_API_KEY is present; on Windows TLO also checks persisted User/System environment values when the process environment is stale.

While GUI Tag is active, the main Main GUI owns Pause/Resume and Quit/cancellation behavior. Conflicting main actions remain disabled until the Tag worker exits. Tag writing must check for cancellation before each audio-file write so a long folder can stop between files. After the worker exits, the main action states must be recalculated immediately.

When a GUI Tag run completes, the main Main GUI must display the elapsed-time/completion summary using the shared completion workflow. Format elapsed time as M:SS for runs under one hour and H:MM:SS for runs of one hour or longer.

The main tlo-main window must not display an Error/OK validation-status label beneath the Path(s) text box. Inventory and Tag must remain clickable whenever no conflicting workflow is active so clicking either can report path or option validation errors directly. The former main-window Tag Copy/Delete Original path label, text box, and validation label must not exist. Its modal destination dialog may display path and available-storage validation beside the dialog controls. Add Shows storage-volume validation may remain visible near its related controls.

Before Full Inventory, Tag, Process New Shows, or Process Potential Duplicate/Upgrades begins, the shared Review Operation dialog must report the same ordered main-window checkbox section: etreeDB; Compliant; Tag In Place; Artist In Album Tag; setlist.fm; setlist.fm Upgrade; Thorough Setlist Matching; Rename Compliantly; Tag Copy; Convert shn; As-Is Artist Name; Proper Grammar; Tag Copy/Delete Original; Delete Extra Tags; Dry Run. After that common section, report workflow-specific paths or path sources, destinations, and controls.

The shared Review Operation dialog shall display a vertical scrollbar when the reviewed content exceeds the available height, hide that scrollbar when everything fits, and allow mouse-wheel navigation. All review lines and any original-file warning must remain readable. The Start, Go Back and optional Preview Changes buttons shall remain visible below the scrolling region even with a lengthy Path(s) list or reduced screen height. Resizing shall update the scroll range without changing the selected operation or its recorded settings.

After Start is selected, append the reviewed settings to TLOHome/logs/runSettings.log before launching the worker or Dry Run. Use the same review-line list for the dialog and the log entry so displayed and recorded values cannot diverge.

Dry Run must perform the same show-group discovery, metadata resolution, enabled lookup sequence, album construction, and track-title selection needed to describe the results of the requested operation, but it must not write tags, rename, copy, move, delete, convert, create inventory output, or modify operational/output TLO logs. The required runSettings.log audit entry described in Section 12 is the sole logging exception and is written after Start exactly as for a live run. The main Inventory window must provide the single Dry Run checkbox. Full Inventory uses it directly; Tag and Add Shows use its current value and must not provide separate Dry Run controls. When main Dry Run is checked, clicking Inventory, Tag, Process New Shows, or Process Potential Duplicate/Upgrades analyzes the selected input instead of starting the destructive or output-producing operation. Full Inventory and Add Shows Dry Runs must list the resulting Show Name for every resolved show group. When an inventory tagging mode is selected, and for every Tag Dry Run, the output must list each applicable audio file together with the Artist, Album, Track, and Title values that would be written, the title source, and any planned SHN-to-FLAC target or reason the file would be skipped. Unresolved metadata and title-selection failures must be shown with the affected folder. Every dry run must report root count, music-folder count, media-file count, SHN/SHNF count, planned actions, input/read issues, and elapsed time.

The main Inventory window and Add Shows updater must display a structured Current Operation area during active work. Inventory and GUI Tag share the main Inventory Current Operation area. It must show the current stage or task, current path or item when available, useful cumulative counts when available, warning and error counts, elapsed time, and an active progress indicator while preserving the existing detailed console output where applicable. The indeterminate activity indicator must use a 120-millisecond animation interval; this visual timing must not affect throughput, worker scheduling, elapsed-time updates, or results.

Existing console and log lines must be classified into user-facing issue groups where possible, including unidentified shows, missing setlists, track-title mismatches, unreadable audio, copy/verification problems, online lookup problems, consequential tagging warnings, Add Shows folder errors, and general file or operation errors. Successful parser-choice/informational notices must not be promoted into the Issues list merely because they identify a folder. Duplicate issue records should be suppressed.

After Full Inventory, Add Shows processing, or Tag finishes, display a completion summary with success or failure state, elapsed time, operation-specific counts, warning count, and error count. The completion window must provide View Issues, Open Output when applicable, Open Logs, and Close actions. Add Shows folder failures must retain the affected folder path and exception message for issue review.

The Issues window must group records by reason, show severity and message, permit selection of individual issues, and provide an Open Path action when the issue contains an accessible file or directory path. Its horizontal scrollbar must have an actual scrollable range for long Explanation and Path values; those columns must not simply stretch/shrink to eliminate horizontal overflow. Detailed logs remain authoritative and accessible from the completion window. Open Path must never launch an arbitrary issue file. Local files are revealed/opened through their containing folder; UNC, device, and other network/non-local paths are refused.

The GUI has no Tagger child window. GUI Tag is intentionally integrated into the main Inventory window: it uses master Path(s), including inline --/slam directives, shared options, Review Operation, main Current Operation/progress, Pause/Resume, and main output. It must not provide a second set of Tag controls or a second Dry Run checkbox. The standalone tlo-tag CLI remains available as a separate command-line surface and requires an explicit search folder.

When packaged as a Windows PyInstaller executable, tlo-main.exe must support multiprocessing path-worker startup without treating worker bootstrap arguments as GUI arguments and without launching child GUI windows.

The current RTF manual must carry document metadata/keywords that name the current public build; stale build numbers in document properties are not permitted. When TLO opens an .rtf support/documentation file on Windows it must use the file type's registered Windows handler; .txt, .log, and .csv remain plain-text files suitable for Notepad. On Windows, directory opening and plain-text (.txt, .log, .csv) helper launches must use explicit explorer.exe and notepad.exe paths rooted in the Windows directory returned by GetSystemWindowsDirectoryW (with GetWindowsDirectoryW as the API fallback), and must not trust SystemRoot or executable-name search order.
The current user manual shall provide a first-inventory Quick Start before detailed installation and path theory.
The manual shall include symptom/cause/action troubleshooting and explain the structured SKIP_, WARN_, and ERROR_ reason codes exposed to users.

The documented command-line table shall cover every supported user-facing option, including --proper-grammar on the applicable Inventory/GUI/Tag surfaces, while continuing to omit intentionally undocumented compatibility options.
The manual shall include a glossary for TLO-specific terms and shall identify summary.log, runSettings.log, tokenized Inventory logs, tagsT.txt, and tageT.txt accurately.

The manual shall include current screenshots of the main Inventory window, Review Operation, and Add Shows. GUI Tag has no separate window, so no separate Tag screenshot is required; the main Inventory screenshot and Tag workflow text document that action. Screenshots are explanatory and do not override normative control requirements.
One-time optional shortcut instructions shall not outweigh recurring operational, troubleshooting, tagging, and logging guidance.
The main Main GUI shall include a visible button labeled Research. Research is read-only and uses the Main GUI's already-resolved TLOHome.

When Research is clicked, TLO shall open a Research input dialog containing one text-entry box and Search/Close actions. The prompt shall state that the input is an artist followed by a date, a venue, or a date. The Search button shall remain the active/default action whenever the Research dialog is active, and pressing Return or keypad Enter while focus is anywhere within that Research dialog shall be equivalent to Search.

A successful GUI research operation shall display the same formatted result produced by the standalone tlo-research command in a new read-only, non-wrapping text window with vertical scrolling and a horizontal scrollbar along the bottom of the results box. Ctrl-A at the results-window level shall select the complete result even when another control owns focus. The results window shall include a Search button, and Ctrl-F at the results-window level shall invoke the same action. Search shall open a dialog containing a text box labeled Search for: plus mutually exclusive Forward and Backwards radio buttons, with Forward selected by default. Repeated searches shall continue from the current selection/insertion position in the selected direction, compare case-insensitively, and wrap to the opposite end if no further match exists in that direction. If the requested text is absent from the complete result, report Not found without altering the result text. Search errors, missing TLOHome/logs, or invalid Research input shall be reported in GUI message dialogs without terminating the Main GUI.

Manual Tweaks opens the Manual Updates child window. Original accepts one folder or one .txt batch file; New Name supplies the authoritative replacement leaf for one-folder updates; Update Tags is checked by default. Inventory-backed updates use canonical [Volume] rootless-path identity, preserve the existing volume/parent path, fail closed on ambiguous/cross-volume matches, and replace only the affected bootlist/setlist identity. The unidentifiedShows.txt recovery branch prompts for the already-moved destination and performs inventory repair without moving/renaming the filesystem object. Batch Path ----> Folder Name lines use the same rules. Tag changes, when enabled, happen before final inventory commit and are not rolled back if a later commit fails, so failures must disclose that fact.

Copy Requests is opened from the hamburger menu and is independent of Full Inventory, Tag, Add New Shows, and Manual Updates. The New Copy Request input is labeled Path(s) and uses the same semicolon-separated entry and optional matching-double-quote rules as the main GUI Path(s) field. Path(s) may mix plain request text, direct filesystem path/volume items, and .txt request files in one expression; repeated native-Windows drag/drop appends one or more dropped folders/.txt files instead of replacing the existing value. A .txt entry is expanded immediately when a new request is created using the toBeInventoried.txt blank-line/#/REM whole-line comment convention. Its usable lines are inserted into the request aggregate at that entry position and persisted under TLOHome/copyRequests so later Continue/Process All passes do not require the source .txt file to remain accessible or unchanged. An aggregated request item may contain an exact Show, Artist, Artist + single date/year, Artist + increasing year range using the established yy-yy wraparound rule, or a direct filesystem path/volume item. A rooted path, [Volume], or [Volume] path is direct-copy syntax. A bare visible volume label is direct-copy syntax only when it does not also match an Artist/alias or exact Show expression; a collision is ambiguous, is reported in Preview/reporting, and must be written explicitly as [Volume] to request a whole-volume copy.

Direct directory trees retain their source leaf name at Destination; an entire-volume item uses the volume label as its Destination folder name. Whole-volume safety is determined from the resolved source, not request spelling: [Volume], a bare unambiguous volume label, and a direct path that resolves to a connected volume/mount root all exclude operating-system-managed root entries that TLO cannot safely or meaningfully reproduce (Windows System Volume Information and $RECYCLE.BIN; macOS .Spotlight-V100, .fseventsd, .Trashes, and .TemporaryItems). The same exclusion set must be used by free-space sizing, copying, and verification, and Preview/reporting must state that the exclusions apply.

A Copy Request Destination must not be the same path as a requested source, inside that source, or an ancestor containing that source. Source/target identity is never treated as Already Satisfied or Complete; it is reported as a no-copy failure so a request cannot complete without creating the requested second copy. When a direct tree contains inventoried Shows, TLO records those Shows in the same completed-Show tracking used by ordinary request matches, so mixed path/volume and Artist/date/Show items are de-conflicted in the same pass and on later passes. The direct item itself is also persistently recorded so Continue does not recopy it.

Direct items and ordinary matched folders participate together in the complete current-pass free-space preflight. For Path(s)-based requests, state persists under TLOHome/copyRequests per normalized Path(s) expression plus Destination; the expanded aggregate request specification is stored in the request directory and is the authoritative input for future passes. TLO determines whether an already-saved request exists from the Path(s) expression and Destination before attempting to reopen any contributing .txt file, so an existing request remains reopenable after a list file is moved or deleted. Legacy requests created by older builds from one Request File remain readable for compatibility. Completed Shows are not recopied. Copying preserves the complete eligible source folder/tree, never retags/renames/moves/deletes the source, and never exposes a partial copied tree under the final Show/volume folder name. For each planned copy TLO first reserves the final destination name without overwriting an existing directory, copies into a uniquely named sibling .tlo-copy-* temporary tree carrying a TLO ownership marker, verifies that temporary tree byte-for-byte, and only then publishes it under the final name. Immediately before a Copy Request copies a source tree, TLO must recheck for symbolic links. The copy operation must preserve any link that appears after that check rather than dereferencing its target; the completed temporary tree must be rejected if it contains a symbolic link. Exact tree comparison must compare symbolic links as links using their link target text, not as the bytes of the linked-to file or directory.

A failed reservation must never delete or modify the directory that caused the reservation failure. On handled copy/verification/finalization failure, TLO removes only its own temporary tree and may remove only its own still-empty reservation; it must never recursively delete a destination target. At pass start, stale .tlo-copy-* trees are removed only when the TLO ownership marker is present; an unmarked similarly named user folder is left alone. Existing non-identical collisions are never overwritten/merged; already-identical destination content at a distinct target is treated as satisfied. Requests are Open until complete or explicitly Closed.

REQ-COPY-001  Copy Request destination/source overlap is prohibited in either direction, source-as-target is never “Already Satisfied”, and a foreign pre-existing destination entry is never deleted or overwritten.

REQ-COPY-002  Each copy pass is a recoverable transaction. Before reserving a target, TLO must persist the pending source, target, temporary tree, and phase in that request state. The pass must hold an exclusive request lock and an exclusive Destination lock. Owner identity must include hostname, PID, and a process-start identity when the platform exposes one so PID reuse cannot make a stale owner appear live. On Windows, PID liveness must use Windows process APIs rather than os.kill(pid, 0); on POSIX, an EPERM/PermissionError existence check is treated as alive. A later pass may recover only a reservation or temporary tree explicitly recorded by that request and owned by TLO; it must not sweep another live pass merely because a name begins with .tlo-copy-. A same-host dead-owner lock is stale. A different-host Destination lock becomes eligible for user-confirmed clearing only after the configured stale-age threshold; the GUI must show the recorded owner host and approximate age and require explicit confirmation before clearing it.

REQ-COPY-003  Copy data must be written to a TLO-owned temporary sibling, verified, and only then published under the final folder name. The ownership marker remains through publish until completion state is persisted. If TLO is interrupted after publish but before completion state is finalized, the next pass must recognize the owned verified tree without deleting foreign data.

REQ-COPY-004  Copy Requests must provide Cancel Copy while a copy pass is active. Cancellation is checked between files, cleans only the current TLO-owned pending transaction, preserves previously completed items, leaves the request Open, and reports cancellation as a user action rather than a copy failure.

REQ-COPY-006  The New Copy Request Path(s) field must use the same semicolon/optional-double-quote splitting rules and repeated native-Windows drag/drop append behavior as the main GUI Path(s) field. It may mix direct paths/volumes, ordinary Artist/date/Show request text, and .txt request-list files. Each .txt input must be expanded exactly once at request creation using blank-line/#/REM whole-line comment filtering. A direct filesystem path item ending in * must also be expanded exactly once at request creation before copying begins: a form such as C:\TLO* selects every immediate directory in C:\ whose name begins with TLO, while C:\TLO\* selects every immediate child directory of C:\TLO and does not select C:\TLO itself. Only directories are selected; regular files and symbolic-link directories are not wildcard matches. The same trailing-* expansion applies to request lines obtained from .txt inputs. If the wildcard parent cannot be accessed or the wildcard matches no directories, request creation must fail with a clear error rather than saving an unresolved wildcard. The resulting ordered aggregate of plain items, expanded .txt items, and expanded wildcard paths must be persisted before copying begins and must be sufficient for all later Preview, Continue, Process All, report, and resume operations without rereading the source .txt files; later operations must also use the persisted wildcard expansion without re-expanding wildcard paths. An existing request identity must be resolved from the original Path(s) expression plus Destination before any source .txt file or wildcard source is revisited, so a saved request remains reopenable if those original inputs later move, disappear, or change.

REQ-COPY-007  Copy Request state directories are authoritative for deletion identity. Request IDs must match the strict [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ allowlist and must not equal the special path components "." or "..". When state.json is loaded, its request_id must exactly equal the containing request-directory name. The GUI delete action must use the directory ID discovered during request listing rather than trusting state.json for the deletion path. Before recursive deletion, TLO must resolve the candidate target and prove that its resolved parent is exactly the resolved TLOHome/copyRequests root; malformed IDs, traversal, absolute paths, path separators, mismatched state IDs, and symlink escapes must fail closed.

Redundancy Groups is opened from the hamburger menu and stores ordered equivalence declarations in TLOHome/redundancyGroups.txt using A = B = C syntax. A visible volume label may appear in only one group. Declaration order is source precedence. Paths with spaces do not require quotes in redundancy declarations. For a requested Show inventoried on any group member, Copy Requests tests the same rootless path on connected equivalent members in declaration order and uses the first valid non-symlink source. Redundancy Groups affect Copy Request source resolution only; they do not create inventory rows or change normal duplicate detection. The editor-dismiss button is labeled Close.

tlo-search shall resolve TLOHome from --TLOHome (including the retained hidden compatibility alias) or the TLOHome environment variable; if none is supplied, it must fail clearly rather than use a developer-specific default path and requires readable bootlist.csv/setlists paths as applicable. Normal search reads the two positional bootlist columns and honors a leading sep= delimiter declaration; an empty normal search returns all rows. Deep search requires a non-empty term and searches setlist text under TLOHome/setlists. Search expressions support case-insensitive |AND| and |OR| with parentheses and quoted outer-term stripping. --find supplies the initial query; otherwise a nonempty [search] search_query is used, then clipboard text if clipboard_prefill=true (default). An explicit clipboard_prefill=false prevents startup clipboard access. Existing INI preferences are never automatically overwritten. Result View derives the normal setlist filename directly from Show, enforces the confirmation/open-count limits, and reports missing/unreadable inputs without terminating the application. When opening a normal-search result, tlo-search must call the shared inventory/postprocess setlist filename creator directly. Supported partial date tokens such as 1973-12-xx must therefore retain the same internal dashes as the originally exported .txt filename. Search version reporting must derive from the central tlo_version module rather than a separate internal version constant. Search View SHALL resolve an exported setlist by both Show and exact VolumePath through a maintained setlist-index.json sidecar; with multiple identical Show rows and no trusted row identity, View SHALL not guess a filename. bootlist.csv remains two columns. Unquoted apostrophes and parenthesized show qualifiers SHALL be accepted literally. Explicit |AND| and |OR| grouping SHALL remain supported; excessively deep/long expressions shall produce a readable search-expression error without recursion failure.

search-artist-db shall resolve TLOHome from --TLOHome or TLOHome, open TLOHome/TLO_DBs/artists.sqlite, and search the terms table by exact case-insensitive term_text. A blank query reports that a search term is required. No matching artist reports no results. Matching artists are listed by master name and their associated master/alias terms in term order. Missing database and SQLite errors are reported in readable GUI messages without crashing unrelated TLO state.

The main Full Inventory console shall be a non-wrapping text area with its existing vertical scrolling plus a horizontal scrollbar along the bottom. Long paths/log lines must remain on one line and be horizontally scrollable.

REQ-ADDSHOW-DELETE-001  Add Shows backup/replacement cleanup uses deleteReplacedFolders.bat on Windows and deleteBackupFolders.sh elsewhere. Targets are derived only from a bootlist row retaining its recorded volume identity and a canonical rooted path. Literal .. components, bare drive/mount roots, drive-relative forms such as E:, and TLOHome or ancestors of TLOHome are rejected; a deletion target must be at least one directory below a recognized root. Windows .bat entries display the recorded source label in [Volume Label] format ([] for unlabeled) and fully quote each rooted target path. For each labeled entry, the batch file MUST compare the current drive volume label to the recorded label immediately before allowing deletion; a mismatch, disconnected drive, unavailable PowerShell/label probe, or empty actual label MUST skip that entry. Labels are encoded for the runtime comparison so cmd.exe punctuation, percent signs and Unicode cannot change control flow. Windows scripts MUST emit no active delete command for an unlabeled entry; instead show a SKIPPED/manual-verification line and a disabled example command. The recorded volume need not be connected at script generation time. Each active entry MUST derive the checked drive letter and the rmdir target from one editable TLO_DELETE_TARGET assignment, so changing the drive letter cannot cause the guard to check a different drive. The expected label is encoded; to target a different labeled backup drive, regenerate that entry rather than changing only the displayed comment. The batch output must disable delayed expansion, encode literal percent signs as %%, quote all deletion paths, and write CRLF line endings. For the POSIX .sh variant, WSL /mnt/<drive> roots must check the Windows volume label using powershell.exe before considering findmnt; other platforms may use their native exact-label mechanism. No generated command may weaken canonical delete-target safety checks.

REQ-ADDSHOW-DELETE-002  A new Add Shows session must not append silently to cleanup commands from an older session. When a prior deleteBackupFolders script exists and the user chooses Continue, TLO archives that script under TLOHome/logs with a timestamp and starts a fresh session script. For the POSIX deleteBackupFolders.sh variant, every active destructive command must retain a verifiable expected volume identity and check it at execution time before deletion; a mismatch or inability to verify the volume aborts rather than deleting. If the recorded volume is unlabeled and no stronger identity is available, TLO must not emit an active rm -rf command for that entry. It must emit a non-destructive skipped/manual-verification entry, with any example delete command disabled as a comment until the user manually verifies and enables it. Windows deleteReplacedFolders.bat MUST provide the same per-entry fail-closed identity protection specified in REQ-ADDSHOW-DELETE-001; one mismatch skips that deletion without silently authorizing any other deletion.

Per-item POSIX cleanup volume verification. Generated POSIX cleanup scripts skip and report each wrong or unverifiable volume instead of aborting the entire list. They continue to later valid entries, preserve existing label safeguards and report deleted/skipped counts.

TLO Main and Search SHALL create or read only TLOHome/tlo-preferences.ini at startup and preserve an existing file. The Edit Preferences hamburger command SHALL validate all supplied values before an atomic save; the editor buttons SHALL be “Save & Close” and “Cancel”. Save & Close SHALL save the validated file, close the editor and advise that restart is required. Cancel SHALL leave the INI unchanged and request confirmation before discarding unsaved edits. After any save, the running application SHALL continue with exactly its currently selected settings (including fonts, options, paths and operational switches), independent of the edited INI; only a subsequent launch SHALL read the updated defaults. The configuration sections are [general], [main], [search], [manual_updates], and [add_new_shows]. [general] update_downloads = msi | zip defaults to msi and controls Windows update downloads independently of MSI/ZIP installation origin; missing keys and missing INIs default to MSI. Explicit command-line options SHALL override saved startup defaults. No Startup Profiles menu or preset selection/writer SHALL exist.

Consistent INI syntax and Auto Update writes. Preferences accept both = and : assignments, preserve inline comments and unknown user text during validated atomic saves, and keep the Auto Update toggle consistent with grammar accepted by the editor.

Safe corruption defaults for new installations. New installations default to Keep and report for corrupt files and Never remove folders. Existing preferences and explicit deletion choices remain unchanged. Tagging and Deep Audio controls retain their semantics.
Startup preference behavior: editing tlo-preferences.ini SHALL NOT change the running app. Changes apply after restarting Main and Search.
The Startup Profiles feature has been retired. Main SHALL NOT expose profiles or any profile selection, saving, or application flow.

Trap Ctrl-C. When Ctrl-C occurs during active inventory scanning or worker execution, request cancellation, terminate the active path-worker pool before log deletion when one exists, delete only tokenized logs whose tokens were newly allocated by the interrupted run, and exit cleanly. Tokens reused from an earlier inventory must never be deleted wholesale during cancellation.
Trap the Quit button.
Before inventory starts, Quit closes the GUI normally and no logs are deleted.

During active inventory scanning or worker execution, Quit must request cancellation, terminate the active path-worker pool before log deletion when one exists, delete only tokenized logs whose tokens were newly allocated by the interrupted run, close/destroy the GUI window, and exit the process so child workers cannot continue writing logs after the GUI closes. Reused pre-existing log tokens are not cancellation-cleanup targets. When scanning has finished but cleanup, sibling-collection aggregation, or output generation is still active, the GUI must warn before a forced exit that an in-progress collection move can be interrupted and that TLO will attempt journal-based automatic rollback on the next normal Inventory run.
The implementation must delete logs only after the worker-pool termination request has been issued, so workers do not recreate or continue writing tokenized logs after cleanup.

If the active inventory is running serially rather than in a process pool, Quit must still request cancellation, delete only newly allocated active-run tokenized logs, and exit the process. Reused tokens remain intact.

After inventory scanning has completed, Quit must not delete completed logs. If cleanup, aggregation, or output generation is still running, allow that work to finish unless the user confirms forced exit. After postprocess completion, Quit closes the GUI normally.

Missing TLOHome startup errors in Main and Search SHALL say "TLO can't start - TLOHome is not set" and explain that TLOHome locates settings and database files. The same setup guidance SHALL provide a fully qualified Windows example such as "C:\.tlo\apps\Windows\tlo-main.exe" --TLOHome "C:\.tlo" and instructions to retain the existing executable in shortcut Properties > Target while appending --TLOHome; Linux/WSL example "/mnt/c/.tlo/apps/Linux/tlo-main" --TLOHome "/mnt/c/.tlo"; the TLOHome environment-variable alternative; replacement-of-example-path guidance; and https://traderslittleorganizer.com for Installation and Quick Start. Examples SHALL use the entry point actually launched (Main vs Search, Tag, Inventory CLI etc.). GUI instructions SHALL be readable, selectable, scrollable and offer Copy Instructions; on systems without a display, print the full guidance to stderr. Missing TLOHome SHALL prevent Main from continuing into an unusable GUI. Supplied but invalid home paths SHALL continue to fail validation. This requirement concerns messages and startup behavior only, not --myTLO/--TLOHome/environment precedence.
After the inventory phase finishes, print a console message stating that cleanup, aggregation, and output generation still need to run.
After cleanup, aggregation, and output generation finish, print a console message stating that cleanup, aggregation, and output generation are complete.
In GUI mode, errors must not be written only to a console window that closes before they can be read.

The selected-setlist metadata header reader is an untrusted-input path and must follow the same bounded-read policy: reject text files larger than 16 MiB and read at most a 1 MiB sample because only the first 100 usable metadata lines are consumed. It must not read the entire file and then discard the remainder.

Files encountered in scanned collection trees are untrusted input. Ordinary text sampling must read no more than 1 MiB from disk before decoding and applying any smaller character-sample limit. A requested full ordinary-text read larger than 16 MiB must be rejected with a readable outcome instead of loading the complete file into memory. Every later full read of a selected plain-text/RTF/DOCX setlist, including Tag, descriptor/date fallback, sibling aggregation, and duplicate review, must use the same bounded reader. Oversized ordinary-text candidates must be disqualified before selection. Text decoding must use the shared reader. BOM-marked UTF-16 and NUL-dominant BOM-less UTF-16 LE/BE must be recognized before UTF-8 because NUL bytes are legal UTF-8. Otherwise clean UTF-8/UTF-8-sig is preferred. A bounded sample ending inside a UTF-8 multibyte character must retain the valid UTF-8 prefix instead of causing the whole sample to fall back to a single-byte encoding. If a file contains valid UTF-8 plus isolated legacy bytes, valid UTF-8 spans must remain intact while only invalid bytes fall back to cp1252/latin-1. RTF and DOCX selected setlists must be decoded through the same shared bounded reader rather than as raw container/control bytes. RTF hexadecimal and Unicode character escapes must be decoded before RTF control words are stripped so accented artist, venue, and location text is preserved.

For DOCX setlist candidates, inspect the ZipInfo.file_size of word/document.xml before reading or decompressing it. Reject the candidate when the uncompressed entry exceeds 16 MiB. Missing, corrupt, encrypted, oversized, binary-like, or otherwise unreadable candidates must be treated as unusable input, reported with the affected path when practical, and must not stop unrelated roots or shows from being processed.

REQ-TEXT-001  RTF setlist conversion must be group-aware: destination groups such as font/color/style/info/picture/header/footer metadata are skipped; \ansicpgN, \ucN, \uN and hexadecimal character escapes are honored; \par, \line, and TextEdit backslash-newline boundaries become line breaks; \tab becomes a space; and escaped braces/backslashes are decoded without leaking control syntax into Artist/Venue/Location evidence. Symbol controls must preserve text semantics: \lquote and \rquote become apostrophes; \ldblquote and \rdblquote become double quotes; \emdash and \endash become a hyphen; \~ becomes a space; \_ becomes a hyphen; \- emits nothing; \emspace, \enspace, and \qmspace become spaces; and \bullet is retained for later normalization. Legacy binary .doc files are not decoded as text and are treated as unsupported.
On macOS, paths passed to osascript for Trash/Recycle Bin operations must be passed as argv/data rather than interpolated into AppleScript source text.

The duplicate-cleanup FLAC full-decode validator must use a finite per-file timeout of 180 seconds. A timeout is unverifiable, not healthy or corrupt; if a kept folder contains an unverifiable FLAC, do not relocate that duplicate cluster.

REQ-CANCEL-001  External requests, interprocess coordination waits, and converter invocations must use finite timeouts. The setlist.fm state location, atomic-write rules, 20-second reservation-lock deadline, normal/upgraded request spacing and quota are canonical in Appendix I. SHN/SHNF conversion uses a maximum per-file runtime of 30 minutes. A timeout must produce a readable observation or error and allow processing to continue when the affected operation is optional. GUI-worker marshaling waits must also use a finite deadline; if a scheduled Tk callback cannot complete before the deadline, the worker must fail with the existing GUI-closed/startup error rather than wait indefinitely. Lock-status probes must not create directories or modify lock-file contents, and lock acquisition must tolerate a brief transient probe collision before reporting the lock busy.

Transactional update-package validation. A downloaded update must pass signed-asset size/hash checks and archive inspection while staged under a non-release filename. Only a validated file may receive its official Downloads name. An unrelated same-named user file is never overwritten. Failure removes the staged file.

TLO imposes no application-specific fixed ceiling on the number of search roots, show groups, music folders, or media files. Practical capacity is determined by the selected performance mode, configured worker cap, available memory, filesystem performance, and platform limits. Path length and directory depth are subject to the host operating system and filesystem; path-too-long, inaccessible, or malformed-path failures must be reported for the affected item without crashing unrelated roots.

Intentional best-effort broad exception boundaries must not silently pass. Record suppressed exceptions at debug level, narrow the exception type where practical, and surface update-settings persistence failures in the update-check result so a read-only/full TLOHome does not fail quietly.

Section: 17. Test Suite Architecture and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The regression suite shall separate fast unit checks, executable behavior checks, multi-module integration scenarios, source/document/release contracts, and GUI checks into tests/unit, tests/behavior, tests/integration, and tests/contracts.

Section: 17. Test Suite Architecture and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Source-text and documentation assertions remain valid contract tests, but they shall not be presented as behavioral assurance.

Section: 17. Test Suite Architecture and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Important application behavior shall be tested by executing functions or workflows rather than only inspecting source text.

Section: 17. Test Suite Architecture and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Every test module must carry exactly one category marker from unit, behavior, contract, or integration. Trait markers such as gui and slow may be added in addition. The suite must contain and use both gui and slow, and a contract test must enforce category-marker coverage across tests/.

Section: 17. Test Suite Architecture and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The suite shall register and use the pytest markers contract, gui, integration, slow, behavior, and unit. Unknown-marker warnings are not acceptable.

Section: 17. Test Suite Architecture and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Tk-dependent regression modules must be skipped cleanly before module import when tkinter is not installed, so a minimal Python installation still runs the non-GUI suite without collection failures. Individual GUI tests may also use pytest.importorskip("tkinter", reason="Tkinter is required for GUI regression tests"). Tests that execute Tk widgets may skip when no graphical display is available; the Linux CI build shall execute them under Xvfb. Worker-thread completion callbacks scheduled onto Tk must treat both tkinter.TclError and RuntimeError indicating that the main thread is no longer in the Tk main loop as an ordinary closed-window/shutdown condition; those shutdown races must not emit daemon-thread tracebacks.

Section: 17. Test Suite Architecture and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Behavioral and integration tests must exercise real parser, metadata, copy/verification, GUI-state, and mutation paths rather than relying only on source-text inspection. Pure predicates should receive focused unit coverage where practical, and regressions involving malformed/untrusted input must include executable fixtures that reproduce the relevant boundary condition.

Section: 17. Test Suite Architecture and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Behavioral coverage shall execute the shared progress-indicator interval, the actual checkbox grid positions, command-line parsing, Artist in Album tag behavior, parenthetical preservation, and exact runSettings.log output.

Section: 17. Test Suite Architecture and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The integration category shall contain at least ten small synthetic filesystem or workflow scenarios covering grouping, unrelated-sibling blocking, rename path propagation, same-filesystem Copy/Delete moves without size checks, cross-filesystem Copy/Delete verification, ordinary Tag Copy verification, dry-run non-modification, Add Shows, and labeled-volume re-inventory replacement. Transfer coverage must include nested non-music files and empty descendant directories for same-filesystem moves, cross-filesystem Copy/Delete Original, and ordinary Tag Copy.

Section: 17. Test Suite Architecture and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: Synthetic audio placeholders and mocked Mutagen/conversion operations may be used when real encoded audio is not necessary to exercise the workflow.

Section: 17. Test Suite Architecture and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: tlo_version.py is the authoritative release-version/summary source. Per-module stale package-version comments and duplicated __version_summary__ strings must not be carried forward. Application/source modules may retain a simple __version__ stamp when required by release contracts, but pytest test modules and test infrastructure must not carry independent __version__ stamps. Tests that open current versioned source-bundle artifacts must derive those filenames from tlo_version.VERSION rather than hard-code the current build number.

Section: 17. Test Suite Architecture and Execution Requirements
Requirement_Text: The flat source-bundle root shall retain test_tlo_requirements.py as a backward-compatibility subset entry point for the current separately versioned TLO GitHub Build Process and historical/direct callers. It must not be used as the sole official release-test gate. The official release process shall run the full categorized pytest suite by source-root discovery, including current build-specific regression modules, with the compatibility subset retained only for backward compatibility.

The release shall include tlo-deleteDupes.py as a console main. It shall accept one required positional Input Path plus --TLOHome and the compatibility alias --myTLO. TLOHome resolution shall use the same shared resolution logic as the other mains. The Input Path shall be rejected unless it is a fully qualified, existing, readable directory path.

The utility shall search the Input Path recursively and analyze same-parent sibling directories. Candidate discovery shall combine two rules. First, an exact copy family consists of folders whose names reduce to the same base when a terminal case-insensitive (copyN) or (copy N) suffix is removed; X, X (copy2), and X (copy3) therefore belong to one candidate family, and numbered copies shall be compared with one another even when X is absent or has different contents. Second, folders whose normalized artist and date are identical shall be candidate siblings even when the remaining folder-name text differs. Same-artist/date discovery shall recognize a standalone four-digit 19xx/20xx year, a yyyy-mm-dd style date with numeric or xx month/day components, and a four-digit-year to four-digit-year range. An unknown date without an actual four-digit year shall not broaden candidate discovery. Candidate discovery alone shall never establish that two folders are duplicates.

Before moving any candidate into the duplicates holding folder, the utility shall compare the complete recursive manifests of all folders in each same-parent discovery component. A duplicate match requires the same relative directory structure, including empty nested directories, and the same relative file names and file sizes throughout the entire tree. The duplicate-cleanup comparison intentionally does not hash or compare file bytes and does not use timestamps, ownership, permissions, or other filesystem metadata. Symbolic links and unsupported filesystem objects shall be rejected; no link targets are followed. Folders with identical manifests shall form a content-equivalence cluster, so copies are compared with one another in addition to being compared with unsuffixed folders. Each cluster containing two or more identical trees shall keep exactly one folder and relocate the remaining cluster members. Prefer an unsuffixed folder as the keeper when one exists; if more than one unsuffixed folder is identical, keep the alphabetically first name without regard to case. If a cluster contains only numbered copy folders, keep the lowest-numbered copy, with alphabetical order as the final tie-breaker. Folders in different content-equivalence clusters remain in place as separate masters/variants. Thus, if X differs from X (copy2) and X (copy3), but copy2 and copy3 match one another, X and copy2 remain while copy3 is relocated. Iterative traversal is mandatory; Python call-stack recursion is not permitted for folder-tree comparison.

Full FLAC decode validation must use a finite 180-second per-file timeout. Timeout means unverifiable; an unverifiable FLAC in the kept folder blocks relocation of that duplicate cluster and is reported to the user.

After a content-equivalence cluster contains two or more identical trees under 18.3, and before any duplicate member of that cluster is moved into the duplicates holding folder, tlo-deleteDupes shall recursively validate every regular .flac file in the selected keeper directory tree. Validation SHALL decode the complete FLAC audio stream using the application-bundled LGPL FFmpeg PCM path, calculate its full decoded PCM MD5, verify the STREAMINFO MD5 and declared sample count when available, and require successful decoder completion. A failed fingerprint or incomplete decode proves corruption; an unset/all-zero STREAMINFO MD5 or infrastructure failure is unverifiable and cannot authorize relocation. Validation must explicitly select the FLAC demuxer (-f flac) and restrict input protocols to file only; renamed non-FLAC content must not be accepted through ffmpeg content probing. A successful tag/header read alone is not sufficient. When MD5 is unset, emit the actual FLAC pathname and missing-MD5 reason and preserve all duplicate candidates; the user may compare separately backed-up re-encodes. Do not misreport this case as a timeout.

For each corrupt FLAC in the selected keeper directory, the utility shall look for the same relative FLAC path in the other members of that same content-equivalence cluster. Copy-suffixed repair sources shall retain ascending numeric copy order (copy1, copy2, copy3, and so on). Qualifying unsuffixed repair sources shall be considered alphabetically without regard to case. A candidate FLAC may be used as a replacement only if its complete FLAC stream validates successfully. Folders in a different content-equivalence cluster shall not be used as repair sources and shall remain outside that cluster's relocation set.

When a healthy replacement is found, tlo-deleteDupes shall copy it to a temporary file in the keeper's directory and byte-verify that staged copy before any keeper replacement. Before installation, the utility shall create a backup of the existing keeper and verify that backup by both size and SHA-256 against the pre-repair keeper snapshot. A backup that is partial, unreadable, or otherwise unverifiable must never be restored over the keeper. Only after the staged source and keeper backup are verified may the staged source replace the keeper atomically. The installed replacement shall be byte-verified and decoded again. If post-install verification fails, rollback may use only the previously verified keeper backup. A staging-copy, backup-copy, or installation failure that occurs before installation completes must leave the original keeper bytes unchanged. Every duplicate member of that content-equivalence cluster remains intact until repair attempts for its keeper have completed.

If no healthy replacement can be found, or a replacement cannot be installed successfully, the utility shall report the unrepaired corrupt FLAC and leave that entire content-equivalence cluster in place for later review. No member of a cluster may be relocated while the selected keeper still contains an unrepaired corrupt FLAC. The selected keeper directory itself shall never be moved. An unverifiable keeper validation, including timeout, file-open or permission failure, I/O/resource failure, or validator-infrastructure failure, is handled the same fail-closed way: preserve the entire cluster in place and do not classify the file as corrupt merely because it could not be opened or validated. A missing validator return code is validator-infrastructure failure and is therefore unverifiable, never healthy. The ffmpeg validation subprocess should use a stable C locale for diagnostic classification where the platform honors LC_ALL.

For the filesystem/partition containing the Input Path, tlo-deleteDupes shall use a folder named duplicates at the root of the partition. If that folder does not exist, the utility shall create it before moving qualifying duplicates. On Windows this is the drive/share root (for example E:\\duplicates). On Linux and macOS this is the mounted-filesystem root containing the Input Path (for example /mnt/music/duplicates or /Volumes/Music/duplicates). When and only when a folder is a non-keeper member of a content-equivalence cluster, that duplicate directory shall be moved as one complete directory tree into the holding folder; the utility shall not enumerate or move child files individually. Keeper selection shall prefer an unsuffixed folder when possible, but an unsuffixed folder is not globally sacrosanct: a different content cluster may keep a numbered copy when that is the only representative of that variant. The utility shall not overwrite an existing holding-folder entry: when the same directory name already exists in duplicates, use a collision-safe suffix such as (moved 2), (moved 3), and so on. If the Input Path includes the partition root, the utility shall exclude the duplicates holding folder from duplicate discovery so previously moved material is not analyzed again. After each successful move, the utility shall append the full pre-move source path of that duplicate directory to TLOHome/deletedDirs.txt and flush the log. Non-matching, singleton-cluster, or unverifiable candidates shall be left in place and shall not be logged.

When two folders in the same discovery component are compared and their recursive manifests differ, tlo-deleteDupes shall append one simple CSV record to TLOHome/deleteDupesMismatches.txt. Copies shall therefore be compared with one another as well as with unsuffixed candidates. Each record shall contain: folder name, folder name, simple reason. Only the directory names shall be recorded, not full paths. Folder names containing commas shall be CSV-quoted. Reasons shall remain concise and use forms such as different number of files, different sub-structure, different file names, or <relative-file-name> different sizes. The mismatch log is separate from deletedDirs.txt, which remains limited to folders actually moved into the duplicates holding folder.

If Ctrl-C is invoked, the utility shall stop further scanning/move work, unwind through the open deletedDirs.txt and deleteDupesMismatches.txt contexts so both log files are closed, report cancellation, and return exit status 130. Any entries successfully logged before the interrupt remain in their respective log files; any duplicate directory already moved into the partition-root duplicates folder remains there.

The Windows onefile and shared-onedir distributions, generic Linux distribution, and macOS distribution shall include the tlo-deleteDupes functionality with the same checksum-pinned FFmpeg 9.0.2 executable used by SHN conversion. Windows tlo-deleteDupes.cmd shall carry that executable inside its adjacent private embedded-Python runtime under tlo_ffmpeg_bin. Linux/macOS and local Windows PyInstaller packaging shall add the exact prepared ffmpeg binary directly. send2trash is not required by tlo-deleteDupes because qualifying duplicate directories are moved into the partition-root duplicates holding folder.

Native release builds shall use CPython 3.13.16 and the exact hashed dependency lock in requirements-build.txt. PyInstaller shall be exactly 6.22.3; build scripts shall fail closed when the interpreter or required native-build dependency versions differ. The official GitHub process shall install the lock with --require-hashes, run Ruff from the pinned environment, and run pip-audit 2.10.1 in an isolated temporary environment whose complete runtime closure is separately pinned and hashed in requirements-audit.txt. The audit environment shall verify CPython 3.13.16's ensurepip bootstrap, install the audit closure with dependency resolution disabled and hashes required, run pip check, verify the audit-tool version, and run pip-audit with pip subprocess use disabled. The audit helper shall remove inherited PIP_* configuration from its subprocess environment and shall use pip --isolated for pip installation and consistency checks. Before it audits a requested build lock, it shall audit requirements-audit.txt itself with strict, hash-required, no-dependency, pip-disabled settings. Because PEP 508 platform markers are host-sensitive, the helper shall also audit a marker-neutral exact-pin view of the requested lock so Windows-only and macOS-only pinned packages are checked even when the audit runs on another platform. When the local Windows packaging script performs Authenticode signing, it shall select signtool.exe only from the installed Windows Kits x64 toolchain, require the SignTool binary itself to have a valid Microsoft Authenticode signature, record its exact path, SHA-256, file version, signature status, and signer in the tool receipt, and verify every signed executable with signtool verify /pa /all /v before malware scanning. Each platform build shall record Python, PyInstaller, FFmpeg, and dependency-lock identity in its build receipt. Any local verification represented as a release verification run shall use the pinned release dependency environment from requirements-build.txt, shall set TLO_RELEASE_VERIFY=1 for the full pytest run, and shall fail if Ruff is unavailable. A non-release developer run may skip the Ruff regression test when Ruff is unavailable, but any verification record for that run must state that lint was not attested. If any required release-gate tool or release-gate check was unavailable or did not execute, the verification record heading shall include "NOT RELEASE-ATTESTED"; a passing pytest count alone shall not be presented as a complete release attestation.

The release shall include tlo-research.py as a standalone console main. It shall accept one required research input string. The string may be supplied as one quoted command-line argument or as multiple positional words that are joined with spaces. It shall accept --TLOHome and the compatibility alias --myTLO. TLOHome precedence shall use the shared rule: --myTLO, then --TLOHome, then the TLOHome environment variable. TLOHome must resolve to the same existing writable directory required by the other TLO mains.

The research input shall be classified as one of exactly three forms: a date by itself; an artist name followed by a date; or, when neither of those forms applies, a venue string. Research date classification shall reuse the canonical TLO Inventory date parser rather than a separate Research-only grammar. Therefore every date representation accepted by Inventory shall also be accepted as a Research date, including numeric dates, textual-month dates, compact dates, slash dates, supported year ranges, same-month multi-day ranges such as 1970-04-12-13 and 12-13 April 1970, partial x-placeholder dates such as 2001-04-1x, 2004-0x-xx, 202x-xx-xx, and xxxx-xx-xx, plus a standalone four-digit 19xx/20xx year. Same-month multi-day ranges normalize to their first date. The input date shall be normalized using the same Inventory date rules before matching metadata. If one raw date representation has more than one valid canonical normalization, Research shall retain all canonical interpretations and match a metadata DATE equal to any of them. An empty input shall be rejected. After whitespace normalization, Research input must not exceed 2,048 characters; longer input must fail with a readable query error before date classification. Artist-plus-date classification must examine no more than the trailing 256 characters as a candidate date expression while retaining the existing longest-supported-suffix interpretation within that window.

tlo-research shall search every TLOHome/logs/meta*.log file in case-insensitive filename order and parse complete SHOW_NAME through END_SHOW_METADATA records. If an interrupted historical log begins a new SHOW_NAME record without the prior END_SHOW_METADATA marker, the new SHOW_NAME shall also act as a record boundary so later records remain searchable.

For a date-only query, a metadata record matches when its DATE field equals any canonical normalization of the input, case-insensitively after whitespace normalization. For an artist+date query, the ARTIST field must equal the artist input and the DATE field must equal any canonical normalization of the trailing date expression. For a venue query, the normalized input shall be matched case-insensitively as a substring of the metadata VENUE field. Research shall not treat arbitrary occurrences in OBSERVATION, tag samples, show names, or unrelated fields as venue/date matches.

For every matching metadata record, Research shall correlate related comp*.log path entries using the record's MAIN_DIR_PATH and MUSIC_DIRS_JSON directory values. A comp line is related when its normalized path is the directory itself or a descendant of one of those metadata paths. Blank lines, comments, and SEARCH_PATH header lines are not research results.

The result shall begin with the original research string, interpreted query type, and total number of matching metadata records. Each structured match shall show the source meta log filename, the complete metadata record text, and a COMP LOG section containing every correlated comp entry with its comp log filename. If a matching metadata record has no correlated comp entry, the result shall say so explicitly. If no metadata records match, the result shall state that no matching metadata records were found. Research shall then perform a second exhaustive raw-line pass across every meta*.log and comp*.log file and shall not stop after the first matching record or first matching line. There shall be no per-file or per-query hit cap. A raw line is related when it contains the complete normalized research input, or when it contains the query evidence appropriate to the interpreted type: any canonical date candidate for a date query; the normalized artist plus any canonical date candidate on the same line for an artist+date query; or the normalized venue text for a venue query. The output shall include an ALL RELATED RAW LOG LINES section containing every such occurrence with the source log filename, one-based line number, and complete original log line. This raw-line section shall still be produced when there are zero structured metadata matches so historical/source evidence outside SHOW_NAME metadata blocks remains discoverable.

The standalone tlo-research application shall write the complete formatted result to standard output and use standard error plus a nonzero status for startup/query errors. Ctrl-C shall stop the operation and return status 130.

The Research button behavior defined in Section 14.4 shall call the same shared research implementation used by tlo-research.py. The GUI shall not maintain a separate search/parser implementation. This ensures that identical TLOHome content and input produce the same research result in the CLI and GUI.

tlo-research shall be included as a console application in Windows onefile, Windows shared-onedir, generic Linux, and macOS distributions and in both complete and update release packages. The source publication shall include tlo-research.py and tlo_research_lib.py. The test suite shall cover query classification, field-aware metadata matching, comp correlation, exhaustive raw meta/comp line capture without early exit, raw-hit behavior when no structured metadata record matches, TLOHome precedence, CLI console output/error behavior, GUI Research button/input/results behavior, Research default-button keyboard activation, results Ctrl-A, results Search/Ctrl-F, forward/backward find direction and wraparound, and platform packaging contracts.

False state-word matches inside ordinary album titles must not qualify as location evidence when unexplained trailing text remains. Example: A Spanner In The Works remains an album fallback rather than being interpreted as Indiana.

For a date-bearing non-compliant show folder, descendant music reached only through recognized media/source/supplemental components must remain part of that dated logical show rather than becoming a second show solely because the descendant contains audio. Covered examples include EXTRAS/bonus/source folders, Source 2 EXTRAS, Right Channel (Soundboard Feed), Open Mic Lithium, art-docs/documentation/pictures, Concert Pictures/Video, Disc 1/Flac, and Disc end tracks. Promotion to the dated show root must fail closed when a descendant component contains its own complete performance date, when sampled FLAC Artist/AlbumArtist evidence materially conflicts with the dated root artist, or when another music-bearing descendant below that dated root is a non-supplemental branch such as an opening act. The existing guarded nested-wrapper rule retains priority when its stronger wrapper structure applies.

REQ-CORR-000  Full Inventory and standalone tlo-tag default to Corrupt files = Keep and report and Folder removal = Never (corrupt_files=keep, corrupt_folders=never, threshold=100). Explicit valid deletion choices remain available. These are configured defaults, not defensive fallbacks. If a malformed/incomplete internal caller omits or supplies invalid corruption fields, mutation code must fail closed to Corrupt files = Keep and report, Folder removal = Never, and threshold = 100; an explicitly supplied valid threshold of 0 remains 0.

REQ-CORR-001  Replace the former acceptable corruption % control and --acceptable-corruption-percent CLI option with independent corruption policies. The GUI must show a Corruption Handling group containing Corrupt files with Keep and report / Delete corrupt files choices; Folder removal with Never / 100% corrupt only / At threshold choices; and Folder corruption threshold as an integer 0-100. In the main GUI these three label/control pairs are displayed on one horizontal row beneath the checkbox block. When Corrupt files is Keep and report, Folder removal is effectively Never and both the Folder removal control and Folder corruption threshold control must be disabled/greyed because a report-only corruption policy authorizes no corruption-driven folder removal. When Corrupt files is Delete corrupt files, Folder removal becomes selectable again and the threshold entry is enabled only when At threshold is selected.

REQ-CORR-002  Before any corruption-driven or later rename/tag/copy-delete/SHN mutation, inspect the directly inventoried logical-show audio, including FLAC and MP3 and classify each path as healthy under the selected validation mode, proven corrupt under that mode, or unverifiable. A successfully parsed header alone does not establish that the entire audio stream decodes; optional Deep Audio Check performs a complete decode (REQ-CORR-008/009).
