Compute all corruption counts and percentages from the original pre-removal snapshot. Folder decisions are evaluated before individual-file decisions. Folder removal Never authorizes no corruption-driven folder removal. Folder removal 100% corrupt only authorizes removal when all audio in the evaluated folder population is proven corrupt. Folder removal At threshold authorizes removal when the proven-corruption percentage is greater than or equal to Folder corruption threshold; equality qualifies. The logical-show MAIN_DIR_PATH uses the aggregate logical-show audio population. When the logical show is retained, each directly inventoried physical music directory is evaluated from its own direct-audio population using the same selected folder policy.

REQ-CORR-003  When the logical-show folder is authorized for removal, move MAIN_DIR_PATH to the operating-system Trash/Recycle Bin before considering individual-file handling and omit it from inventory only after that move succeeds. When the logical show remains, qualifying physical music directories may be moved to Trash/Recycle Bin under the selected folder policy. To protect healthy nested material, do not trash a candidate directory when it is an ancestor of another inventoried music directory. Files inside a successfully trashed folder are not separately processed. There is never a permanent-delete fallback.

REQ-CORR-004  Apply the independent Corrupt files policy only to proven-corrupt files that remain after successful folder-level actions. Keep and report retains those files. Delete corrupt files attempts to move remaining proven-corrupt FLAC and MP3 files to operating-system Trash/Recycle Bin without a permanent-delete fallback. A failed whole-show, qualifying music-directory, or individual-file Trash operation must terminate further corruption-driven removal attempts for that show, record an UNVERIFIABLE failure, and suppress subsequent renaming, tagging, copy-delete, and SHN mutation. A failed folder move must never retry as individual-file deletion, regardless of the Corrupt files selection.

REQ-TRASH-001  After successful folder/file Trash operations, remove affected paths from in-memory group and ShowMetadata records so later processing cannot access paths that no longer exist. If a whole-show, music-directory, or individual-file Trash operation fails, log the failed operation, mark the show UNVERIFIABLE, retain the failed target, and stop further Trash actions for that show. Previous successfully trashed paths must still be pruned. There is no permanent-delete fallback.

REQ-CORR-005  Full Inventory Dry Run must not write or restore a probe tag, rename, copy, move, Trash, or delete any files or folders regardless of the selected Corruption Handling policies. A user may enable the read-only Deep Audio Check during Dry Run. The GUI defaults for real runs must remain unchanged (REQ-CORR-000). It must report the selected file and folder policies and whether TLO would Trash the whole logical-show folder, one or more qualifying music folders, Trash individual corrupt files, or keep/report individual corrupt files. Percentage-mode output includes corrupt/total counts and the configured threshold. Regression coverage must include every file-policy/folder-policy combination, threshold equality, all-corrupt and partially corrupt folder cases, no corruption, and folder-Trash failure behavior.

REQ-CORR-006  Corruption evaluation must be separated into a directly testable pre-mutation assessment and a mutation/application stage. The assessment records the original audio snapshot, positively corrupt paths, unverifiable details, aggregate percentage, Corrupt files policy, Folder removal policy, folder threshold, authorized top-level action, and qualifying direct music-directory candidates. The assessment stage performs no Trash/Recycle action. The orchestrator consumes one structured outcome rather than reimplementing the destructive decision inline. The original audio snapshot and percentage denominator include MP3 and FLAC under the same rules.

REQ-CORR-008  Corruption classification always performs the normal audio header/metadata parse. When an actual tagging mode is active, every taggable audio path must additionally prove that its metadata container can accept a temporary TLO-private test tag, persist that value, and then restore the exact prior value (or prior absence) before processing continues. The restored value must be reopened and verified. A tag-format/write failure with no filesystem/resource cause is treated as proven corruption. Permission, I/O, memory/resource, validator-infrastructure, or tag-restoration/verification failure is UNVERIFIABLE and suppresses corruption-driven and later mutation for that logical show. Full Inventory Dry Run must never perform the temporary tag write. When Deep Audio Check is off, non-tagging inventory remains header/metadata validation only; a header failure counts as corruption, while a readable header is not a guarantee of complete-stream integrity. An actual tagging mode additionally tests tag-write/restore; Dry Run does not write tags.

REQ-CORR-009  Deep Audio Check is a default-off main-window checkbox displayed directly beneath Proper Grammar and is also available as --deep-audio-check to inventory and standalone Tag command-line workflows. When selected, corruption classification must decode the complete audio stream of every directly inventoried audio path with TLO's application-bundled ffmpeg after normal header/metadata validation and, during actual tagging, the reversible tag-write probe. The invocation must be noninteractive, restricted to local-file input, and map the first audio stream. A confirmed decoder failure is corruption; missing ffmpeg, cancellation, timeout, permission/access/I/O/resource errors, unexpected tool output, or validator-infrastructure failure is UNVERIFIABLE and suppresses corruption-driven and subsequent mutation. For FLAC with a known, nonzero STREAMINFO total_samples, the complete decoded PCM sample count must exactly match that declared count as well as a successful decoder exit. A clean FFmpeg return code alone is insufficient proof of FLAC completeness: mismatch is corruption. If the FLAC declared count is zero/unknown, or a trustworthy decoded count cannot be obtained, the result is UNVERIFIABLE, never automatically corrupt. Use a bounded, local scratch record of PCM frame durations without writing audio to the collection; interruption and source-file changes during validation must fail closed. For other audio codecs, full decoding still checks readable frames, but a successful decoder exit alone does not guarantee the original recording was complete if the container provides no trustworthy declared total. Deep Audio Check must appear in Review Operation and runSettings.log, remain read-only when not tagging, and remain off by default so Artist In Album Tag is the only checkbox selected by default.

REQ-TRASH-002  The operating-system Trash/Recycle implementation remains the only corruption-removal primitive. Whole-show, qualifying music-directory, and individual-file removals must be applied only from a completed structured assessment; successful removals must be reflected in the carried group/ShowMetadata paths before downstream work resumes. Folder policy is evaluated before file policy from the same original snapshot. On native Windows the implementation must conservatively establish recyclability before calling IFileOperation: require a fixed local NTFS volume, a successful SHQueryRecycleBinW query, confirmed per-volume Recycle Bin enablement and capacity, and no applicable Explorer no-recycle policy. Disconnected/removable/network/non-NTFS volumes and unavailable or unconfirmable recycling settings must be retained and reported without a destructive call. The Shell must be requested to recycle only, with no automatic permanent-delete confirmation. This preflight cannot replace native Windows regression testing or eliminate external changes between preflight and execution.

REQ-SAFETY-001  Destructive mutation, repair, copy, cleanup, update-state persistence, and reversal code must catch the narrowest expected filesystem/domain exception classes practical at the operation boundary. An intentionally suppressed cleanup/recovery exception in these paths must be recorded through the low-noise suppressed-exception diagnostic logger. Unexpected programming exceptions must not be silently converted into destructive success. If an automatic rollback after a destructive mutation fails or cannot safely complete, the user-facing failure must state that rollback was incomplete and identify the current path or state of affected material where practical.

REQ-SAFETY-002  Each destructive safety rule changed during Builds 525-528 must have direct behavioral or fault-injection regression coverage. The minimum closure matrix includes FLAC stage/backup/install rollback, Copy Request deletion confinement, unverifiable-volume POSIX cleanup, reversal conflict/cross-filesystem rollback, inventory/Copy Request ownership locking, SHN target-appearance refusal, and atomic persistence failure that preserves prior settings/log bytes.

FFmpeg source availability policy: Native builds shall retrieve FFmpeg 9.0.2 only from official FFmpeg HTTPS release hosts. On transient network errors (including connection reset while streaming), try up to five bounded downloads with backoff and an official-hostname fallback. Download into a temporary file; enforce a strict 64 MiB transfer budget, verify the existing pinned SHA-256 before publishing to the cache, and remove incomplete transfers. Corrupt cached archives, checksum mismatches, certificate-verification failures, local filesystem errors, and permanent HTTP failures must remain fail-closed and must not be bypassed or replaced with unverified prebuilt binaries. Tests shall cover interrupted streams, retry exhaustion, alternate host, cache reuse and the security failure matrix.

The FFmpeg source compilation recipe shall work under strict Bash (set -Eeuo pipefail) on native macOS and Linux without expanding an empty or unset optional linker array. The additional --extra-ldexeflags=-static option shall be passed only for UCRT64 Windows builds. Regression coverage shall execute a fixture configure+make in a Unix environment and assert no Windows-only option leaks into its arguments. The Windows PE DLL-import allowlist remains a mandatory release gate.

FFmpeg redistribution: TLO native packages must not include binaries configured with --enable-nonfree or --enable-gpl. Audio-only builds are sourced from a SHA-256 pinned FFmpeg 9.0.2 upstream source archive. Source, LGPL terms, configure recipe and platform binary provenance must accompany all released native packages. Public release is blocked until native builds, codec regressions and legal compliance have been verified.

SHN to FLAC conversion SHALL request FFmpeg -xerror and -v error, reject nonzero results and diagnostic errors, independently decode the source SHN and candidate FLAC to canonical 32-bit PCM, and require equal PCM MD5 and decoded byte/sample counts. The converter SHALL NOT publish an unverified FLAC or permanently delete the SHN. Once the verified FLAC is published, attempt native Trash/Recycle Bin. If native Trash fails or leaves the source in place, move the SHN by same-volume rename into a recoverable .tlo-shn-originals directory beside the original, with a unique filename, exclude it from inventory traversal and log the full holding path. If neither operation can preserve the original in a recoverable location, roll back the newly generated FLAC while the SHN remains. The successful tag log SHALL record verified PCM MD5 and PCM byte count.

Recoverable XDG Trash when gio is absent. On Linux without gio, a private same-filesystem XDG Trash location stores recoverable originals with collision-safe metadata. Failures or unavailable Trash preserve originals; no hard-delete fallback is permitted.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: These detailed operational and release-safety requirements supplement the governing Sections 2, 7, 14, 17, and 20. They are normative wherever they use SHALL, MUST or equivalent language.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: The Windows FFmpeg binary bundled with TLO must run without a separately installed FFmpeg or MSYS2 runtime. The build must link MinGW runtime libraries statically where possible, inspect imported PE DLLs before staging, and reject any dependency outside an explicit Windows system DLL allowlist, including libwinpthread-1.dll. Run a clean Windows execution smoke test in GitHub Actions before releasing. Linux and macOS behavior remains unchanged.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: Repeated inventories of the same source path shall not fail when the same short-token log (including groupsN.log) is rewritten. Matching in-process logging handles shall be flushed and released before atomic replacement, and future entries appended without losing unrelated scopes. Transient Windows file-sharing failures may be retried briefly; permanent failures must be reported and the original log preserved.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: Release prerequisites: setuptools 84.2.1 (SHA-256 locked) replaces vulnerable 84.0.0. Windows, Linux, and macOS release artifacts must receive an actual passing malware scan, with hash-bound scan receipts. MacOS artifacts may be scanned in the Linux final packaging job when native ClamAV fails signature validation; no unsigned or unscanned ZIP may be released.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: When TLO_FFMPEG_SOURCE_ARCHIVE is set, the native FFmpeg source loader SHALL accept only a present regular archive named ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz whose SHA-256 equals the immutable upstream FFmpeg pin and whose size does not exceed the source limit. It SHALL reverify the source after copying into the native compilation cache, publish the cache atomically, and fail closed without making network requests if the provided artifact is missing, corrupt or oversized.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: When that environment variable is absent, the existing verified source cache and bounded upstream HTTPS retries MAY be used for local builds. All native compilers SHALL continue to compile from source; FFmpeg 9.0.2 LGPL-only codec configuration, scanned build outputs, Windows signing, and THIRD_PARTY/FFmpeg corresponding-source distribution SHALL remain mandatory.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: In the GitHub Actions Linux test job, TLO_FFMPEG_SOURCE_ARCHIVE SHALL remain populated for native compilation and verify the supplied source artifact without upstream fallback. Legacy network-retry tests SHALL clear the inherited variable only within their isolated test fixtures, exercise actual upstream HTTP error handling, and restore the environment after the test. Production FFmpeg source selection and integrity enforcement SHALL remain unchanged.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: The evergreen TLO-FAQ.txt SHALL remain version-neutral and SHALL not include release-by-release history.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: TLO Main and TLO Search SHALL create (if absent) and load a shared tlo-preferences.ini file in the resolved TLOHome directory before setting GUI control defaults. The file SHALL be a human-readable, editable INI document and SHALL ship as a template with the current default values. An existing file SHALL NOT be overwritten during startup, update, or installation.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: The [main] section SHALL cover all displayed option checkboxes, Dry Run, Performance Mode, Max Workers, corrupt-file and folder policy and threshold, Path(s) default, font family, default font size, heading font size and fixed font size. The [search] section SHALL control Deep, default query, font family and font sizes. [manual_updates] SHALL control Update Tags; [add_new_shows] SHALL control Check For Duplicates; [general] SHALL control shared Auto Update.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: Max Workers = 0 SHALL retain the performance-mode automatic worker ceiling. Font-size values of 0 SHALL retain existing platform/application defaults. With no --find and no nonempty search_query, startup SHALL use clipboard text by default unless clipboard_prefill=false was configured. Unavailable clipboard data shall not abort startup. Explicit command-line options SHALL override corresponding preferences on that launch; Search --find SHALL have priority over the configured default search query.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: Main and Search hamburger menus SHALL offer Edit Preferences. The editor SHALL expose “Save & Close” and “Cancel”. Save & Close SHALL validate syntax, type, range and relationships before atomic same-directory replacement; successful save closes the editor and advises that restart is needed. Invalid changes SHALL NOT replace the existing INI and SHALL leave the editor open. Cancel SHALL discard edits only after confirmation when text changed. Saving SHALL NEVER modify running application defaults, font settings, active GUI variables, current selections or in-progress operations. New INI values are loaded on next Main/Search launch.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: Shared Auto Update state SHALL be synchronized with the preference file when toggled through the running GUI. Existing defaults are retained when preferences are absent; the current persisted auto-update choice SHALL initialize a newly created preferences file. Missing or unavailable fonts SHALL fall back without preventing GUI startup.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: The distributed tlo-preferences.ini template SHALL describe accepted values, with concise explanatory comments. The performance_mode choices SHALL be gentle, balanced, fast and extreme; corrupt_files SHALL be keep or delete; corrupt_folders SHALL be never, all or threshold. Boolean keys, numeric bounds, font names and free-text/path fields SHALL also carry adjacent explanatory comments, without changing the default values.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: INI section names, keys, boolean words and enumerated choice values SHALL be case-insensitive. The font family SHALL match installed font names case-insensitively. Normalized enumerated values SHALL match the current GUI policy values. Older INI keys [main] search_path and [search] search_query or clipboard_prefill SHALL be silently ignored without affecting startup or producing validation errors.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: Before saving edited preferences, the system SHALL validate the complete INI, collecting syntax errors, duplicate/unknown sections and keys, invalid value types/ranges, enum choices, and conflicting dependent settings. Each error SHALL identify its line number where available, the section, the preference key and the allowable values or conflict. Any error SHALL block atomic replacement and preserve the previously saved file; the built-in editor SHALL display all diagnostics. A successful save SHALL continue to require restart.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: The preferences validator SHALL reject corrupt_files=keep when corrupt_folders is not never, because the GUI disables folder deletion under Keep and report. The error SHALL identify both keys and the conflicting values, and shall not replace the stored INI.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: The standard tlo-preferences.ini startup template SHALL follow the user-approved compact format: six concise introductory guidance lines and one shared boolean-alias note; sections [general], [main], [search], [manual_updates], [add_new_shows] in that order; and existing key names, ordering and defaults retained except adding [general] update_downloads = msi with the enumerated-value help comment. Earlier INIs without this setting default to msi. Individual true/false fields SHALL NOT repeat the accepted-value comment. Comments for enumerated pull-down choices, numeric limits, font families, paths and free-text fields SHALL remain adjacent to the affected setting. The distributed template and generated first-run defaults SHALL be byte-for-byte consistent, except when initializing the persisted Auto Update value to true.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: The compact template is a presentation change only. The INI grammar SHALL continue accepting case-insensitive sections, keys, boolean aliases, and choice values, while preserving the capitalization of paths and free-text queries. Full diagnostics, rejection of invalid files, atomic saves, restart notice, CLI override precedence, and preservation of existing user preferences SHALL remain unchanged.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: In non-compliant mode, a uniquely DB-matched artist found as an exact path component closer to the show folder SHALL take precedence over an incompatible two-character Artist DB name found in a more distant parent path component, when the nearer artist has at least four normalized letters. The rule SHALL not blacklist two-character artists: an actual short artist in a nearer directory or with no closer full-name match SHALL remain eligible. Distinct plausible full-name artist directories SHALL continue to raise an unresolved conflict. Compliant path-only behavior and audio-tag or explicit artist priority SHALL remain unchanged.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: The structured setlist metadata parser SHALL recognize the bounded header shapes Artist / City, Country / Date and Artist / City, Country / Unknown venue / Date (including punctuation and case variants). A missing-venue marker SHALL NOT become a venue from explicit metadata, venue-database hits, or inferred unlabeled venue lines. If the artist is uniquely DB-confirmed, this evidence SHALL resolve weaker path conflicts without changing the original source-precedence safeguards. The original Weather Report 1973-08-24 Chateauvallon, France example SHALL be included as a regression fixture. Its correct output SHALL leave the venue blank and shall not be reported as unidentified.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: The versioned BUILD_VERIFICATION report SHALL include an exact "Ruff lint:" field, and SHALL accurately state "lint not attested" when Ruff has not been run in the local environment. This field SHALL be present even when lint is unavailable locally. The report SHALL NOT claim a passing lint gate without execution. Mandatory hosted Ruff lint, native build, malware scan and signing gates remain unchanged. A regression test SHALL enforce this report schema prior to packaging.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: The released source bundle SHALL pass the mandatory Ruff F401 check for unused imports, including versioned regression tests. A module-level Path import SHALL NOT be shadowed by an unused local Path import in a test. Release evidence SHALL continue distinguishing local lint that was not executed from mandatory hosted verification, and SHALL NOT claim release attestation until all gates pass.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: Dated show roots whose direct audio subfolders are named one/two (and later consecutive number words) may be aggregated into a single non-compliant Full Inventory record only with shared parent setlist evidence, disjoint contiguous track numbering from 01 through N, and no unrelated subdirectories; audio tag artist differences must not decide grouping. Preserve the nested physical files; no flattening or destructive content merge occurs. Applies to Return to Forever 1976-03-07 Olympia Paris, France, where the one and two subfolders contain tracks 01-06 and 07-12. Compliant-mode grouping and existing collision protection are unchanged. Native build/signing gates remain mandatory.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: The dedicated GitHub FFmpeg source job SHALL try the checksum-keyed persistent Actions cache before making a network request; any cached archive SHALL be independently verified against the immutable FFmpeg 9.0.2 SHA-256 pin. On a cache-service outage, the job SHALL retain an ordinary verified-download fallback. A corrupt cached archive SHALL cause a fail-closed error rather than silently being trusted or replaced.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: If upstream source hosts are unreachable with transient network errors, TLO SHALL alternate between the official ffmpeg.org hostnames and the OmniOS FFmpeg source-archive mirror with bounded retries. Each candidate SHALL be verified against the same immutable source SHA-256 and size budget before publication. Permanent errors, TLS certification errors, altered archives, unsupported formats, and missing CI shared artifacts SHALL NOT be accepted. The native Windows/Linux/macOS jobs SHALL continue using only the common verified source artifact.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: For dated show folders assembled from separate recordings, the physical parent+child relationship SHALL determine grouping without audio-tag values. Complete-date same-name parts with (copyN), (altN), and related numbered or worded labels SHALL be recognized as one logical performance when at least two qualifying direct music-bearing children are present. Existing nested independent shows, collections, stand-alone Set 1/CD1 and Compliant-mode behavior retain their safety gates. The Return to Forever 1976-03-07 one/two layout and the manually consolidated Return to Forever ... / Return to Forever ... (copy1) and (... two) layout SHALL produce one show and one verified Copy/Delete transfer, retaining original part folders. For these groupings, tags remain metadata sources only after the folder group is selected.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: In non-compliant Full Inventory, the explicit fully dated parent and at least two same-show first-level named child branches SHALL determine aggregation even when a branch contains additional recognized CD1, Disc 1, Set 1, FLAC or other supplemental wrapper layers. Each descendant audio directory SHALL remain within one recognized child branch, and each additional intervening directory SHALL be a known wrapper rather than a new artist or dated show. All music-bearing branches of the same parent MUST qualify, the parent MUST NOT itself contain directly inventoried audio, and any independently named or dated music branch or symbolic-link traversal SHALL block this special promotion. The result SHALL be one logical record, one safely verified transfer and an unchanged source-part hierarchy. Audio tags SHALL NOT influence structural grouping; existing tag-based metadata precedence after grouping is preserved. A single suffix-bearing folder stays independent. Non-date sibling collections, same-base volume exceptions, existing sequential one/two rules, Compliant mode and collision protections SHALL remain unchanged.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: Release verification reports SHALL distinguish full hosted CI runs from separately executed headless GUI subsets, report pass/skip/fail counts accurately for each run, and state whether a display was available. Historical observations SHALL NOT be presented as new release attestation.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: In non-compliant Full Inventory, a fully dated performance parent containing at least two direct, audio-bearing child folders named CD1 final/CD2 final (and equivalent Disc, Disk, Set, Part or Tape numbered final labels) SHALL inventory as one logical show. This applies only when the numbered parts are unique and consecutive starting at 1 and every music-bearing descendant beneath the parent belongs to that same direct sibling set. CD1 final by itself, unmatched parts, unrelated artist or separately dated descendants, nested non-wrapper music branches, mixed direct-parent audio, and undated collection folders SHALL NOT trigger this special promotion. Grouping SHALL use the physical folder hierarchy and never audio tags. The shared parent SHALL retain its setlist, original part directories, all audio files, one inventory identity, and a single safely staged Copy/Delete transfer when selected. Compliant mode and existing CD/Disc/Set, copy/alt, sequential one/two, volume, collection and collision policies SHALL remain unchanged.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: In non-compliant Full Inventory, directly nested music-bearing sibling folders below the same fully dated show parent SHALL aggregate when their leading CD/Disc/Disk/Set/Part/Tape label identifies a complete unique sequence beginning at one. The sequence value MAY be written as a numeral (1, 2), a cardinal word (one, two), or an ordinal word (first, second), including mixed forms. The remaining descriptive suffix MAY differ between siblings (for example, CD1 fixed and CD two remastered), and SHALL NOT by itself cause separate shows or a destination (copy1). A single part, gaps, repeated sequence numbers, any extra music-bearing descendant, conflicting date-bearing child description, and undated parent SHALL prevent this narrow promotion. Existing Compliant mode behavior, original child directories, setlist selection, metadata precedence, tagging, Copy/Delete and source-edition safeguards are unchanged; audio tags SHALL NOT decide grouping.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: In non-compliant Full Inventory, when a selected setlist begins with a plausible artist heading and a nearby explicit “Recorded Live in City YYYY” statement, TLO SHALL extract the city and year. The artist SHALL be promoted only if uniquely resolved in the Artist DB or independently corroborated by an explicit artist attribution in the same setlist. An otherwise unresolved date SHALL become YYYY-xx-xx without inventing a month, day, venue, state or country. A complete or partially known date SHALL NOT be overwritten. Punctuation-only unmatched ARTIST or ALBUMARTIST tags (such as “-”) SHALL be treated as missing before artist precedence decisions. Compliant mode and folder grouping SHALL remain unchanged.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: In non-compliant Full Inventory, a complete performance date at the end of a folder MAY trigger an additional fallback when the preceding text has the form Artist at Place Date, Artist in Place Date, Artist Live at Place Date, or Artist Live in Place Date. TLO SHALL identify the artist from the longest complete, unique Artist DB match anchored at the beginning of the folder; a shorter match SHALL NOT override a longer matching artist. For state/country-anchored place text, existing venue, city, region, and country parsing SHALL be used. For a venue/city string without a state or country, TLO SHALL require an exact venue match from venues.sqlite or the legacy venues.txt before inferring the venue/city boundary; otherwise the artist and date MAY be preserved without inventing a venue or city. Live in City MAY identify a city without inferring a missing state. This fallback SHALL NOT run for ambiguous multiple dates or in Compliant mode; it SHALL NOT override stronger confirmed metadata, nor change existing Artist - Album or Artist - String2 Date behavior. The older Artist Venue City Date fallback SHALL yield to explicit at/in evidence when present.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: In non-compliant Full Inventory, when a unique Artist DB match anchors a name of the form Artist at Place Date, Artist in Place Date, Artist Live at Place Date, or Artist Live in Place Date, and one complete date terminates the name, TLO SHALL first offer enabled etreeDB, selected setlist metadata, and setlist.fm venue/location sources their existing opportunity. Only when no venue, city, region, country, or location has been determined SHALL a guarded last-resort inference consider the unqualified place string. That inference SHALL select the longest whole recognized city suffix from a conservative built-in city vocabulary or external TLOHome/TLO_DBs/cities.sqlite; the remaining left text, after trimming leading/trailing punctuation and whitespace, MAY become the venue. An at-form requires a nonempty venue; an in-form MAY be location-only. The city reference SHALL NOT supply an unmentioned region or country. Unknown, non-unique, or ambiguous suffixes SHALL NOT be split. The original place, inferred venue/city, medium confidence and inference source SHALL be recorded in observations. Confirmed online/setlist metadata SHALL NOT be overwritten or combined with an inferred place. Existing Artist - String2 Date, explicit state/country, compliant, grouping and multi-disc behavior SHALL remain unchanged.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: In non-compliant Full Inventory, a folder component whose leading 1–4-character all-lowercase or all-uppercase Artist DB term immediately precedes a complete YYYY-MM-DD date (such as who1974-05-18.sbd or who1997-07-23.flac16 Milwaukee, WI - Marcus Amphitheater) SHALL retain its complete date and SHALL NOT use post-date technical/source/venue/city/collector strings as competing artist evidence. A matching Artist DB term in the prefix MAY identify the performer, subject to the existing DB collision rule. A uniquely DB-backed ancestor artist directory (such as Who, The) SHALL remain eligible even if the compact prefix is absent as an alias. An incompatible real performer identified from the dated prefix or another substantive artist directory SHALL still create a conflict. Folders beginning with a numbered disc/set/part marker and a descriptive track/source/title tail (Disc1 - Soccer Rock; Disc2 - Love Rain O'er Me) SHALL be excluded from generic embedded Artist DB scans but SHALL retain their original names and physical grouping behavior. TLO SHALL not infer performer names from such title tails; selected setlist metadata and other established sources MAY still identify the performer. Media tokens immediately attached to a complete date via a dot or underscore (for example DATE.flac16) SHALL be removed from the leading String2 location-parsing text only when the original folder unambiguously contains that technical marker. Such tokens SHALL NOT be treated as cities or venues. Compliant mode, the global date parser, String1/String2 interpretation outside these conditions, and grouping and transfer safeguards SHALL remain unchanged.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: In non-compliant Full Inventory, a uniquely matched Artist DB name at the beginning of a folder, followed by a comma, one unambiguous city token (or recognized multiword city), and a single terminal numeric performance-date token SHALL be eligible for Artist, City Date parsing even when no venue is provided. For example, Jethro Tull, Derby 2007-02-04 SHALL identify artist Jethro Tull, date 2007-02-04, city Derby and no invented venue or state. A single-word unknown city SHALL require a plausible capitalized city token and reject common recording/album descriptors. Compliant behavior SHALL be unchanged.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: For ambiguous two-digit numeric dates such as 02-04-07, TLO SHALL preserve viable YY-MM-DD and MM-DD-YY interpretations, and in the guarded comma-delimited pattern SHALL also consider DD-MM-YY. The selected local setlist SHALL have the first opportunity to corroborate a single interpretation. If it cannot and etreeDB and/or setlist.fm lookup is enabled, TLO MAY probe no more than three complete candidate dates against the uniquely identified artist; the lookup SHALL require an exact matching artist and date, usable venue/city, and agreement with any independently identified city. All enabled sources and candidate dates SHALL be compared before selecting a unique corroborated date. Conflicting, incomplete, unavailable, or nonmatching responses SHALL preserve the unresolved date conflict; TLO SHALL NOT choose by numeric date order, locale guess or first hit. No venue/location from online data SHALL override established local metadata. Online lookup budgets and source priority SHALL remain enforced.

Section: Appendix K - Supplemental Current Operational Requirements
Requirement_Text: MSI install and update requirements: a per-user, Windows Installer-managed TLO installation owns its application files under LocalAppData/Programs/Traders Little Organizer, not TLOHome. First-run setup prompts for an existing writable TLOHome; subsequent launches reuse the configured location without affecting portable ZIP installations. By default every Windows update (including a portable ZIP installation) must select only the published Windows_x64 MSI; an explicit [general] update_downloads = zip selects the exact matching downloadable ZIP instead. An MSI update shall validate the independently signed release metadata, the MSI hash and Authenticode signature, and invoke an external worker for MSI-owned installations after all MSI-owned TLO processes exit. For a portable Windows installation the authenticated MSI may be launched interactively and the old TLOHome/apps folder left for manual cleanup. Linux/macOS ZIP download behavior is retained. All inventories, setlists, databases and preferences in TLOHome must survive MSI upgrade, repair and uninstall.

Requirement_Text: data integrity: Child-path re-inventory SHALL archive only reversible operation lines actually removed from that child scope, deduplicate archived history and preserve operations from other roots for Reverse. Duplicate identical records SHALL NOT create false Reverse ambiguity.

Rename Compliantly: A proposed rename SHALL NOT change a fully known ISO performance date or omit a numeric source identifier such as etree shnid 101589 or a resolution qualifier such as 24-96. Uncertain identification SHALL keep the original folder name.
inventory preflight: If an existing bootlist.csv is not valid UTF-8, inventory SHALL abort before renaming, tagging, or copying and identify bootlist.csv and the CSV UTF-8 remedy.

bootlist: All writers SHALL apply reversible spreadsheet-formula escaping and atomically replace the master CSV after flushing; Search SHALL unescape data before matching setlist-index.json identities.

Build 686 Windows MSI: The Start Menu group SHALL offer an additional shortcut named TLO Artist Database Search targeting search-artist-db.exe. Multi-path existing-inventory dialogs SHALL default to Skip.

Show/Album stability: When Rename Compliantly refuses a punctuation-only reduction, and the proposed Show differs from the existing folder name only by venue punctuation, use the unchanged folder spelling as the Show and Album identity during tagging and bootlist output. Other unsafe renames remain skipped.

Multilingual rename safety: Source and proposed names shall be compared after equivalent accent folding, while preserving every non-Latin identifying word. International month names may be omitted from normalized dates only when recognized as part of an explicit date; words in artist and city names, including May and New, shall not be removed.

Search: Ordinary text and explicit Boolean expressions shall support apostrophes, curly apostrophes, nested literal qualifiers inside grouped expressions, and repeated whitespace; expression complexity limits remain enforced. Ambiguous View shall provide a clear re-inventory remedy without exposing internal placeholder filenames.

parallel failure feedback: If a potentially mutating worker fails, do not claim that bootlist or setlist outputs were finalized. In-memory completed results do not imply committed output; do not replay unfinished mutating work automatically.
Rename Compliantly reporting: Report per-search-path actual renames and skipped renames on the console, in the tagging log, and in summary.log, with reasons retained in the tag error log.

City-catalog last-resort inference SHALL use only the raw span of a date already independently parsed and selected by the inventory parser. For dotted, dashed, numeric and textual date spellings, match that exact source span when looking for a trailing whole-city name; refuse contradictory, ambiguous or multiple date spans. Never invent a date or override established location or venue metadata.

Foreign-month date parsing SHALL avoid interpreting Mars and Juli as month-year dates when no day is available. A month-first Mars/Juli date following an artist prefix is ambiguous and SHALL not be inferred from the folder alone; day-first or year-first complete dates may still be used. Two adjacent complete dates separated by a spaced dash SHALL not generate a hybrid date crossing their boundary.

Source_Locator: Build 691 Add Shows verified transfer addendum
Requirement_Text: Add Shows accepted-show staging, duplicate holding, and rollback moves SHALL preserve all files and subdirectories across different filesystems. A cross-filesystem move must first copy into an exclusively owned, hidden directory on the destination filesystem; check the complete directory structure, file sizes and SHA-256 content identity; and atomically publish without overwriting any destination. It SHALL NOT delete the source until publication of a fully verified tree succeeds. On copy/verification failure, the source shall remain intact and no visible destination shall appear. On deletion failure after publication, retain the verified destination and report both locations and the need for manual reconciliation. On the same filesystem, retain an atomic non-overwriting directory rename. Do not follow symlinks for cross-filesystem transfers.

Same-filesystem Tag Copy/Delete Original SHALL write and synchronize a restricted recovery journal containing the original source path, hidden stage path, intended destination and worker identity before moving the source to an excluded stage. Successful publication and successful rollback shall remove the journal. An abruptly terminated worker may leave a complete show inside a hidden .tlo-partial-* stage. TLO Reverse SHALL offer an explicit --recover-staging mode for an existing destination directory, with --dry-run preview, to restore only a valid journaled staged move when its recorded worker is no longer active and both the original source and published destination paths are absent. Restoration uses an atomic no-replace rename. Invalid or ambiguous journals, occupied original paths, possible active workers, remote hosts, and unjournaled partial folders SHALL NOT be moved automatically; report a recovery conflict and preserve data for manual review. Incomplete cross-volume copy stages SHALL never be treated as completed same-volume moves.

Search SHALL distinguish malformed expressions, invalid UTF-8 bootlist input, structurally invalid CSV and filesystem access errors. A UTF-8 decode error SHALL identify bootlist.csv and the CSV UTF-8 remedy without modifying input. Formula-escaped CSV Show values SHALL display without their storage apostrophes. City source is the external cities.sqlite catalog, not an embedded Python catalog.

If any day is future, the entire range SHALL remain unresolved, and no first-day canonical date shall be emitted. Historical and partial dates retain existing precedence.
